Cashman told reporters on Tuesday that he was "surprised" by Posada's comments and spoke to him after they surfaced. He added that Posada and the rest of the team's legends have an open line of communication with the organization. During an appearance on The Show podcast (h/t Matt Ehalt of the New Yor
item.content:encoded:
New York Yankees legend Jorge Posada raised some eyebrows when he declared that he doesn't "feel welcome" around the franchise, but general manager Brian Cashman is hoping to rectify the situation.
Cashman told reporters on Tuesday that he was "surprised" by Posada's comments and spoke to him after they surfaced. He added that Posada and the rest of the team's legends have an open line of communication with the organization.
During an appearance on The Show podcast (h/t Matt Ehalt of the New York Post), Posada explained that he hasn't felt the love from the Yankees in recent years.
"I don't feel welcome when I go there, you know? Even in spring training, I don't feel like — I'm just like, I don't know, like, I don't feel welcome," he said. "I don't feel like they want me there, so I don't go. ... I don't know what happened. I'd rather just move forward. My last season of my career was a really tough one when it comes to handling everything in my part and also the Yankees toward Jorge Posada. So, it's tough to go back and feel that again."
Posada was one of the many Yankees legends in attendance for Old Timers' Day in August. New York went 93-68 this season before losing in the ALDS for the second consecutive season, continuing its World Series title drought dating back to 2009.
Cashman and manager Aaron Boone aren't going anywhere despite the ongoing lack of success, but any further missteps could run the risk of alienating some of the Yankees' most beloved players like Posada.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] 4 Potential Landing Spots for Paul Blackburn if Yankees Let Him Walk in Free Agency
item.dc:creator: Jonna Perlinger; Unknown
item.description: The New York Yankees have several difficult decisions ahead following their disappointing elimination by the Tampa Bay Rays in the American League Division Series, but few are generating as much debate as the future of free-agent reliever Paul Blackburn. Yankees fans have made a compelling case for bringing Blackburn back, and it's difficult to blame them. The 32-year-old right-hander has experienced quite the career resurgence since arriving in the Bronx. Blackburn earned his first All-Star sel
item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees have several difficult decisions ahead following their disappointing elimination by the Tampa Bay Rays in the American League Division Series, but few are generating as much debate as the future of free-agent reliever Paul Blackburn.
Yankees fans have made a compelling case for bringing Blackburn back, and it's difficult to blame them.
The 32-year-old right-hander has experienced quite the career resurgence since arriving in the Bronx.
Blackburn earned his first All-Star selection with the Oakland Athletics in 2022, but his career subsequently took a downturn. An unsuccessful stint with the New York Mets left his future uncertain before the Yankees acquired him in 2025.
What followed was another successful Yankees pitching lab experiment.
New York took a chance on Blackburn, effectively making him its latest pitching staff "group project," and the results exceeded expectations.
After struggling during his initial stint in pinstripes, Blackburn reinvented himself as a dependable bullpen weapon in 2026, finishing 7-3 with a 1.69 ERA across 62 appearances and 85 innings.
His transformation has made a potential departure particularly difficult to justify, although not everyone agrees that retaining him should be a priority.
According to Gary Phillips of the New York Daily News, the Yankees have expressed strong interest in re-signing Blackburn.
However, analyst Stephen Parello of FanSided has argued that New York would be better served allowing him to leave rather than committing significant money to a reliever without an established track record as a back-end reliever.
With Jim Bowden of The Athletic projecting a two-year, $22 million contract, the concern isn't necessarily Blackburn's ability, but whether the Yankees should make that investment while also prioritizing the return of closer David Bednar.
Should general manager Brian Cashman decide to allocate those resources elsewhere, these four teams could make compelling landing spots.
1. Philadelphia Phillies
The Phillies have an established closer in Jhoan Duran, but their bullpen remains a concern heading into 2027.
With José Alvarado and Brooks Raley entering free agency, Philadelphia has decisions to make about its late-inning depth.
Blackburn wouldn't necessarily address the Phillies' need for another left-handed reliever, but his ability to work multiple innings and navigate high-pressure situations would offer manager Don Mattingly additional flexibility.
For a team with championship aspirations, adding a veteran who can bridge the gap between its starters and Duran could prove valuable.
2. Kansas City Royals
Few teams have a more pressing need for bullpen reinforcements than the Kansas City Royals.
Kansas City's relievers finished 2026 with a 5.07 ERA, ranking 29th in Major League Baseball, and the organization has already begun making changes.
The Royals declined closer Carlos Estévez's $13 million club option following a season derailed by injuries, creating another vacancy in an already struggling relief corps.
Blackburn wouldn't necessarily solve their ninth-inning problem, but his versatility and ability to generate weak contact could provide much-needed stability.
For a pitching staff desperate for dependable innings, Blackburn represents an intriguing opportunity to acquire an established veteran coming off a career year.
3. Washington Nationals
The Nationals desperately need bullpen help, and Blackburn could provide the veteran presence their young pitching staff has been missing.
Washington's bullpen endured a disastrous 2026 campaign, recording an MLB-record 42 blown saves and finishing with a National League-worst 4.99 ERA.
Despite having an intriguing young offensive core featuring James Wood, Dylan Crews, and CJ Abrams, Washington has struggled to consistently protect leads.
Blackburn wouldn't single-handedly transform the Nationals' bullpen, but his experience, ability to handle multiple innings, and recent success in high-leverage situations could make him an attractive addition.
At 32, Blackburn could also provide valuable mentorship while helping Washington establish greater stability in the later innings.
4. Texas Rangers
The Rangers represent another logical destination, particularly with their front office preparing for another bullpen overhaul.
General manager Chris Young has acknowledged that Texas intends to be active in rebuilding its relief corps, with several pitchers entering free agency.
The Rangers have found success identifying overlooked veteran arms in recent years, making Blackburn's career resurgence in New York particularly intriguing.
His ability to pitch multiple innings, generate ground balls, and adapt to different situations could make him a valuable addition alongside returning relievers Jacob Latz and Robert Garcia.
For an organization looking to strengthen its pitching staff without committing to another expensive closer, Blackburn could offer a practical solution.
Ultimately, the Yankees know better than anyone what Blackburn can provide when utilized effectively. Whether that familiarity is enough to justify his projected asking price remains to be seen.
But if New York lets another successful pitching project walk, there should be no shortage of teams interested in seeing whether Blackburn's resurgence can continue elsewhere.
Jonna Perlinger's love for baseball began long before Yankees manager Buck Showalter handed her a broken bat at six years old, but that moment helped shape a lifelong passion for the game and the Bronx Bombers. She serves as Baseball Content Lead, Lead Yankees Writer, and Director of Social Media for On New Jersey Sports (ONNJ), and is the founder of Babe's Babes Media, an independent, women-led baseball platform established in 2023. Her reporting has taken her to some of baseball's biggest stages, including the World Baseball Classic, MLB All-Star Week, Winter Meetings, and Men's College World Series. Jonna has a deep appreciation for baseball's history and traditions, and a passion for telling the stories of the people who make the game special, both on and off the field.

item.content:encoded:
LAS VEGAS — New York Yankees general manager Brian Cashman didn't try to hide his cards about his team's biggest offseason need on Tuesday in Las Vegas.
Speaking to the media during Major League Baseball's general manager meetings, Cashman said his team's bullpen would be a focal point this offseason.
Of course, it already has been in some ways with the $23.15 million qualifying offer extended to Yankees closer David Bednar. However, that was just the first piece of an elaborate puzzle Cashman has to put together in the back end this offseason.
"I don't want to say if there have been conversations going or not going," Cashman said of any potential long-term contract talks with Bednar if he chooses to turn down the qualifying offer. "Obviously, we made the qualifying offer. He has until November 17 to make the decision on his end, and bullpen is an area of need for us."
Cashman said that the bullpen situation is fluid because of a number of potential losses this offseason among the group. Five of the seven Yankees who recorded a save last season are free agents this offseason, including Bednar, Ryan Yarbrough, Paul Blackburn, Tim Hill and John Schreiber.
"That's probably our biggest need because we have so many vacancies of certainly important people that did a great job for us," Cashman said. "(Brent) Headrick is still here, obviously, but with Timmy Hill and Bednar and Blackburn, all free agents, those guys were a really nice bridge for us late in the game and they were consistent throughout the whole year. We have to rebuild that."
Cashman said there are a multitude of ways the Yankees could rebuild the bullpen.
"That doesn't mean that we don't have answers from within that can handle it somehow some way," Cashman said. "If I can pull down a trade or through free agency some individuals that make you sleep better at night, even though bullpens are volatile regardless, that would be a priority for me."
The key to the entire bullpen this offseason, however, seems to be Bednar and what it will take to bring him back to the Bronx.
"Listen, we dropped a big qualifying number on him. That factored a lot," Cashman said of Bednar's ability to pitch under pressure in New York. "He's a cool customer. He provided, from what I understand, even though I'm not in the bullpen, obviously, but from what I hear from everybody involved, we've been very lucky over the course of time, for the most part, to have somebody with a strong presence and great leadership to lead out there. He checked all those boxes along with the performance.
"I've had some good additions. I've had some not so good additions. He's been a good addition so far, and hopefully we find a way to keep him so I can worry about surrounding him with more quality individuals that our manager can turn to late in the game to try to close things out."

item.dc:creator: Alexander Wilson
item.description: Anthony Volpe belongs in the Yankees' second-base competition. I wouldn't give him the job in November just because he is already on the roster. Jon Heyman of the New York Post reported that the Yankees see Volpe and possibly Luis Garcia Jr. as options at second, while prioritizing third base and the bullpen. MLB.com's GM meetings roundup carried the report Monday. No starter has been announced. What the Yankees should ask of Volpe at second New York started Volpe at second when it recalled him
item.content:encoded:
Anthony Volpe belongs in the Yankees' second-base competition. I wouldn't give him the job in November just because he is already on the roster.
Jon Heyman of the New York Post reported that the Yankees see Volpe and possibly Luis Garcia Jr. as options at second, while prioritizing third base and the bullpen. MLB.com's GM meetings roundup carried the report Monday. No starter has been announced.
What the Yankees should ask of Volpe at second
New York started Volpe at second when it recalled him in September. He appeared in 12 games there in 2026. The position isn't new to him, but it gives the Yankees limited major-league evidence on turning double plays or handling the position every day.
Statcast's batting line shows the other half of the decision: a .321 on-base percentage and a .336 slugging percentage over 246 plate appearances. I can live with modest power if the on-base gains hold and the defense translates. I'm not treating either as settled.
Garcia gives them a left-handed bat to evaluate, though the current depth chart lists him at first base. If neither makes the case at second, look outside the organization. The Yankees can put third base first on the winter shopping list without promising Volpe everyday at-bats.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] The 2013 Aaron Judge Card That Sold for $324,000 in 2022 Just Sold for $5.2 Million
item.dc:creator: Miracle Dimwesh
item.description: The market for elite baseball memorabilia has found a new standard in a card tied to the New York Yankees' biggest star. The one-of-one 2013 Bowman Chrome Draft Superfractor Autograph card featuring Aaron Judge sold privately through Fanatics Collect for $5.2 million in March. The deal established a new high for a modern-era baseball card, as ABC7 New York reported. The card's journey makes the sale even more striking. A collector paid $324,000 for the same item through PWCC Marketplace in 2022.
item.content:encoded:
The market for elite baseball memorabilia has found a new standard in a card tied to the New York Yankees' biggest star.
The one-of-one 2013 Bowman Chrome Draft Superfractor Autograph card featuring Aaron Judge sold privately through Fanatics Collect for $5.2 million in March. The deal established a new high for a modern-era baseball card, as ABC7 New York reported.
The card's journey makes the sale even more striking. A collector paid $324,000 for the same item through PWCC Marketplace in 2022. Its latest price is more than 16 times that amount, showing how dramatically demand for elite Judge memorabilia has grown.
Sports Illustrated detailed the record-setting transaction, which was brokered by Fanatics Collect. The identities of the buyer and seller were not disclosed.
The card's rarity is central to its appeal. It is the only copy of its kind, carries Judge's autograph and dates to 2013, before he made his major league debut. That combination places it among the most coveted pieces tied to the Yankees captain.
Judge's career has helped drive that interest. He homered in his first major league at-bat in 2016, then hit 52 home runs in his 2017 rookie season. His 62 homers in 2022 broke Roger Maris' American League single-season record.
The new mark also moves Judge ahead of the previous modern baseball card record. A one-of-one signed 2009 Mike Trout Superfractor sold for $3.936 million in 2020. Shohei Ohtani's modern cards have also reached multimillion-dollar territory, but Judge now sits above them.
The sale illustrates how a player's achievements, scarcity and collector demand can combine to create extraordinary prices. For the memorabilia market, Judge's card is now a benchmark that future high-end baseball releases will be measured against.
This story was originally published by Athlon on Nov 10, 2026, where it first appeared in the MLB section. Add Athlon as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

item.title: [Pinstripes Nation] Los Problemas De Los Yankees En Los Playoffs Dan Pie A Una Afirmación Explosiva Sobre La Cultura Condenatoria Del «75 %» De Aaron Boone
item.dc:creator: Esteban Quiñones

item.content:encoded:
NUEVA YORK — Se acaba la entrada. Se han hecho tres outs. Lo que pase en los próximos 30 segundos, según un ojeador veterano, dice más de los Yankees que cualquier marcador.
Le pidió a un periodista que prestara atención a eso durante la Serie Mundial. ¿Qué jugadores vuelven trotando a sus posiciones? ¿Y cuáles van andando?
Parece una tontería. Pero para un equipo que lleva 17 temporadas sin ganar un campeonato, se ha convertido en algo mucho más importante.
The Yankees won 93 games in 2026, then scored five runs in three games as Tampa Bay swept them out of the American League Division Series. In Game 1, Rays starter Drew Rasmussen held New York to one hit, a first in franchise postseason history.
Ahora, Bob Klapisch, un veterano columnista de béisbol de Nueva York, ha achacado esa tendencia al entrenador Aaron Boone. En una mesa redonda fuera de temporada con Randy Miller, el periodista que cubre a los Yankees, Klapisch describió a un equipo cuyo nivel de esfuerzo se ha quedado muy por debajo del máximo y a un entrenador que deja que eso pase.
Los entrenamientos de primavera marcan la pauta de un rendimiento al 75 %
Klapisch dijo que el problema no empieza en octubre. Lo remonta a febrero, cuando cree que la actitud relajada del equipo se afianza con el visto bueno del entrenador.
«La actitud de los Yankees se nota incluso durante los entrenamientos de primavera. Son muy relajados, y Aaron Boone les da mucha libertad. Esa permisividad se refleja en cómo juegan cada noche, cada semana, cada mes. Su motor funciona al 75 % más o menos», dijo Klapisch.
También cuestionó la idea de considerar los 162 partidos como un único y largo proyecto. En su opinión, esa mentalidad da lugar a buenas temporadas regulares, pero no te da la ventaja necesaria para ganar el campeonato.
Miller se refirió a unos ejercicios que, según él, los Yankees han descuidado. Quiere que se haga entrenamiento en el campo interior antes de cada partido y que se practiquen los toques de verdad, no solo dos toques simbólicos contra lanzamientos suaves de entrenamiento de bateo.
Dos ojeadores, dos señales de alarma
Klapisch respaldó su argumento con lo que escuchó de los ojeadores tras la temporada. Uno de ellos planteó el tema como una cuestión de intensidad.
«¿Cuándo fue la última vez que viste a los Yankees jugar como si les fuera la vida en ello?», preguntó el ojeador, según Klapisch.
Otro ojeador le dijo que se fijara en los momentos de transición entre entradas, cuando no se lanza ninguna bola y no se registra ninguna estadística.
«Fíjate entre entradas y mira cuántos Yankees corren hacia su posición y cuántos van andando», le dijo el ojeador a Klapisch.
Klapisch dijo que el ojeador se quedó alucinado con lo que vio. Relacionó ese hábito directamente con el primer escalón del banquillo.
Se cuidó mucho de no menospreciar a Boone. Dijo que el entrenador es inteligente y que los críticos de las redes sociales lo subestiman, pero señaló que Boone evita exigir demasiado a los jugadores o hacer que se sientan incómodos. Añadió que Boone se adapta a sus estrellas y no le da importancia a los pequeños detalles.
«El carácter, la actitud y la intensidad importan tanto como cualquier conjunto de cifras, si no más. Si quieres enderezar a los Yankees, tienes que empezar por lo que hay en el corazón de un jugador y no por lo que aparece en una hoja de cálculo», dijo Klapisch.
El historial de Boone en octubre cuenta la misma historia
Las cifras que respaldan las críticas muestran a un entrenador que gana con regularidad de abril a septiembre, pero que se estanca en cuanto empieza la postemporada.
Boone tiene un balance de 790-565 en nueve temporadas regulares, lo que supone un porcentaje de victorias del 0,583, solo superado por los Dodgers de Los Ángeles de Dave Roberts desde 2018, según CBS Sports. Los Yankees llegaron a la postemporada ocho veces en ese periodo.
Octubre ha sido otra historia. Boone tiene un balance de 27-30 en partidos de postemporada, lo que le convierte en el único entrenador en la historia de los Yankees con un balance negativo en los playoffs. Ha dirigido 57 partidos de postemporada sin ganar una Serie Mundial, superando los 52 de Mike Hargrove con Cleveland como el entrenador con más partidos sin título con un mismo equipo, según el recuento de Sports Illustrated.
Cada una de esas ocho participaciones en la postemporada terminó en eliminación. Los Yankees cayeron cuatro veces en la Serie Divisional, dos veces en la Serie de Campeonato de la Liga Americana, una vez en la ronda de comodines y una vez en la Serie Mundial de 2024.
Miller relacionó esta tendencia con la plantilla. Los Yankees solo hicieron 10 toques de sacrificio en 2026, lo que les situó en el segundo puesto por el menor número de las Grandes Ligas, mientras que los Rays lideraron la clasificación en este aspecto. Nueva York quedó segunda en jonrones y sexta en strikeouts.
Klapisch dijo que los Yankees se centran en los ángulos de lanzamiento a costa de los roletazos y los golpes al campo contrario, hábitos a los que él atribuyó el éxito en Milwaukee y Tampa Bay. Los Brewers vencieron a los Rays en la Serie Mundial.
Aumenta la presión con el regreso de Boone para 2027
The criticism adds to a difficult Yankees offseason. Former club icons CC Sabathia, Derek Jeter, Alex Rodriguez, Paul O’Neill, Joe Girardi and Jorge Posada have questioned the club’s culture and fundamentals. Brewers manager Pat Murphy was caught on camera after the World Series saying the 2023 Yankees played for themselves.
Klapisch argumentó que la solución requiere algo más que una nueva voz. Quiere jugadores versátiles y que se lancen al contacto, dispuestos a aceptar papeles secundarios, y puso como ejemplo a Max Schuemann, que pasó parte de la temporada con los Yankees tras ser llamado desde la Triple A.
Se espera que Boone vuelva para su décima temporada en 2027, el último año de su contrato, según informó en octubre el periódico «The Record» del condado de Bergen. Los Yankees no han despedido a ningún entrenador que tuviera contrato desde Stump Merrill, tras la temporada de 1991.
Dado que el convenio colectivo vence el 1 de diciembre y existe la posibilidad de un cierre patronal, puede que Boone no tenga mucho tiempo para estar con sus jugadores antes de que empiecen los entrenamientos de primavera. Ahí es donde, según sus críticos, tiene que empezar el cambio.
¿Qué opinas? Deja tu comentario más abajo.

item.title: [si.com] Kevin McGonigle’s Historic Rookie Season Is Just the Beginning
item.dc:creator: Ryan Phillips
item.description: The Tigers traded their franchise cornerstone in 2026. Luckily, the team didn’t have to look far to find the next one. item.content:encoded:
The Tigers traded their franchise cornerstone in 2026. Luckily, the team didn’t have to look far to find the next one.
Kevin McGonigle was named American League Rookie of the Year on Monday after an incredible debut season that put him in the company of several all-time greats. The 22-year-old made Detroit’s Opening Day roster at 21 and quickly established himself as one of baseball’s most promising young stars.
In 156 games, McGonigle slashed .278/.376/.430 with 18 home runs and 72 RBIs. He led all rookies in runs (97) and finished with an excellent 129 wRC+. His strikeout rate (14.1%) was best among all qualified AL rookies, while his walk rate (13.4%) was second behind Munetaka Murakami (16.6%). Those are good numbers even on the surface, but when put in historical context, they are even more remarkable.
Ted Williams (1939) was the last rookie to equal McGonigle’s totals in home runs (18), doubles (28), RBIs (72), walks (95) and runs scored (97). Cherrypicking stats? Sure. But that combination does speak to McGonigle’s nearly unmatched all-around game as a rookie.
Perhaps even more impressive, he became only the fourth rookie since 1990 to reach base 266 times. The others? Albert Pujols and Ichiro Suzuki in 2001, and Aaron Judge in 2017. McGonigle didn’t just put up impressive numbers for a rookie, he announced himself as an emerging superstar.
McGonigle’s ability to make contact is excellent, but it’s not even his best trait. He simply doesn’t swing at bad pitches. His chase rate (19.6%) ranked in the 98th percentile league-wide, while his walk rate is in the 94th. Here’s where I remind you he played most of the season as a 21-year-old. His combination of plate discipline and contact rates evokes Juan Soto, who displayed a similarly advanced approach at an even younger age.
Soto had more power as a rookie than McGonigle and walked more. He slugged .548 and hit 34 home runs, while posting a walk rate of 16.4%. But his strikeout rate (20.0%) was considerably higher than the Tigers’ star. The rookie’s ability to command the zone and avoid strikeouts is extraordinary for his age, even when compared to Soto, a future Hall of Famer. McGonigle’s 95 walks were the most by a rookie since Aaron Judge in 2017, and the Yankees star was four years older.
McGonigle finished atop the AL leaderboard in bWAR (7.1) as a rookie, topping MVP favorite Yordan Álvarez (6.8). The last rookie to lead his league in bWAR was Mike Trout in 2012 when he reached 10.2 and finished second in MVP voting. McGonigle didn’t have the best offensive season in the American League, but his defensive value while splitting time at third base and shortstop vaulted him over his competition. He finished with 10 defensive runs saved, which ranked 14th among all big league infielders. It is exceedingly rare for a player to arrive in the majors with McGonigle’s offensive maturity and defensive ability.
The Tigers selected McGonigle with the 37th pick in the 2023 MLB draft as a 5'9" prep middle infielder from just outside Philadelphia. A sweet lefty swing and excellent plate discipline made him one of the most advanced hitters in his draft class, but there were questions about his future defensive position and offensive upside.
He quickly put those doubts to rest.
After just one full professional season, he had established himself as one of the best hitters in the minors. By the end of the 2025 campaign, he was widely considered the best. We ranked him as baseball’s No. 2 prospect entering this year and it appears we were one spot off. He was the sport’s best rookie this year.
Despite his incredible traits, McGonigle still has room to grow offensively. His average exit velocity (87.8 mph), hard-hit rate (37.6%) and bat speed (71.2 mph) are all below average, and his isolated power (.152) ranked 20th among qualified rookies this year. But the fact that he was an offensive force in 2026 despite those numbers is what makes his future so bright. Power isn’t his defining trait, and that’s an aspect of his game that could come as he continues to develop. McGonigle’s overall profile means he doesn’t need to hit 35 home runs to remain a star.
The Tigers traded ace Tarik Skubal to the Dodgers at the deadline, sending their two-time Cy Young winner to Los Angeles in exchange for a three-prospect package. Skubal’s departure marked the end of an era in Detroit. He had been the face of the franchise and the centerpiece of the team’s rotation. Skubal’s production on the mound will be nearly impossible to replace, but replacing him as the face of the franchise has already happened.
Two weeks after his debut, Detroit signed McGonigle to an eight-year, $150 million contract extension. After one season, it is already clear he’ll be leading the franchise’s next era. His historic rookie campaign was just the beginning.
Ryan Phillips is a senior writer on the Breaking and Trending News team at Sports Illustrated. He has worked in digital media since 2009, spending eight years at The Big Lead before joining SI in 2024. Phillips also co-hosts The Assembly Call Podcast about Indiana Hoosiers basketball and previously worked at Bleacher Report. He is a proud San Diego native and a graduate of Indiana University’s journalism program.

item.content:encoded:
Los Philadelphia Phillies podrían dar de qué hablar esta temporada baja.
Philadelphia sufrió otra decepcionante eliminación en los playoffs al caer ante los Atlanta Braves en la ronda de comodines. Tras esa salida prematura, los Phillies podrían ser protagonistas en la agencia libre.
Philadelphia no gana la Serie Mundial desde 2008.
Pronostican que los Philadelphia Phillies ficharán a Jazz Chisholm Jr.
Los Phillies podrían tener una vacante en la segunda base, ya que Luis Arraez está por convertirse en agente libre.
Philadelphia podría recurrir al mercado de cambios o a la agencia libre para reemplazar a Arraez. Ryan Finkelstein, analista de MLB en JustBaseball, pronostica que ficharán al exsegunda base de los New York Yankees Jazz Chisholm Jr. por dos años y 40 millones de dólares.
“Si solo miráramos las estadísticas de su tarjeta de béisbol, Jazz Chisholm Jr. estaría en posición de firmar un contrato a largo plazo este invierno”, escribió Finkelstein. “Incluso en una temporada floja, Jazz conectó 19 jonrones y robó 41 bases. Hace apenas un año tuvo una temporada de 30 jonrones y 30 bases robadas y todavía le quedan muchos años en plenitud. El problema es que ha sido irregular de forma constante y su personalidad excéntrica puede causarles dolores de cabeza a los equipos”.
“Lo más conveniente para Jazz probablemente sea un contrato de un año con opción para el segundo: así tendría la oportunidad de elevar su valor en el mercado y la seguridad de una opción a su favor. Los Phillies han asumido compromisos a largo plazo con demasiada frecuencia, pero en este caso podrían apostar por un contrato más corto para incorporar a un jugador talentoso aunque poco confiable. No hay duda de que Jazz puede darle más poder a la parte media de la alineación de los Phillies. Y sería un gran escenario para su segundo intento de revalorizarse de cara a la agencia libre”.
Chisholm sería una incorporación interesante para los Phillies, aunque genera opiniones divididas. Llegó a jugar una entrada con una paleta en la boca, algo que no le gustó a Aaron Boone.
Chisholm viene de una temporada floja y apunta a recuperarse. Bateó para .231 con 19 jonrones y 55 carreras impulsadas. Sus marcas personales son 31 jonrones y 80 carreras impulsadas.
Philadelphia busca reforzarse con decisión
Los Phillies vienen de otra eliminación temprana en los playoffs y buscan ser más agresivos.
Dave Dombrowski, presidente de operaciones de béisbol del equipo, dijo que intentan armar un plantel capaz de ganar la Serie Mundial.
“Esperamos ganar una Serie Mundial y queremos hacerlo”, dijo Dombrowski. “… Nuestros propietarios han estado tan dispuestos como cualquiera a tomar las medidas necesarias. Todavía no nos hemos sentado a definir el presupuesto salarial definitivo para el próximo año”.
“[El socio gerente y director ejecutivo de los Phillies] John [Middleton] y el grupo siempre han mostrado mucha disposición, pero ahora tenemos a muchos jugadores con salarios altos, así que creo que hay que decidir qué camino tomar. No creo que eso signifique necesariamente fichar solo a jugadores con salarios altos, pero sí creo que tenemos margen [para incorporar jugadores]”.
Los Phillies todavía no han hecho movimientos en esta temporada baja.

item.title: [Heavy.com] Philadelphia Phillies Predicted to Sign Polarizing Slugger to $40M Deal
item.dc:creator: Cole Shelton
item.description: The Philadelphia Phillies could be a team to watch this offseason. Philadelphia has another disappointing playoff exit, losing in the Wild Card round to the Atlanta Braves. After an early playoff exit, the Phillies could be a team to watch in free agency. Philadelphia hasn’t won the World Series since 2008. item.content:encoded:
The Philadelphia Phillies could be a team to watch this offseason.
Philadelphia has another disappointing playoff exit, losing in the Wild Card round to the Atlanta Braves. After an early playoff exit, the Phillies could be a team to watch in free agency.
Philadelphia hasn’t won the World Series since 2008.
Philadelphia Phillies Predicted to Sign Jazz Chisholm Jr.
The Phillies could have an opening at second base with Luis Arraez being a pending free agent.
Philadelphia could look to the trade market or free agency to replace Arraez. MLB analyst Ryan Finkelstein of JustBaseball predicts they will sign former New York Yankees second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. to a two-year, $40 million deal.
“If you solely looked at the back of the baseball card, Jazz Chisholm Jr. would be in line to sign a long-term deal this winter,” Finkelstein wrote. “Even in a down year, Jazz hit 19 home runs and stole 41 bases. He is a year removed from a 30-30 season, and he still has plenty of real estate left in his prime. The problem is that he has been consistently inconsistent, and his eccentric personality can become a headache for teams.
“The best case for Jazz is likely a 1+1 deal where he can reset his market and have a pillow of a player option to fall back on. The Phillies have too often been in the business of long-term commitments, but this is a case where they can focus on a shorter deal to add a talented, yet unreliable player. There is no doubt that Jazz can add some more thump to the middle of the Phillies lineup. And that would be quite the stage for him to host his second crack at a platform year.”
Chisholm would be an intriguing fit for the Phillies and is a polarizing figure. He played an inning with a lollipop in his mouth, which Aaron Boone wasn’t happy about.
Chisholm is also coming off a down season and is poised for a bounceback year. He hit .231 with 19 home runs and 55 RBIs. His career-high is 31 home runs and 80 RBIs.
Philadelphia Looking to be Aggressive
The Phillies are coming off another early playoff exit, and they are looking to be more aggressive.
Dave Dombrowski, who is the team’s President of Baseball Operations, said they are trying to build a World Series team.
“We’re expecting and we want to win a World Series,” Dombrowski said. … Our ownership has been as open to doing things as anybody possibly can be. We still haven’t sat down and set our final payrolls by any means for next year.
“[Phillies managing partner and chief executive officer] John [Middleton] and the group have always been quite accommodating, but we have a lot of high-salaried guys at this point, so I think you have to figure out which way you go. I don’t think it necessarily means signing all high-salary guys, but I do think we have the flexibility [to add players].”
The Phillies have yet to make a move this offseason.

item.title: [Heavy.com] Yankees’ Jazz Chisholm Jr. Predicted To Join AL East Rival in Free Agency

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees are on the verge of losing Jazz Chisholm Jr. in free agency.
As a high-profile Silver Slugger, it’s no surprise he’s floating in endless rumors.
But one MLB writer is predicting he’ll land with an AL East rival.
Yankees’ Jazz Chisholm Jr. May Head to Toronto
Per Zachary Rotman of FanSided, the Toronto Blue Jays remain the top destination for 28-year-old Chisholm.
“Ernie Clement was a surprising All-Star for the Toronto Blue Jays, but he struggled mightily down the stretch, posting a .442 OPS from August 1 through the end of the regular season,” he wrote.
“That was not only the lowest mark among 161 qualified position players, but it ranked more than 60 points below the second-worst mark. Clement should not be guaranteed a starting role, which leaves second base open for Chisholm, a player whose strengths are where the Jays are weakest.”
NEW YORK, NEW YORK – AUGUST 11: Jazz Chisholm Jr. #13 of the New York Yankees takes his turn at bat against the Seattle Mariners at Yankee Stadium on August 11, 2026 in the Bronx borough of New York City. (Photo by Elsa/Getty Images)
During Chisholm’s 2026 campaign, he was hitting .231/.312/.399 with a .711 OPS and 19 homers through 137 games.
He logged 16 doubles, three triples and 55 RBIs.
The year before, he slashed .242/.332/.481 with an .813 OPS and 31 homers through 130 games.
Along the way, he recorded 15 doubles, one triple and 80 RBIs.
As pointed out by Rotman, Chisholm has a tendency to strike out, but he balances himself by smacking home runs.
Looking at Chisholm’s Journey Through the Major Leagues
NEW YORK, NEW YORK – JULY 01: Jazz Chisholm Jr. #13 of the New York Yankees runs to first base after hitting a infield single during the ninth inning against the Detroit Tigers at Yankee Stadium on July 01, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images)
Chisholm made his Major League Baseball debut with the Marlins on Sept. 1, 2020.
He spent five seasons in Florida before they traded him to the Yankees in exchange for minor leaguer Abrahan Ramirez, along with Agustín Ramírez and Jared Serna.
NEW YORK, NEW YORK – AUGUST 12: Jazz Chisholm Jr. #13 of the New York Yankees tosses his bat after advancing to first base on a bases-loaded walk allowing Ben Rice #22 (not pictured) to score during the seventh inning against the Seattle Mariners at Yankee Stadium on August 12, 2026 in the Bronx borough of New York City. (Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images)
Shipping Chisholm out of New York would undoubtedly be a massive change for the organization and its fanbase, but seeing him land with an AL East rival would shake things up even more.

item.content:encoded:
Los New York Yankees están cerca de perder a Jazz Chisholm Jr. en la agencia libre.
No sorprende que el ganador del Bate de Plata sea objeto de tantos rumores.
Pero un periodista de la MLB pronostica que fichará con un rival de la División Este de la Liga Americana.
Jazz Chisholm Jr. podría dejar a los Yankees por Toronto
Según Zachary Rotman de FanSided, los Toronto Blue Jays siguen siendo el destino más probable para Chisholm, de 28 años.
“Ernie Clement fue una inesperada selección al Juego de Estrellas por los Toronto Blue Jays, pero tuvo muchas dificultades en el tramo final de la temporada: registró un OPS de .442 desde el 1 de agosto hasta el cierre de la temporada regular”, escribió.
“No solo fue el registro más bajo entre 161 jugadores de posición que cumplieron con el mínimo de apariciones al plato, sino que quedó a más de 60 puntos del segundo peor. Clement no debería tener asegurada la titularidad, lo que deja libre la segunda base para Chisholm, un jugador cuyas fortalezas coinciden con las principales debilidades de los Blue Jays”.
NUEVA YORK, NUEVA YORK – 11 DE AGOSTO: Jazz Chisholm Jr. #13 de los New York Yankees toma su turno al bate contra los Seattle Mariners en Yankee Stadium el 11 de agosto de 2026 en el distrito del Bronx de la ciudad de Nueva York. (Foto de Elsa/Getty Images)
En la temporada de 2026, Chisholm bateó .231/.312/.399, con un OPS de .711 y 19 jonrones en 137 partidos.
También conectó 16 dobles, tres triples y remolcó 55 carreras.
Un año antes, bateó .242/.332/.481, con un OPS de .813 y 31 jonrones en 130 partidos.
Además, conectó 15 dobles, un triple y remolcó 80 carreras.

item.content:encoded:
← Back to Sports
Bellinger Adds Platinum Glove to Yankees' Trophy Case
Cody Bellinger is adding another piece of hardware to his collection
Cody Bellinger is adding another piece of hardware to his collection, and this one is especially sweet for the New York Yankees. The Yankees outfielder was named the American League winner of the 2026 Platinum Glove Award on Friday night, recognizing him as the best overall defensive player in the league, regardless of position.
Rawlings announced the Platinum Glove winners for both leagues, with Chicago Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong taking home the National League honor. It was the first Platinum Glove Award for both players, but Bellinger's latest recognition adds to an already impressive defensive résumé.
Bellinger previously captured his second career Gold Glove this season, earning his first since his MVP-winning campaign with the Los Angeles Dodgers in 2019. Now, he has followed that up by being recognized as the top defensive player in the American League. It's quite a statement for a player who has brought the Yankees another level of versatility and athleticism in the outfield.
The numbers certainly back up the honor. Bellinger finished with 21 Defensive Runs Saved, tied for the third-most in all of Major League Baseball. Only Wilyer Abreu, with 28, and Brice Turang, with 23, finished ahead of him. Bellinger's ability to cover ground, read the ball off the bat and make difficult plays look routine has made him a valuable part of the Yankees' defense.
He also joins an exclusive group in Yankees history. Bellinger and catcher Jose Trevino, who won in 2022, are the only Yankees to capture the Platinum Glove since the award was introduced in 2011.
For the Yankees, Bellinger's defensive contributions have been just as important as anything he provides at the plate. In a lineup filled with power hitters, having an outfielder capable of changing games with his glove is a tremendous asset.
Bellinger has already proven he can deliver at the highest level, and his latest award is another reminder of just how valuable he is to the Yankees. The Platinum Glove is reserved for the very best, and this season, Bellinger earned his place at the top of the American League.

The report establishes interest, not an agreement or a known offer. A Yankees success story with a
item.content:encoded:
Paul Blackburn made himself much more expensive to replace than the Yankees probably expected a year ago. I'd make a serious effort to retain him, but not at the expense of pretending the rest of the bullpen is complete.
Newsday's Erik Boland reported that New York would like Blackburn back, while noting the club has several other needs and may not spend heavily on both him and closer David Bednar. The report establishes interest, not an agreement or a known offer.
A Yankees success story with a price attached
Blackburn finished the 2026 regular season with a 1.59 ERA over 85 innings in 62 games, including two starts. The right-hander gave New York more than a ninth-inning specialist: he could cover different parts of a game and handle more than one inning when needed.
That workload has value, particularly with Bednar and several other relievers reaching free agency. It also needs context. Blackburn struck out 69 and walked 33 in those 85 innings; repeating a sub-2.00 ERA is a much higher bar than remaining a useful pitcher.
0What do you think?Post a comment.
I'd pursue Blackburn with a clear term and salary limit, then add another reliable late-inning option rather than count on a single reunion. Keeping Bednar and shopping for a less expensive multi-inning reliever is a defensible alternative if Blackburn's market climbs.
The public reporting does not establish his price or whether he prefers to return. New York should pay for the flexibility he showed, not assume that his best season sets a guaranteed baseline for the next contract.

item.title: [Yanks Go Yard] Yankees 2027 lineup's Steamer projections make absolutely no sense

item.content:encoded:
2026 was proof of the gravity that Aaron Judge has on the New York Yankees lineup. Heading into the year with largely the same crew intact in a lineup that was at the top of the 2025 leaderboards in nearly every offensive category, the unit slumped without the three-time MVP. Weak isn't the right word to describe the group; rather "top-heavy" is a spot-on label.
So while we like what we've seen from Ben Rice, Cody Bellinger, and Luis Garcia Jr., we hope that the Yankees go into the offseason with plans to upgrade various spots behind these stars. That's why when the first batch of Steamer projections dropped, we found them ... curious.
Rice's projection sees him taking a step back to 2025's marks with a 135 projected wRC+, down from the 149 he posted in 2026. While that's a reasonable take solely looking at the data, Rice's cada día es lo mismo work ethic would make one believe that as long as he's healthy, he'll continue to ascend.
Bellinger and Garcia Jr. are both projected for 118 wRC+ performances. For Bellinger, that's exactly where his career average stands and seems like a rock-solid bet. Garcia Jr. put up a 124 mark in 2026, so this is a slight slide, but again, completely reasonable.
Youngsters Spencer Jones and George Lombard Jr. are both projected to be about league-average, give or take. Jones recorded a 106 wRC+ over 86 games this year and is now projected to post a 103 wRC+ in 2026. Lombard Jr. is projected to jump from a 93 mark in 2026 to a 99 mark in 2027. With so little data, we can't quibble much here, either. Development isn't always linear, so one future building block taking a tiny step back while the other takes a small step forward is likely.
From there, though, things start getting weird.
2027 Yankees projections are wildly bullish on Ryan McMahon and Austin Wells, pessimistic on Aaron Judge
It's pretty much a foregone conclusion that the Yankees will try to ditch Ryan McMahon this winter, but if they don't, can we really expect him to produce a nearly league-average line, as his predicted 93 wRC+ indicates? He put up a 78 wRC+ this year and was one of the worst hitters to get somewhat regular playing time in 2026.
As for Austin Wells, his prediction could be a bit more reasonable. He managed a 77 wRC+ in 2026, but that was based on a tale of two seasons. The 27-year-old backstop posted a 41 wRC+ in the first half, and a 124 wRC+ in the second half. If we believe the cervical headaches that sidelined him in June were the root cause of his struggles, then his projected mark of 99 isn't out of the question.
In total, a league-average bat at catcher and above-average defensive performance would make Wells a pretty valuable piece, considering the nature of the position. Maybe he doesn't need to be replaced after all.
Finally, there's Aaron Judge. From 2022-2025, he had put up a wRC+ over 200 in three of the four seasons. The 161 wRC+ Steamer projects him to produce in 2027 would've been the second-best wRC+ in the majors in 2026, but it's also a sizable step back for one of the game's all-time greats. On the one hand, this just highlights how otherworldly Judge's peak has been. On the other, it could foreshadow the start of the 34-year-old's decline.
Ultimately, while these are fun to look at, they're not incredibly telling. What projection systems like Steamer do is plug things into an algorithm and attempt to account for variables like the aging curve in order to predict future performance. In cases like Jones and Lombard Jr., there's not enough data to be incredibly accurate. In the case of Judge, his injury this year looms large. In the case of McMahon and Wells, well, the computer just went wild with those.

item.title: [Reviewing the Brew] Why Brewers fans should keep a close eye on David Bednar's qualifying offer decision with Yankees
item.dc:creator: Tyler Koerth
item.description: It took less than one week after the Milwaukee Brewers secured a World Series victory over the Tampa Bay Rays before trade rumors surrounding Trevor Megill began to surface. This speculation comes as little surprise, considering the Brewers entertained trade offers for Megill last winter as well before ultimately holding on to their All-Star closer. Now, a year later, Megill's trade stock is just as high as he is coming off back-to-back regular seasons with at least 30 saves, along with five add
item.content:encoded:
It took less than one week after the Milwaukee Brewers secured a World Series victory over the Tampa Bay Rays before trade rumors surrounding Trevor Megill began to surface. This speculation comes as little surprise, considering the Brewers entertained trade offers for Megill last winter as well before ultimately holding on to their All-Star closer.
Now, a year later, Megill's trade stock is just as high as he is coming off back-to-back regular seasons with at least 30 saves, along with five additional saves during the Brewers' World Series run. He is also entering the final year of team control before becoming a free agent, with MLB Trade Rumors projecting Megill to earn a $9 million salary in arbitration this year -- not bad for an All-Star flame-thrower.
With a probable lockout looming on December 1, ESPN's Jeff Passan reported that the Brewers' front office is once again going to listen to offers for the 32-year-old closer in the coming weeks. The New York Yankees have emerged as one potential suitor for Megill, though their level of interest ultimately hinges on whether or not their current closer, David Bednar, accepts the team's qualifying offer.
David Bednar's qualifying offer decision to have major impact on Yankees' trade interest in Brewers' closer Trevor Megill
The eight MLB players who received a qualifying offer last week, which includes Brewers' first baseman Jake Bauers and Bednar, the Yankees' closer, have until November 17 to decide if they want to accept the one-year, $23.15 million salary for the 2027 season or enter free agency. Bednar is coming off a season with New York where he racked up 35 saves over 69.1 innings with just a 2.47 ERA.
If Bednar accepts the qualifying offer, he would surpass Edwin Díaz's $23.01 million average annual salary as the highest single-season salary ever earned by a reliever. The alternative is to pursue a multi-year contract. Despite being the top closer available this offseason, the caveat with said alternative is that he would still likely have to settle for a lower annual average salary than the qualifying offer, but secure more guaranteed money over the life of the deal.
At 32 years old, Bednar faces an important decision, made even more complicated by uncertainty surrounding baseball's financial landscape and the looming potential work stoppage. However, his decision could ultimately determine whether the Yankees pursue Megill.
If Bednar accepts the qualifying offer and returns to New York, the Yankees may have little reason to pursue another closer on the trade market. However, if he declines, Brian Cashman could once again find himself on the phone with Brewers' front office head Matt Arnold to discuss a deal for a ninth-inning arm. Such a move would bring a sense of déjà vu, as the two previously negotiated a trade that sent All-Star closer Devin Williams to New York for Nestor Cortes and Caleb Durbin.

Rawlings awarded Bellinger with the Platinum Glove following a season in which he posted +21 defensive runs saved (DRS) in left field along with a +8 fielding run value (FRV) This is Bellinger’s first ever Platinum Glove, and he also won his second Gold Glove in 2026 as well. Though a former MVP and reliable power bat when healthy, he has always been a great fie
item.content:encoded:
New York Yankees outfielder Cody Bellinger has always been a great glove in the outfield, and can now add Platinum Glove to his resume. Rawlings awarded Bellinger with the Platinum Glove following a season in which he posted +21 defensive runs saved (DRS) in left field along with a +8 fielding run value (FRV)
This is Bellinger’s first ever Platinum Glove, and he also won his second Gold Glove in 2026 as well. Though a former MVP and reliable power bat when healthy, he has always been a great fielder too. He owns a +65 career DRS along with a +46 FRV, not to mention 38 outs above average (OAA).
What’s more, if we dig a little deeper, Cody Bellinger winning both a Gold and Platinum Glove disproves the argument that the Yankees Twitter folk love to make on the daily: the New York Yankees “don’t teach the fundamentals” or whatever rage-take to explain sloppy play in the field.
When, in reality? The Yankees haven’t finished with a negative team FRV since 2021. If anything, that’s one area in which they’ve significantly improved in the ensuing years. The team has been quite streaky with OAA, but think of what that stands for: Outs Above Average. As in outs that are tough to begin with and aren’t so routine.
But I digress. This is about Cody Bellinger, whose excellent outfield glove helps offset his sometimes streaky bat. The Yankees can look forward to at least one more year of him patrolling left field. He signed a five-year, $162.5 million deal last offseason that includes an opt-out after 2027.
Here’s hoping that the Yankees retool with a healthy Aaron Judge and a more consistent lineup next season. Platinum Glove for Cody Bellinger or no, fans’ restlessness continues.
Josh Benjamin has been a staff writer at ESNY since 2018. He has had opinions about everything, especially the Yankees and Knicks. He co-hosts the “Bleacher Creatures” podcast and is always looking for new pieces of sports history to uncover, usually with a Yankee Tavern chicken parm sub in hand.

item.content:encoded:
La temporada baja de la MLB de 2026 comenzó con varios premios individuales para los jugadores que marcaron la diferencia durante la temporada regular. Las actuaciones defensivas han recibido especial atención: los Guantes de Oro y los Guantes de Platino distinguen a los mejores defensores de las ligas Americana y Nacional.
Los New York Yankees y los Chicago Cubs tuvieron jugadores entre los defensores más destacados de las Grandes Ligas. Mientras los equipos evalúan sus plantillas y se preparan para la próxima temporada, estos premios también reconocen a quienes influyeron de forma constante en los partidos con su trabajo defensivo.
Los premios más recientes suman otro capítulo destacado a la temporada de dos jugadores que compartieron vestidor en Chicago. Sus actuaciones defensivas les valieron ahora el máximo reconocimiento individual.
Cody Bellinger y Pete Crow-Armstrong ganan el Guante de Platino
El jardinero de los Yankees Cody Bellinger ganó el Guante de Platino de la Liga Americana de 2026, mientras que su excompañero en los Cubs Pete Crow-Armstrong obtuvo el de la Liga Nacional. Ambos fueron elegidos los mejores defensores de sus respectivas ligas.
Rawlings anunció a los ganadores el viernes, después de la ceremonia del Guante de Oro. Los aficionados y las métricas defensivas determinan quién recibe el Guante de Platino entre los ganadores del Guante de Oro de cada liga.
Crow-Armstrong ganó el premio de la Liga Nacional tras una temporada sobresaliente en el jardín central: registró 26 outs por encima del promedio y 16 carreras salvadas a la defensiva, según “MLB”.
También ganó su segundo Guante de Oro consecutivo y lideró las Grandes Ligas en outs por encima del promedio.
La consistencia, el alcance, la velocidad y la cobertura del jugador de 24 años le permitieron realizar atrapadas difíciles y ubicarse entre los líderes de la liga en varias categorías defensivas.
Bellinger ganó el Guante de Platino de la Liga Americana tras una temporada sobresaliente a la defensiva con los Yankees: registró 21 carreras salvadas a la defensiva, empatado en el tercer puesto de las Grandes Ligas.
Ya había ganado un Guante de Oro con los Dodgers en 2019. Esta fue su segunda temporada con un Guante de Oro y la primera en la que obtuvo un Guante de Platino.
Bellinger jugó dos temporadas con los Cubs antes de unirse a los Yankees, mientras Crow-Armstrong se convirtió en uno de los mejores defensores del equipo de Chicago.
Sus logros más recientes les dan a los excompañeros otro gran premio individual para celebrar mientras avanza la temporada baja de la MLB de 2026.
Cubs y Blue Jays también reciben premios por su defensa colectiva
Los Chicago Cubs ganaron su segundo Guante de Oro por equipos consecutivo en la Liga Nacional, en reconocimiento a su sólida defensa en 2026.
Chicago lideró las Grandes Ligas con 72 outs por encima del promedio y 115 carreras salvadas a la defensiva, cifras que reflejan la solidez defensiva de los Cubs como equipo.
Crow-Armstrong contribuyó a ese éxito, mientras que el tercera base Alex Bregman ganó un Guante de Oro y sumó otro premio defensivo para Chicago.
Fue el tercer premio de los Cubs desde que Rawlings introdujo la categoría por equipos en 2020. Los dos triunfos consecutivos reflejan la consistencia de su defensa en las últimas dos temporadas.
En la Liga Americana, los Toronto Blue Jays recibieron el Guante de Oro por equipos. Toronto registró 51 carreras salvadas a la defensiva, la tercera mejor cifra de la Liga Americana, y terminó quinto con 14 outs por encima del promedio.
El reconocimiento a Crow-Armstrong se suma a una exitosa temporada de premios. La Asociación de Jugadores de la MLB lo nombró Jugador del Año y sigue entre los finalistas al Jugador Más Valioso de la Liga Nacional y al Bate de Plata.
El anuncio del Jugador Más Valioso está previsto para el 12 de noviembre y los premios Bate de Plata se anunciarán el 17 de noviembre.
El Guante de Platino de Bellinger y el nuevo premio de Crow-Armstrong suman reconocimientos para dos de los defensores más destacados de la temporada.

item.title: [Heavy.com] Yankees’ Cody Bellinger & Former Cubs Teammate Handed Major Honor
item.dc:creator: Debayan Biswas
item.description: The 2026 MLB offseason has begun with several individual awards recognizing the players who made a difference throughout the regular season. Defensive performances have received particular attention, with the Gold Glove and Platinum Glove honors highlighting the best fielders across the American and National Leagues. The New York Yankees and Chicago Cubs both had players among the league’s standout defenders. As teams assess their rosters and prepare for next season, these awards also recognize
item.content:encoded:
The 2026 MLB offseason has begun with several individual awards recognizing the players who made a difference throughout the regular season. Defensive performances have received particular attention, with the Gold Glove and Platinum Glove honors highlighting the best fielders across the American and National Leagues.
The New York Yankees and Chicago Cubs both had players among the league’s standout defenders. As teams assess their rosters and prepare for next season, these awards also recognize players who consistently influenced games with their work in the field.
The latest honors have added another notable chapter to the season for two players who previously shared a clubhouse in Chicago. Their defensive performances have now earned recognition at the highest individual level.
Cody Bellinger and Pete Crow-Armstrong Win Platinum Glove Awards
Yankees outfielder Cody Bellinger won the 2026 AL Platinum Glove, while former Cubs teammate Pete Crow-Armstrong claimed the NL award. Both were named their leagues’ top defenders.
Rawlings announced the winners Friday after the Gold Glove ceremony. Fans and defensive analytics select each league’s top defender from Gold Glove winners for the Platinum Glove.
Crow-Armstrong won the National League award after an outstanding season in center field, recording 26 Outs Above Average and 16 Defensive Runs Saved, according to “MLB.”
He also earned his second straight Gold Glove, leading the majors in Outs Above Average.
The 24-year-old’s consistency, range, speed, and coverage helped him make difficult catches and rank among league leaders in several defensive categories.
Bellinger won the American League Platinum Glove after a standout Yankees defensive season, recording 21 Defensive Runs Saved—tied for third-most in the majors.
He previously won a Gold Glove with the Dodgers in 2019. This marks his second Gold Glove season and first Platinum Glove.
Bellinger played two seasons with the Cubs before joining the Yankees, while Crow-Armstrong became one of their top defenders.
Their latest achievements give both former teammates another major individual award to celebrate as the 2026 MLB offseason continues.
Cubs and Blue Jays Also Earn Team Defensive Honors
The Chicago Cubs earned their second consecutive National League Team Gold Glove, recognizing their strong defense in 2026.
Chicago led the majors with 72 Outs Above Average and 115 Defensive Runs Saved, highlighting the Cubs’ collective defensive strength.
Crow-Armstrong helped lead the success, while third baseman Alex Bregman earned a Gold Glove, adding to Chicago’s defensive honors.
The Cubs’ latest award was their third since Rawlings introduced the team category in 2020. Back-to-back wins reflect their consistent defense over the past two seasons.
In the American League, the Toronto Blue Jays received the Team Gold Glove Award. Toronto recorded 51 Defensive Runs Saved, ranking third in the American League, and finished fifth with 14 Outs Above Average.
Crow-Armstrong’s recognition adds to a successful awards season. He was named MLB Players Association Player of the Year and remains an NL MVP and Silver Slugger finalist.
The MVP announcement is scheduled for November 12, while the Silver Slugger Awards will follow on November 17.
Bellinger’s Platinum Glove win and Crow-Armstrong’s latest achievement have added further recognition to two of the season’s most notable defensive performers.

item.content:encoded:
Los jardineros Pete Crow-Armstrong y Cody Bellinger fueron los nombrados al guante platino por la Liga Nacional y Liga Americana respectivamente.
Redacción
La empresa Rawlings anunció la noche del viernes a los ganadores de los Premios Guante de Platino 2026, reconocimiento que distingue al mejor jugador defensivo de cada liga de las Grandes Ligas, sin importar su posición, así como al equipo con el mejor desempeño defensivo de cada circuito.
En la Liga Nacional, el jardinero central de los Cachorros de Chicago, Pete Crow-Armstrong, obtuvo el galardón, mientras que Cody Bellinger, de los Yankees de Nueva York, fue reconocido en la Liga Americana. Para ambos peloteros fue la primera ocasión que reciben este premio.
Crow-Armstrong respaldó su distinción luego de conquistar su segundo Guante de Oro consecutivo y encabezar las Grandes Ligas con +26 Outs Por Encima del Promedio (OAA). El jardinero registró su segunda temporada consecutiva liderando o compartiendo el primer lugar de MLB en esta estadística, además de acumular 16 Carreras Salvadas a la Defensiva (DRS).
Por su parte, Bellinger consiguió el segundo Guante de Oro de su trayectoria, el primero desde 2019, y sumó 21 DRS, cifra que lo colocó empatado en el tercer puesto entre todos los jugadores de las Mayores.
En la categoría de equipos, los Cachorros de Chicago fueron reconocidos como la mejor defensiva de la Liga Nacional, mientras que los Azulejos de Toronto recibieron el premio correspondiente a la Liga Americana.
Chicago consiguió esta distinción por segundo año consecutivo y por tercera ocasión desde que Rawlings incorporó el reconocimiento colectivo en 2020. El conjunto terminó la temporada como el mejor defensivo de MLB, con +72 OAA y +115 DRS; además, Crow-Armstrong y Alex Bregman también fueron ganadores del Guante de Oro.
Los Azulejos, por su parte, conquistaron el reconocimiento por tercera ocasión, luego de obtenerlo también en 2023 y 2024, igualando a los Cachorros como las franquicias con más premios desde la creación de esta categoría. Toronto finalizó tercero en la Liga Americana con 51 DRS y quinto con +14 OAA, cifras que respaldaron su desempeño defensivo durante la campaña 2026.

item.content:encoded:
Two New York Yankees All-Stars were apparently having some problems with each other last season.
Yankees star slugger Aaron Judge had to “sternly” tell teammate Jazz Chisholm Jr. to knock off certain behaviors during the 2026 campaign that he felt crossed the line, Randy Miller of NJ.com reported this week. However, that reportedly did not stop Chisholm from continuing to act up throughout the Yankees’ season.
Chisholm, the 28-year-old former MLB All-Star, indeed made multiple negative headlines over the course of the year. Among other incidents, Chisholm was seen sucking on a lollipop while in the field during a game and also managed to get himself ejected for berating an umpire over a call.
As for Judge, 34, he is the Yankees’ captain and has been with the team for his entire MLB career since 2016. Thus, it is Judge’s job to an extent to call out unprofessional behavior by his teammates whenever he sees it.
Still, we recently learned that Judge himself was actually causing some internal frustrations with Yankees executives. Now it appears that friction with teammates has also been an issue for the former AL MVP Judge.
Chisholm is a free agent this offseason and might not be back with the Yankees in 2027. But even if New York decides to remove Chisholm from the equation, there may still be plenty of dysfunction left to go around.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Jazz Chisholm Jr. Finds Home With Reds Or Nats
item.dc:creator: Pat Bone
item.description: Jazz Chisholm Jr. brings elite speed and power, but his time in New York faces an uncertain future. The Yankees' second baseman posted a career-high 31 home runs in 2025, yet his consistency remains a major question mark. Fox Sports reports that his 1.7 wins above replacement (bWAR) and 97 OPS+ in 2026 likely cost him a long-term deal. item.content:encoded:
Jazz Chisholm Jr. brings elite speed and power, but his time in New York faces an uncertain future. The Yankees' second baseman posted a career-high 31 home runs in 2025, yet his consistency remains a major question mark. Fox Sports reports that his 1.7 wins above replacement (bWAR) and 97 OPS+ in 2026 likely cost him a long-term deal. Teams will pay for his talent, but they will not commit to a massive contract without proof of stability.
A Fresh Start in Washington
The Washington Nationals offer Chisholm a clear path to rebuild his value. Washington finished third in MLB in runs with 821 and slugged at .423 last season, showing they need more punch up the middle. While Nasim Nuñez led the National League with 49 stolen bases, he lacks the power Chisholm provides. The Nationals could use Chisholm to open 2027 as their starting second baseman and help fill the void left by trading Luis García Jr. and Curtis Mead. Chisholm's move gives him a chance to play either middle infield spot, depending on how the team handles shortstop CJ Abrams.
The Reds Need an Offensive Boost
With only 75 wins, Cincinnati finished last in the National League Central and urgently needs improvement. MLB hits totaled 1,231 for the Reds, who also recorded the league's lowest on-base percentage. Chisholm would give them a capable, impact left-handed hitter to balance the lineup. He would likely start at second base, pushing Matt McLain to the bench. McLain has been the primary second baseman for two years but hit a combined .204 during that stretch. Chisholm's two-time All-Star status would be a massive upgrade for Terry Francona's order.
The market for Chisholm will depend on how teams view his 37.3 stolen bases per season since 2024. He showed he can hit for power, with 80 RBIs in 2025, a year in which he also posted 4.1 wins above replacement. Under Aaron Boone, the Yankees made the postseason eight times over nine years, yet they must determine whether Chisholm belongs in their future. ESPN notes that free agents will come off the board quickly before the league shuts down on Dec. 1.

item.title: [vanguardia.com.mx] Jazz Chisholm, el chico malo de los Yankees que terminó ‘exhibiendo’ a Aaron Judge como capitán
item.dc:creator: Pascual Escandón
item.description: Jazz Chisholm, el chico malo de los Yankees que terminó ‘exhibiendo’ a Aaron Judge como capitán Sus desplantes e indisciplinas desgastaron la relación con el equipo. Ni siquiera los llamados de atención de Judge consiguieron ponerlo en cintura El talento nunca estuvo en discusión, pero su comportamiento terminó convirtiéndose en un problema. Jazz Chisholm Jr. se ganó la etiqueta de chico malo de los Yankees, un jugador que parecía disfrutar más de llamar la atención que de asumir la responsabili
item.content:encoded:
Jazz Chisholm, el chico malo de los Yankees que terminó ‘exhibiendo’ a Aaron Judge como capitán
Sus desplantes e indisciplinas desgastaron la relación con el equipo. Ni siquiera los llamados de atención de Judge consiguieron ponerlo en cintura
El talento nunca estuvo en discusión, pero su comportamiento terminó convirtiéndose en un problema. Jazz Chisholm Jr. se ganó la etiqueta de chico malo de los Yankees, un jugador que parecía disfrutar más de llamar la atención que de asumir la responsabilidad que implicaba vestir el uniforme de una de las franquicias más exigentes del beisbol de Grandes Ligas.
En Nueva York se cansaron de sus desplantes, sus distracciones y, sobre todo, de una actitud que muchos interpretaron como una falta de respeto hacia el equipo. El problema llegó a tal punto que Aaron Judge tuvo que intervenir personalmente para pedirle que dejara de hacer ciertas cosas que estaban cruzando los límites dentro del clubhouse.
La situación resulta todavía más incómoda porque Judge no es cualquier compañero. Es el capitán, la principal figura de los Bombarderos y uno de los jugadores más respetados de las Mayores. Sin embargo, ni su autoridad ni sus llamados de atención consiguieron modificar el comportamiento de Chisholm.
De acuerdo con el periodista Randy Miller, de NJ.com, el propio Jazz reconoció que Judge lo había reprendido en privado. El mensaje del capitán era claro: había comportamientos que no podían repetirse. Chisholm respondía que no volvería a hacerlo, pero las polémicas continuaban.
La paciencia se agotó. El pasado 2 de noviembre, los Yankees decidieron no ofrecerle la oferta calificada de 23.15 millones de dólares, dejándolo en libertad para negociar con cualquier organización. Aunque la decisión no descarta por completo una eventual negociación, representa una señal contundente de que su continuidad en el Bronx está lejos de ser una prioridad.
UN JUGADOR QUE PARECÍA DISFRUTAR LA POLÉMICA
Los episodios que fueron desgastando su relación con los Yankees no fueron pocos. Uno de los más comentados ocurrió en junio, cuando Chisholm apareció jugando como segunda base con una paleta en la boca, una imagen que provocó molestia y críticas, especialmente porque el equipo atravesaba momentos complicados.
También protagonizó enfrentamientos con los umpires que terminaron en expulsiones y exhibió actitudes poco profesionales durante los partidos. En la postemporada, por ejemplo, fue captado con los bolsillos traseros del pantalón volteados hacia afuera, un gesto que generó críticas por considerarse una provocación y una muestra de despreocupación.
A esto se sumaron errores en el corrido de bases y fallas fundamentales que terminaron por alimentar el descontento de los aficionados. El problema no era solamente lo que hacía, sino el momento en que lo hacía: mientras los Yankees necesitaban concentración, disciplina y compromiso, Jazz parecía empeñado en convertirse en protagonista por razones ajenas al beisbol.
La inconformidad también alcanzó a los seguidores del equipo, que terminaron abucheándolo durante la postemporada. Su rendimiento tampoco ayudó a cambiar la percepción: después de una campaña anterior en la que consiguió un histórico 30-30, sus números de 2026 quedaron por debajo de las expectativas.
La intervención de Aaron Judge abrió otro debate sobre el liderazgo dentro del vestidor neoyorquino. Randy Miller consideró que parte de la responsabilidad por los problemas de disciplina también recaía en el capitán, pues su influencia no había sido suficiente para detener las conductas de Chisholm y otros errores del equipo.
El periodista incluso cuestionó si Judge debía asumir una postura más severa con sus compañeros. Sin embargo, el columnista Bob Klapisch defendió al capitán y señaló que la responsabilidad de imponer castigos, sentar jugadores o aplicar sanciones corresponde principalmente al manager Aaron Boone y a la directiva, no necesariamente a quien lleva la distinción de capitán.
La discusión también involucró a figuras históricas de los Yankees, como CC Sabathia, Joe Girardi, Alex Rodríguez y Jorge Posada, quienes han cuestionado la pérdida de disciplina y los errores fundamentales que caracterizaron al equipo.
En ese contexto, el caso Chisholm se convirtió en el ejemplo más evidente de un vestidor que necesita recuperar autoridad y compromiso. Los Yankees conocían los antecedentes de Jazz desde su etapa con Miami, pero el experimento de incorporarlo al Bronx parece haber terminado sin los resultados esperados.
EL TALENTO NO ALCANZÓ PARA SALVARLO
En el terreno, Chisholm sigue siendo un pelotero atractivo por su velocidad, poder y capacidad para producir carreras. Su campaña anterior, con 30 cuadrangulares y 30 bases robadas, había elevado las expectativas sobre lo que podía aportar a Nueva York.
Sin embargo, en 2026 no consiguió mantener ese nivel y tampoco respondió como el equipo necesitaba cuando las lesiones de Judge y Giancarlo Stanton debilitaron la ofensiva. A los problemas deportivos se sumaron las distracciones que terminaron por convertirlo en uno de los personajes más cuestionados de la organización.
La decisión de no ofrecerle los 23.15 millones de dólares de la oferta calificada contrastó con el respaldo que sí recibió el cerrador David Bednar, quien fue incluido entre los jugadores a los que Nueva York extendió esa propuesta.
Para Chisholm, la agencia libre representa una oportunidad para encontrar un nuevo comienzo, pero también un examen sobre su madurez profesional. Puede ofrecer mucho dentro del diamante, aunque las organizaciones interesadas tendrán que valorar si su personalidad y sus antecedentes compensan el riesgo de incorporarlo.
Los Yankees parecen haber llegado al límite de su paciencia. Y si algo deja este episodio es que ni siquiera compartir vestidor con Aaron Judge, uno de los líderes más respetados de las Grandes Ligas, fue suficiente para que Jazz Chisholm entendiera que en Nueva York el espectáculo debe estar en el terreno y no en sus desplantes.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees will have a lot of decisions to make over the offseason.
Free agency across the MLB opened up on Monday night.
New York Yankees Suddenly Lose Key Member
On Friday, news came out that the Yankees lost a key member of their coaching staff.
Joel Sherman of The New York Post reported the news.
Sherman wrote: “The Yankees are losing a key member of their coaching staff, Tanner Swanson, who is joining the Mariners as their bench coach.”
Social Media Reactions
Manager Aaron Boone of the New York Yankees looks on during batting practice before the game against the Boston Red Sox in game two of the American League Wild Card Series at Yankee Stadium on September 30, 2026 in the Bronx borough of New York City.
Here’s what people were saying about the news:
Gary Phillips: “Tanner Swanson, the #Yankees’ longtime and valued catching director, is leaving to be the #Mariners’ new bench coach, as @Joelsherman1 first mentioned. Swanson and new M’s manager Jason Kanzler have some mutual friends, and Swanson is from Seattle. He was on an expiring deal, and he received some interest as a bench coach last year, so this is not a surprise. Mentioned the possibility of SEA here a few weeks ago:”
Jorge Castillo: “Yankees catching coach Tanner Swanson is leaving the organization to become the Mariners’ bench coach, a source confirms to ESPN. Swanson was in that role since the 2020 season. He will now be Jason Kanzler’s right-hand man in Seattle. @Joelsherman1 was first on the news.”
Manager Aaron Boone #17 of the New York Yankees looks on during batting practice before game one of the American League Division Series against the Tampa Bay Rays at Tropicana Field on October 03, 2026 in St Petersburg, Florida.
@eyyankees: “Catching coach Tanner Swanson is leaving the Yankees to join the Seattle Mariners as their bench coach, per @Joelsherman1 . Undoubtedly a tough loss for the organization.”
JackCurryYES: “Tanner Swanson, an impactful coach with the Yankees, is leaving to become the bench coach with Seattle. @Joelsherman1 was on it.”
Looking At The Yankees
The Yankees last won a World Series title in 2009.
They had reached the World Series in 2024.
