item.content:encoded:
Tigers could pursue another Yankees All-Star 2B after Gleyber Torres originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Detroit Tigers could be looking for a new second baseman during this offseason.
Gleyber Torres is a free agent after spending the past two seasons with the Tigers, hitting .260/.364/.363 with eight home runs and a 105 OPS+ in 96 games in 2026.
Torres has become a great on-base guy the last few years, but he offers little to no value with his legs on the basepaths.
Detroit could have Zach McKinstry and Hao-Yu Lee split time at second base, or they could target another former New York Yankees middle infielder.
"The lineup is less of a concern, but Jazz Chisholm Jr. to Detroit wouldn't be a colossal surprise.
"At any rate, the last time the Yankees let a multiple-time All-Star second baseman walk in free agency without even extending him a qualifying offer, Gleyber Torres ended up with the Tigers. Perhaps they bring in Chisholm to replace him," Bleacher Report's Kerry Miller wrote.
Chisholm doesn't get on base nearly enough to match Torres' .364 OBP, but he hit 19 homers and stole a career-high 41 bases this past season.
The Tigers stole 58 bases across 162 games, just 17 more than Chisholm swiped by himself.
Adding athleticism to the lineup could help the Tigers get back to the top of the AL Central. Obviously, Chisholm's been a topic of discussion for some negative reasons, including playing the field with a lollipop in his mouth.
You'd like to think the Tigers would make it clear that those kinds of things are not allowed, especially under manager A.J. Hinch.
They could use a few additions to the starting rotation too, but signing Chisholm would be a solid start to the offseason for Detroit.

item.title: [The Big Lead] Don Mattingly reveals new Kyle Schwarber-Bryce Harper plan for Phillies 2027 season
item.dc:creator: Lou Landers
item.description: The Philadelphia Phillies are already looking at ways to keep their veteran stars fresher throughout the 2027 MLB season, and new manager Don Mattingly has a plan involving Kyle Schwarber and Bryce Harper. The idea would give both players more opportunities to rest while creating additional flexibility for Philadelphia’s lineup. Don Mattingly mentions that the Phillies will look to play Kyle Schwarber at first base 25-35 times a year to get Bryce Harper opportunities at DH ⬇️ https://t.co/pXLEJh
item.content:encoded:
The Philadelphia Phillies are already looking at ways to keep their veteran stars fresher throughout the 2027 MLB season, and new manager Don Mattingly has a plan involving Kyle Schwarber and Bryce Harper. The idea would give both players more opportunities to rest while creating additional flexibility for Philadelphia’s lineup.
Don Mattingly mentions that the Phillies will look to play Kyle Schwarber at first base 25-35 times a year to get Bryce Harper opportunities at DH ⬇️ https://t.co/pXLEJhCC6L
— MLB Network (@MLBNetwork) November 5, 2026
Schwarber could see considerably more time at first base, allowing Harper to move into the designated hitter spot more frequently. It is a strategy that could benefit multiple players over the course of a long season.
Kyle Schwarber could play 25-35 games at first base
The Phillies are considering using Schwarber at first base approximately 25-35 times during the 2027 season. That would represent a significant increase in his defensive workload and give Philadelphia another way to manage Harper’s playing time.
Schwarber has primarily served as the team’s designated hitter, but moving him into the field would allow Harper to take over at DH on those occasions. Harper played every game during the 2026 season, and getting him off his feet more often is an important objective for the Phillies.
Philadelphia president of baseball operations Dave Dombrowski previously discussed budgeting for approximately 30 games at first base for Schwarber. The plan is part of a broader effort to keep the team’s veteran players fresher as they get older.
There is also the possibility that Harper could spend some time in the outfield with Schwarber playing first base. That would create even more options for Mattingly when putting together his daily lineup.
Phillies could have considerably more lineup flexibility
The biggest benefit of the plan is that it would give Mattingly more ways to manage his everyday players without necessarily taking their bats out of the lineup.
If Schwarber plays first base and Harper moves to the outfield, the designated hitter spot becomes available for another player. That could allow someone else in the lineup to receive a half-day off while still contributing offensively.
Rather than giving a player a complete day off, Mattingly could rotate players through the DH position and provide additional rest when needed. Over a 162-game MLB season, those opportunities could become valuable, particularly for a veteran roster with several important contributors.
The Phillies have made it clear that keeping their veteran players healthy and productive is a priority heading into 2027. Finding different ways to use Schwarber, Harper and the DH position could be an important part of that approach.
If the plan works as intended, Philadelphia could have a more flexible lineup while giving two of its biggest stars opportunities to stay fresher throughout the season.

item.content:encoded:
3 Best MLB Free Agent Fits For Jazz Chisholm Jr. If He Leaves Yankees
There's no denying Jazz Chisholm Jr.'s talent.
The New York Yankees' second baseman has whippish power from the left side of the plate, can move like the wind and make highlight-reel plays at second. The issue? Consistency.
Just one year ago in 2025, Chisholm was both an All-Star and a Silver Slugger. Then, he posted just 1.7 wins above replacement and a 97 OPS+ in 2026. Chisholm's talent figures to fetch him a considerable average annual salary, but the inconsistency that dates back to his time with the Miami Marlins (2020-24) likely precludes Chisholm from getting a long-term deal.
Here are the three best MLB free agent fits for Chisholm if he leaves New York:
At face value, Chisholm fits the bill for the Washington Nationals.
Chisholm would open 2027 as Washington's starting second baseman, helping replenish some of the quality production it traded away during the 2026 season in infielders Luis García Jr. and Curtis Mead. Yet, the Nationals still finished third in MLB in runs (821) and slugging percentage (.423).
Now, Washington does have Nasim Nuñez, who led the National League with 49 stolen bases in 2026 and posted 13 defensive runs saved at second base, but he doesn't possess the power, nor the track record of producing at the plate of Chisholm. In 2025, Chisholm totaled a career-high 31 home runs, 80 RBIs and 4.1 wins above replacement. Meanwhile, he has stolen 37.3 bases per season since 2024.
Plus, while shortstop and two-time All-Star CJ Abrams, — who's two years away from free agency — got run at second base down the stretch of last season, it's possible he'll be traded this offseason, given the chance he and the Nationals don't reach an extension. The Nationals could offer Chisholm — who has also played shortstop, including 310 starts in the minor leagues — a roadmap to playing either middle infield position (depending on where they prefer to start Abrams, should he not be traded) and rehab his value for a bigger payday down the road.
All that said, Washington may want to leave the door open for top prospect Eli Willits, the No. 1 pick in the 2025 MLB Draft, to play every day at one of the two middle infield positions should he rocket through the minor-league ranks next year and/or have Abrams be able to ease into playing second base on a full-time basis.
The Cincinnati Reds, who finished last in the NL Central with 75 wins last season, need upside — which Chisholm could provide.
In all likelihood, Chisholm would start at second base, moving Matt McLain to the bench, where he'd presumably be the first infielder off the bench. McLain, who has been Cincinnati's primary second baseman the last two years in a period that has seen him hit a combined .204, has also made 82 career starts at shortstop.
Chisholm, a two-time All-Star, would give Cincinnati an offensive upgrade at second and a capable, impact left-handed hitter to balance out manager Terry Francona's order. As for that offense, the Reds were last in MLB in hits (1,231) and on-base percentage (.305), 27th in runs (666) and 25th in slugging percentage (.394) last year, while recording the second-most strikeouts (1,544). Granted, they were fourth with 213 home runs.
Meanwhile, Cincinnati has been unable to get consistent outfield production from those not named JJ Bleday. Another option for the Reds is keeping McLain at second base and putting Chisholm in center field. Chisholm has extensive experience playing both middle infield positions, third base and center field, where he made 186 starts with the Miami Marlins.
At the same time, Cincinnati may prefer to stay the course with McLain — who was their first-round selection in 2021 — at second base and add a center fielder who consistently plays the position.
The San Francisco Giants need a second baseman, offense and something to smile about. Chisholm could check all those boxes.
Luis Arráez was terrific for the Giants last season, but the infielder's play — highlighted by hitting .324 — turned him into a prime trade candidate for a team that wasn't competing for the playoffs, so off Arráez went to the Philadelphia Phillies at the trade deadline.
Now, Giants shortstop Willy Adames needs a double-play partner. Chisholm would fill San Francisco's void at second base and, perhaps as importantly, enhance an offense that was 29th in MLB in on-base percentage (.306), 26th in runs (669) and tied for 17th in slugging percentage (.400) last season.
From a sheer talent standpoint, Chisholm is an enticing option for any team that needs a second baseman. Still just 28 years old, it's feasible to believe he can be a perennial All-Star-caliber player because that's what Chisholm has been at his best. Perhaps the Yankees not re-signing Chisholm will light a fire under him?
Realistically, the Giants aren't one or two players away from being a wild-card team. With that in mind, they're an ideal situation for Chisholm to get back on track. They're not contenders, and it's a franchise searching for answers. Chisholm aims to get right, and San Francisco hopes to capture lightning in a bottle. It's a low-risk, potentially high-reward setup.

item.content:encoded:
Jazz Chisholm Jr. se encamina a la agencia libre sin recibir una oferta calificada de los New York Yankees. Una propuesta de canje que Baseball Trade Values publicó el jueves plantea que los Yankees lo reemplacen con un exprospecto de los Boston Red Sox.
Los Yankees le hicieron a David Bednar una oferta calificada de 23.15 millones de dólares el lunes, pero no le ofrecieron una a Chisholm. Es una señal clara de que están dispuestos a dejarlo ir en la agencia libre y abrir una vacante en la segunda base. Pero ¿sería el segunda base de los White Sox, Chase Meidroth, una mejora?
El sitio, que evalúa las propuestas de canje asignando un valor numérico a cada jugador, enviaría a Anthony Volpe, Elmer Rodriguez, Will Warren y Ben Hess a los Chicago White Sox. Su modelo calcula un valor excedente de 53.4 para ese paquete, frente a 42.2 para Meidroth.
La agencia libre de Jazz Chisholm Jr. deja vacante la segunda base de los Yankees
Chisholm, de 28 años, nacido en Nassau, Bahamas, y elegido dos veces al Juego de Estrellas, llegó desde Miami en julio de 2024 a cambio del receptor Agustín Ramírez y dos jugadores del cuadro. Esta temporada bateó .231/.312/.399 con 19 jonrones y robó 41 bases, su máximo de por vida, pero se ponchó en el 29.5% de sus apariciones al plato. Sus métricas defensivas fueron de +15 en Outs Above Average y -6 en Defensive Runs Saved.
Un año antes, Chisholm bateó .242/.332/.481 con 31 jonrones. Luego se fue de 2-11 ante Tampa Bay en la serie divisional, cometió un error de tiro en el partido 2 y quedó fuera de la alineación durante dos partidos.
“Aquí es donde quiero estar”, dijo Chisholm tras la barrida, según el New York Post. El exgerente general de MLB Jim Bowden no estaba tan convencido: dijo en “Foul Territory” que, si aún dirigiera un equipo de béisbol, “probablemente descartaría a ambos”, Chisholm y Ketel Marte.
Chisholm ganó 10.2 millones de dólares esta temporada. Según MLB.com, habría pedido 35 millones de dólares anuales por un contrato de ocho a diez años, mientras que un directivo estimó un acuerdo de tres o cuatro años por cerca de 20 millones de dólares anuales. Meidroth ganó 789,100 dólares la temporada pasada y no podrá acudir al arbitraje salarial hasta 2028.
¿Sería Chase Meidroth una mejora respecto a Jazz Chisholm Jr.?
Meidroth, de 25 años, es oriundo de Torrance, California, y jugó en la Universidad de San Diego. Los Red Sox lo seleccionaron en la cuarta ronda del draft de 2022 antes de que llegara a los White Sox en el canje de Garrett Crochet. En 2026 bateó .276/.350/.415 con 16 jonrones. Su OPS de .765 superó el .711 de Chisholm y sus 4.5 de fWAR fueron la mejor cifra entre los segunda base de la Liga Americana, una victoria por encima de las 3.5 de Chisholm.
Chisholm tiene ventaja en poder y velocidad.
El costo del canje son cuatro jugadores. Rodriguez, de 23 años y oriundo de Trujillo Alto, Puerto Rico, es el prospecto número 2 de la organización. Tuvo marca de 0-3 y efectividad de 5.40 en seis aperturas, con 21 ponches en 26⅔ entradas. Los Red Sox lo seleccionaron en la cuarta ronda del draft de 2021 y llegó desde Boston a cambio de Carlos Narvaez.
Volpe, de 25 años, nació en Manhattan y fue seleccionado en la primera ronda del draft de 2019. Ganó el Guante de Oro de la Liga Americana como campocorto en 2023. Bateó .212/.272/.391 en 2025 y, tras una cirugía de hombro, regresó para batear .245 con dos jonrones en 2026, después de firmar un contrato de un año por 3.48 millones de dólares.
Warren, de 27 años, oriundo de Brandon, Mississippi y seleccionado en la octava ronda del draft tras jugar en Southeastern Louisiana, tuvo marca de 11-6 y efectividad de 3.92, con 158 ponches en 156 entradas.
Hess, de 24 años y oriundo de Charleston, Illinois, fue la selección número 26 del draft de 2024 tras jugar en Alabama. Registró efectividad de 4.45 en 56⅔ entradas antes de que su ingreso a la lista de lesionados de 60 días pusiera fin a su temporada. En 2025 había registrado efectividad de 3.22 en 103⅓ entradas.
En lo deportivo, Chicago recibiría a un abridor, un campocorto que ganó el Guante de Oro y dos prospectos de pitcheo. Nueva York cubriría la segunda base, pero perdería las 29 aperturas de Warren. Según el modelo del sitio, Chicago saldría ganando por 11.2 puntos y Warren por sí solo representa más de la mitad de los 42.2 puntos de Meidroth. Los dos equipos rara vez hacen canjes. Un canje de siete jugadores en julio de 2017 llevó a Todd Frazier, David Robertson y Tommy Kahnle a Nueva York. En el más reciente, el relevista Keynan Middleton llegó a Nueva York a cambio de Juan Carela el 1 de agosto de 2023.

item.title: [Heavy.com] Yankees Trade Pitch Lands Jazz Chisholm Replacement in 4-For-1 White Sox Deal
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Vankin
item.description: Jazz Chisholm Jr. is headed for free agency without a qualifying offer from the New York Yankees, and a trade pitch published Thursday by Baseball Trade Values and aimed at the Yankees would replace him with a former Boston Red Sox prospect. The Yankees’ $23.15 million qualifying offer to David Bednar came Monday, but none went to Chisholm, a strong indication that the Yankees are fully prepared to let Chisholm walk in free agency, opening a second base vacancy. But would White Sox second basema
item.content:encoded:
Jazz Chisholm Jr. is headed for free agency without a qualifying offer from the New York Yankees, and a trade pitch published Thursday by Baseball Trade Values and aimed at the Yankees would replace him with a former Boston Red Sox prospect.
The Yankees’ $23.15 million qualifying offer to David Bednar came Monday, but none went to Chisholm, a strong indication that the Yankees are fully prepared to let Chisholm walk in free agency, opening a second base vacancy. But would White Sox second baseman Chase Meidroth be an upgrade?
The site, which grades proposed deals with numerical values assigned to each player, would send Anthony Volpe, Elmer Rodriguez, Will Warren and Ben Hess to the Chicago White Sox, valuing that package at 53.4 in surplus against 42.2 for Meidroth.
Jazz Chisholm Jr. Free Agency Leaves Yankees 2nd Base Open
Chisholm, 28, a two-time All-Star born in Nassau, Bahamas, arrived from Miami in July 2024 for catcher Agustín Ramírez and two infielders. He hit .231/.312/.399 with 19 homers and a career-high 41 steals this season, but struck out in 29.5% of his plate appearances. His glove graded at plus-15 Outs Above Average and minus-6 Defensive Runs Saved.
A year earlier, Chisholm slashed .242/.332/.481 with 31 homers. He then went 2-for-11 against Tampa Bay in the division series, made a throwing error in Game 2 and sat two games.
“This is where I want to be,” Chisholm said after the sweep, as quoted by the New York Post. Former MLB general manager Jim Bowden was less sure, saying on “Foul Territory” he would “probably pass on both” Chisholm and Ketel Marte if he were still running a baseball organization.
Chisholm earned $10.2 million this season. He reportedly sought $35 million annually over eight to 10 years, while an executive projected three or four years near $20 million, according to MLB.com. Meidroth earned $789,100 last season, and is not eligible for arbitration until 2028.
Would Chase Meidroth Be an Upgrade Over Jazz Chisholm Jr.?
Meidroth, 25, a Torrance, California, native and University of San Diego product, was a Red Sox fourth-round pick in 2022 who arrived at the White Sox in the Garrett Crochet trade, and hit .276/.350/.415 with 16 homers in 2026. His .765 OPS topped Chisholm’s .711, and his 4.5 fWAR led American League second basemen, a full win above Chisholm’s 3.5.
Chisholm owns the edge in power and speed.
The price is four players. Rodriguez, 23, from Trujillo Alto, Puerto Rico, is the No. 2 prospect in the system and went 0-3 with a 5.40 ERA in six starts, striking out 21 over 26⅔ innings. The Red Sox drafted him in the fourth round in 2021, and he came from Boston for Carlos Narvaez.
Volpe, 25, a Manhattan native and 2019 first-rounder, won the 2023 AL Gold Glove at shortstop. Volpe hit .212/.272/.391 in 2025 and returned from shoulder surgery to bat .245 with two homers in 2026, after signing a one-year, $3.48 million contract.
Warren, 27, a Brandon, Mississippi, native and eighth-round pick out of Southeastern Louisiana, went 11-6 with a 3.92 ERA and 158 strikeouts in 156 innings.
Hess, 24, from Charleston, Illinois, was the 26th overall pick in 2024 out of Alabama and posted a 4.45 ERA over 56⅔ innings before the 60-day injured list ended his year, after a 3.22 ERA across 103⅓ innings in 2025.
Competitively, Chicago gets a starter, a former Gold Glove shortstop and two pitching prospects, while New York fills second base but loses Warren’s 29 starts. By the site’s model, Chicago wins by 11.2 points, and Warren alone makes up more than half of Meidroth’s 42.2. The two clubs rarely deal. A seven-player trade in July 2017 brought Todd Frazier, David Robertson and Tommy Kahnle to New York. The latest sent reliever Keynan Middleton to New York for Juan Carela on Aug. 1, 2023.

item.title: [roundtable.io] Yankees' Cody Bellinger, Ben Rice Named 2026 Silver Slugger Finalists
item.dc:creator: Matt Levine
item.description: New York had multiple players go off this season. New York was able to make the playoffs, despite not having star Aaron Judge for a large portion of the season. And the team was able to see multiple players put together strong contributions to keep the year alive. Two of them were star outfielder Cody Bellinger and infielder Ben Rice, both of which supplied the Yankees with a ton of power. And due to the performances from the two players, they each have now earned being named Silver Slugger Fina
item.content:encoded:
New York had multiple players go off this season.
New York was able to make the playoffs, despite not having star Aaron Judge for a large portion of the season. And the team was able to see multiple players put together strong contributions to keep the year alive.
Two of them were star outfielder Cody Bellinger and infielder Ben Rice, both of which supplied the Yankees with a ton of power. And due to the performances from the two players, they each have now earned being named Silver Slugger Finalists for the 2026 season.
For the year, Bellinger hit .264 with 17 home runs and 73 RBIs, while posting an OPS of .767 for the Yankees. Bellinger had to take on a larger role for the offense with Judge out, and he delivered during the regular season.
As for Rice, he hit .264 as well, slamming 41 home runs and 97 RBIs, while putting up an OPS of .897. Rice continued his breakout form for the Yankees, delivering an impressive season for this team.
With the Yankees having these two stars and Judge back for next season, the sky is the limit for New York if they can stay healthy. This team is looking to win another World Series, with the drought extending into the past season.
The offense could use a little improvement around the edges of the roster, with the front office needing to add this offseason. But given the overall power that this group has, the Yankees seem to be in good shape for next season.
New York has the pitching staff to make it happen, but the Yankees need a little more luck to get it done. One area that the front office could target is the bullpen, with the Yankees needing to bring in some fresh bullpen arms.
The team tried to land a star closer this year at the trade deadline, but the Yankees weren't able to get the job done. But the front office has been linked to multiple names on the market this winter, with many seeing the Yankees land someone.
Patience has started to wear thin among the fanbase in the Bronx, with the Yankees drought going on for a long time. But this team is in a good place for next season, especially with the offense going strong.

item.title: [Pinstripe Alley] Should the Yankees hold onto Jasson Domínguez?
item.dc:creator: Andrés Chávez
item.description: Three years ago, Jasson Domínguez was one of the most promising position player prospects in baseball. item.content:encoded:
Three years ago, Jasson Domínguez was one of the most promising position player prospects in baseball. The 2023 campaign saw the man known as “the Martian” demolish Double-A, Triple-A, and MLB pitching, the last two in small samples following a pair of quick promotions as the Yankees’ depth depleted due to injury. Since then, however, he has been unable to truly establish himself in The Show both offensively and defensively.
In 2026, Domínguez took another step back. In 222 plate appearances, the 23-year-old outfielder slashed .225/.267/.368 with six homers, eight stolen bases, and a 76 wRC+. He wasn’t exactly a menace the year prior and his glove was rough, but the switch-hitter had at least produced against righties enough to be a league-average bat (99 wRC+). Domínguez was worth -0.2 fWAR in 2026 and now has 0.5 in 206 career MLB games.
Injuries were a factor, particularly that low-grade AC joint sprain he suffered back in May that sent him to the list, but the reality is that even after getting healthy, Domínguez didn’t impress nearly enough to give the Yankees a reason to stick with him as their overall offense sagged. Eventually, the Bombers acquired Heliot Ramos and promoted Spencer Jones, making Domínguez expendable on the active roster. He went to the minors and appeared in just four MLB games post-Trade Deadline.
This all leads to the question: should the Yankees keep Domínguez around for 2027? Has he done enough to keep getting chances? It all comes down to New York’s winter activity and his one minor-league option. That’s probably enough to keep him around as organizational depth, with at least a modicum of breakout appeal, but there are several avenues the team can opt to take with the former top prospect.
The Yankees will enter the 2027 campaign with Aaron Judge, Cody Bellinger, Jones, and Ramos in the outfield, plus Domínguez and José Caballero, who can also play there if needed (Giancarlo Stanton is purely a DH if he returns). A new outfielder via free agency or trade can’t be ruled out, either. That’s a lot of people for just a handful of spots, and for the sake of his development, the Martian should be playing every day.
If Domínguez isn’t traded in the offseason, he will likely start the year in Triple-A unless he wins a spot in spring training (or “summer” training, whenever it takes place due to the looming lockout). It’s probably a less likely scenario at this point, but it’s certainly plausible, especially if any injuries pop up ahead of him.
Trading Domínguez when his value is this low might not be ideal—they’re not going to trade him just to trade him—but again, it will all depend on the proposed return and if he’s fitting in as the lead piece in a deal or part of a larger package. Gauging his current value against what he could offer down the road is tricky because just as he has bounce-back potential, he could also crash out even more and become older and worse.
Probably thanks to that remaining minor-league option, Domínguez will remain with the Yankees if they don’t find a trade scenario that feels appropriate. However, his time with the organization is reaching a turning point as he enters a key offseason in his development. He’s currently playing Dominican winter ball in LIDOM, but things might get messy if/when the Yanks can’t communicate with him to track his training and offseason routine because of the lockout.
Lockout or not, Domínguez needs to take a step forward in the plate discipline department after posting an awful 4.5-percent walk rate in 2026. That’s where it all should start. A quick look at his Savant page, however, tells us that the raw tools are there for Domínguez to be better than he has been to this point:
Upper-echelon bat speed, but subpar contact metrics. Elite arm strength, but subpar defense and range. He has excellent speed, too, so athleticism doesn’t seem to be the problem.
Domínguez needs to hit the ball with more authority, but above all things, he needs to gain consistency with both swings. This year, he posted a 58 wRC+ hitting from the left side of the plate and 105 from the right side, which is baffling because the split was reversed in each of his previous three MLB campaigns.
There’s a very good chance that Domínguez is part of the Yankees organization as teams enter play in 2027. But if so, there’s no longer any margin for error. His spot in the team’s future plans is unquestionably in jeopardy.

item.dc:creator: Ahoramismo Staff
item.description: Los New York Yankees tienen decisiones importantes que tomar esta temporada baja y el equipo parece interesado en conservar a una de las mayores sorpresas de su campaña de 2026. El veterano lanzador Paul Blackburn resurgió esta temporada en Nueva York y se convirtió en una opción confiable para el bullpen tras pasar apuros durante gran parte del año anterior. item.content:encoded:
Los New York Yankees tienen decisiones importantes que tomar esta temporada baja y el equipo parece interesado en conservar a una de las mayores sorpresas de su campaña de 2026.
El veterano lanzador Paul Blackburn resurgió esta temporada en Nueva York y se convirtió en una opción confiable para el bullpen tras pasar apuros durante gran parte del año anterior.
Ahora, los Yankees muestran mucho interés en volver a contratarlo.
En un reporte del 5 de noviembre para el New York Daily News, el periodista de los Yankees Gary Phillips citó fuentes que señalan que el equipo tiene mucho interés en renovar el contrato de Blackburn.
La noticia llama la atención porque antes se pronosticaba que Blackburn dejaría Nueva York como agente libre.
No se ha anunciado ningún acuerdo, pero los reportes más recientes indican que los Yankees prefieren no perder a uno de sus relevistas más productivos.
Los Yankees muestran mucho interés en volver a contratar a Paul Blackburn
La transformación de Blackburn ha sido una de las sorpresas más gratas para Nueva York.
El derecho llegó a los Yankees en 2025 después de que sus rivales de la ciudad, los Mets, lo dejaran libre, pero sus primeros resultados no convencieron.
Terminó esa temporada con una efectividad de 5.28 en ocho apariciones con Nueva York, lo que dejó muchas dudas sobre su futuro.
Sin embargo, Blackburn regresó en 2026 y firmó su mejor temporada en números en las Grandes Ligas.
El lanzador de 32 años terminó con marca de 7-3, efectividad de 1.59 y 69 ponches en 85 entradas, con 62 apariciones, incluidas dos aperturas.
También registró un WHIP de 1.08 y limitó a los bateadores rivales a un promedio de .195.
Esas cifras consolidaron a Blackburn como una opción confiable para las últimas entradas y dieron a los Yankees un valioso complemento para el cerrador David Bednar.
La eficacia de Blackburn impresionó aún más por su trayectoria previa como abridor.
Elegido al Juego de Estrellas de 2022 con Oakland, había trabajado principalmente como abridor antes de pasar al bullpen en una etapa posterior de su carrera.
Aunque su total de ponches fue relativamente modesto, Blackburn demostró que sabe limitar los hits y evitar las carreras.
Su actuación en 2026 reforzó sus posibilidades de conseguir otro contrato en las Grandes Ligas, aunque Nueva York debe evaluar si puede mantener esos resultados.
El FIP de Blackburn, una medida de efectividad independiente de la defensa, fue de 3.74, muy superior a su efectividad, lo que plantea dudas sobre si podrá mantener ese nivel de éxito.
Aun así, los Yankees tienen motivos claros para querer que regrese.
Los Yankees afrontan decisiones clave para su bullpen en la agencia libre
Blackburn no es el único lanzador conocido que Nueva York espera conservar.
Los Yankees ya le hicieron una oferta calificada de 23.15 millones de dólares a David Bednar, quien consiguió 35 salvamentos durante la temporada de 2026.
Bednar tiene hasta el 17 de noviembre para aceptar la oferta por un año o seguir en busca de otro contrato.
Nueva York también debe tomar decisiones sobre otros relevistas que son agentes libres, entre ellos Tim Hill, Ryan Yarbrough, John Schreiber y Michael Fulmer.
Según el reporte de Phillips, los Yankees tienen cierto interés en conservar a Hill y también se han comunicado con Yarbrough.
Sin embargo, volver a contratar a lanzadores conocidos no resolverá necesariamente todos los problemas.
Con varios integrantes del bullpen rumbo a la agencia libre, el gerente general Brian Cashman quizá tenga que sumar varios lanzadores antes del inicio de la temporada de 2027.
Brent Headrick sigue bajo contrato tras una sólida campaña de 2026, pero las demás opciones del bullpen dentro de la organización también generan dudas.
Los Yankees podrían buscar refuerzos fuera de la organización, en particular si algunos de sus agentes libres firman con otros equipos.
Blackburn quizá no atraiga tanta atención como las grandes estrellas de Nueva York, pero su impresionante temporada lo convirtió en una pieza importante de los planes del equipo para esta temporada baja.
Aún no se sabe si los Yankees lograrán retenerlo, pero su interés indica que su etapa en el Bronx tal vez no haya terminado.

item.title: [Heavy.com] Yankees Make Feelings Clear on Breakout Pitcher After Dominant Season
item.dc:creator: Henry DiGennaro
item.description: The New York Yankees have some major decisions to make this offseason, and the organization appears interested in keeping one of its biggest surprises from the 2026 campaign. Veteran pitcher Paul Blackburn enjoyed a career resurgence in New York this season, emerging as a dependable bullpen weapon after struggling for much of the previous year. Now, the Yankees are showing strong interest in bringing him back. In a November 5 report for the New York Daily News, Yankees reporter Gary Phillips cit
item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees have some major decisions to make this offseason, and the organization appears interested in keeping one of its biggest surprises from the 2026 campaign.
Veteran pitcher Paul Blackburn enjoyed a career resurgence in New York this season, emerging as a dependable bullpen weapon after struggling for much of the previous year.
Now, the Yankees are showing strong interest in bringing him back.
In a November 5 report for the New York Daily News, Yankees reporter Gary Phillips cited sources indicating that the club has significant interest in re-signing Blackburn.
The development is noteworthy given earlier predictions that Blackburn could leave New York as a free agent.
No agreement has been announced, but the latest reporting suggests the Yankees would prefer not to lose one of their most productive relief pitchers.
Yankees Show Strong Interest in Paul Blackburn Reunion
Blackburn’s transformation has been one of New York’s more unexpected success stories.
The right-hander joined the Yankees in 2025 after being released by the crosstown rival Mets, but his initial results were underwhelming.
He finished that season with a 5.28 ERA across eight appearances for New York, leaving plenty of questions about his future.
However, Blackburn returned in 2026 and delivered the best statistical season of his major-league career.
The 32-year-old finished with a 7-3 record, 1.59 ERA, and 69 strikeouts across 85 innings, making 62 appearances, including two starts.
He also recorded a 1.08 WHIP while holding opposing hitters to a .195 batting average.
Those numbers helped Blackburn establish himself as a reliable late-inning option and gave the Yankees a valuable complement to closer David Bednar.
Blackburn’s effectiveness was especially impressive considering his previous career as a starting pitcher.
A 2022 All-Star with Oakland, he had primarily worked in starting rotations before transitioning into a bullpen role later in his career.
While his strikeout totals were relatively modest, Blackburn demonstrated an ability to limit hits and prevent runs.
His 2026 performance has strengthened his case for another major-league contract, although New York must weigh whether those results are sustainable.
Blackburn’s 3.74 fielding independent pitching mark was considerably higher than his ERA, raising questions about whether he can sustain that level of success.
Even so, the Yankees have an obvious reason to want him back.
Yankees Face Major Bullpen Decisions in Free Agency
Blackburn isn’t the only familiar arm New York hopes to retain.
The Yankees have already extended a $23.15 million qualifying offer to David Bednar, who recorded 35 saves during the 2026 season.
Bednar has until November 17 to accept the one-year offer or continue pursuing a different contract.
New York also has decisions to make regarding several other free-agent relievers, including Tim Hill, Ryan Yarbrough, John Schreiber and Michael Fulmer.
Phillips’ reporting indicates the Yankees have some interest in retaining Hill and have checked in with Yarbrough as well.
However, bringing back familiar pitchers won’t necessarily solve every problem.
With numerous bullpen contributors entering free agency, general manager Brian Cashman could need to add several arms before the 2027 season begins.
Brent Headrick remains under contract following a strong 2026 campaign, but New York’s other internal bullpen options bring questions of their own.
The Yankees could look outside the organization for additional reinforcements, particularly if some of their free agents sign elsewhere.
Blackburn may not command the attention of New York’s biggest stars, but his impressive season has made him an important part of the club’s offseason plans.
Whether the Yankees can bring him back remains uncertain, but their interest suggests his time in the Bronx might not be over.

item.title: [Heavy.com] Yankees' Aaron Judge Announces Personal Family News After Historic Feat
item.dc:creator: Dibyendu Mondal

Judge debuted Aug. 13, 2016, against the Tampa Bay Rays at Yankee Stadium. He was 24. He is now 34 and a three-time American League MVP. The New York Yankees showed how much they need him. He did not play in the postseason due to injury. The offense missed him against the Tampa Bay Ray
item.content:encoded:
Aaron Judge has reached 10 years of Major League Baseball service time.
“This season, Aaron Judge officially notched 10 Years of Service Time — a feat less than 10% of players achieve in MLB history,” MLBPA wrote.
Judge debuted Aug. 13, 2016, against the Tampa Bay Rays at Yankee Stadium. He was 24. He is now 34 and a three-time American League MVP.
The New York Yankees showed how much they need him. He did not play in the postseason due to injury. The offense missed him against the Tampa Bay Rays.
Now that he has completed this historic feat, he shared more news.
Aaron Judge Announces Personal News
Judge recalled the night before his debut. It was his mother who played the most important role behind the scenes before his big day.
“I was at Dinosaur Bar-B-Que in Rochester, New York. We just finished a game playing in Rochester in Triple-A. I got my family there. So we’re just sitting there eating. And our manager at the time, Al Pedrique, comes up and says, ‘Hey, you better finish up this meal. You got to play right field in New York tomorrow.’”
Rochester sits in upstate New York, more than 300 miles from the Bronx. Judge said the news confused him at first.
“I was kind of like, ‘Skip, what are you talking about? We’re in New York right now. Of course I’m playing right field tomorrow.’ He’s like, ‘No, no, no, you’re playing in the Bronx. It was kind of a whirlwind.”
Alex Rodriguez played his final game as a Yankee Aug. 12. The team called up Judge and first baseman Tyler Austin. The trip to the Bronx came with a catch.
“They had a plane fly for me. Late that night, but my parents weren’t going to be able to get on it. So we just all drove from Rochester through the night.”
Judge slept on the back seat of that rental, rolled up. His mother, Patty, took charge of the drive.
“My mom’s like, ‘Hey, I got this. You guys relax and I’ll get us where we need to go.’”
Her offer let Judge rest before a day that changed his career. The overnight drive helped set up a debut Yankees fans still remember.
Patty and Wayne, both teachers, adopted Judge as an infant. The drive ended at a hotel. He woke up the next morning and reached the Bronx.
Judge started in right field and batted eighth against the Rays. Austin, also making his debut, batted seventh.
Andriese tried to float an 87 mph changeup past Judge, but he crushed it to center field, knocking a 446-foot home run.
Aaron Judge Makes Personal Admission on Wife Samantha & Family
Judge said the milestone made him think about sacrifice and he was never alone.
“I think about just the sacrifices my family’s made, my wife and my parents. And just different family members that have sacrificed their time and their energy. To help kind of push me to get here. And just doing what they can to just be in my corner.”
Judge met his wife, Samantha Bracksieck, at Linden High School in California. The couple married in December 2021 in Maui, Hawaii. They welcomed their daughter, Nora Rose, in January 2025.
“So you don’t do it alone. I could have never done this by myself,” Judge added.

item.title: [AhoraMismo.com] Ryan McMahon preocupa: los Yankees buscan otro tercera base
item.dc:creator: Ahoramismo Staff

New York adquirió a McMahon de los Colorado Rockies antes de la fecha límite de cambios de julio de 2025. item.content:encoded:
Los New York Yankees podrían buscar un refuerzo para la tercera base y dejar ir a Ryan McMahon.
New York adquirió a McMahon de los Colorado Rockies antes de la fecha límite de cambios de julio de 2025. Se esperaba que fuera la solución a largo plazo del equipo en la tercera base, pero ha tenido dificultades en el Bronx.
Con el inicio de la agencia libre, los Yankees podrían buscar un reemplazo para McMahon mediante un cambio o en el mercado de agentes libres.
Una señal preocupante para el futuro de Ryan McMahon con los Yankees
Los Yankees llegan a la temporada baja con varias incógnitas, sobre todo en la tercera base.
McMahon no ha rendido a la ofensiva y los Yankees podrían buscarle un reemplazo. Aunque destaca a la defensiva, su bate ha sido un problema. Por eso, Jack Curry, reportero de los Yankees para YES Network, reveló que el equipo considera la tercera base una posición que necesita reforzar.
“La organización de los Yankees respeta mucho a Ryan McMahon, pero considera que necesita reforzar la tercera base, según Jack Curry”.
El nombre de McMahon ha aparecido en rumores de cambio, pues New York podría dejarlo ir. Si el equipo encuentra un mejor tercera base, ya sea en la agencia libre o mediante un cambio, la decepcionante etapa de McMahon en el Bronx probablemente terminaría.
McMahon entra en el último año de su contrato de seis años y 70 millones de dólares, con 16 millones de dólares por cobrar en 2027, así que no debería ser difícil dejarlo ir.
El pelotero de 31 años bateó para .213, con 11 jonrones y 41 carreras impulsadas en su primera temporada completa con los Yankees. Ha sido seleccionado una vez al Juego de Estrellas.
New York se enfoca en la temporada baja
Los Yankees volvieron a decepcionar con una eliminación temprana en los playoffs y podrían apostar por movimientos audaces esta temporada baja.
Aunque los Yankees no ganan una Serie Mundial desde 2009, su dueño, Hal Steinbrenner, no cree que la próxima temporada sea de ganar el título o fracasar.
“No, para nada”, respondió Steinbrenner. “Eso es, sin duda, lo que esperamos. Esa es nuestra misión. Ese es nuestro objetivo. Sí, este año no lo cumplimos, pero siempre es nuestro objetivo. Por eso dedicamos tanto esfuerzo y tantos recursos a la plantilla cada temporada baja: para formar un equipo capaz de lograrlo. Y sin duda creo que teníamos ese equipo este año. Simplemente, las cosas no salieron”.
Los Yankees aún no han hecho movimientos esta temporada baja, pero es probable que busquen reforzar la ofensiva y el cuerpo de lanzadores.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees could look to upgrade at third base and move on from Ryan McMahon.
New York acquired McMahon from the Colorado Rockies before the trade deadline in July 2025. He was supposed to be the team’s long-term answer at third base, but he’s struggled in the Bronx.
With free agency beginning, the Yankees could look to replace McMahon, either by trade or free agency.
Ryan McMahon Handed Concerning Take on Yankees Future
The Yankees have some question marks going into the offseason, especially at third base.
McMahon has struggled to produce, and the Yankees could look to replace him. Although he is a stellar defender, his bat has been an issue. So, Yankees reporter Jack Curry of YES Network revealed that third base is considered an area of need.
“The Yankee organization has a great deal of respect for Ryan McMahon but see third base as an area of need, per Jack Curry.”
McMahon’s name has come up in trade rumors, as New York could look to move on from him. If New York can find a better third baseman, whether that’s in free agency or a trade, McMahon’s disappointing tenure in the Bronx would likely be over.
McMahon enters the final year of his six-year, $70 million deal, with $16 million due in 2027, so it shouldn’t be hard to move on from him.
The 31-year-old hit .213 with 11 home runs and 41 RBIs in his first full season with the Yankees. He’s a one-time All-Star.
New York Focused on Offseason
The Yankees had another early playoff disappointment and could look to make some bold moves this offseason.
Although the Yankees haven’t won since 2009, owner Hal Steinbrenner doesn’t think this upcoming year is World Series or bust.
“No, not at all,” Steinbrenner replied. “That’s absolutely what we expect. That is our mission. That is our goal. Yes, we failed at the goal this year, but that is always our goal, which is why we put so much effort and resources into the roster every offseason to field a team that can accomplish that. And I certainly believe we had that team this year. It just didn’t pan out.”
The Yankees have yet to make a move this offseason, but New York will likely look to add some offense and pitching.

item.title: [New York Daily News] Yankees need to think bigger than reunions when addressing their bullpen

item.content:encoded:
The Yankees took the first step in addressing a bullpen that needs attention this offseason when they extended the qualifying offer to David Bednar on Monday.
Of course, the righty remains a free agent and has until 4 p.m. on Nov. 17 to accept or reject the one-year, $23.15 million offer. There is always the possibility that he pursues a multi-year deal, whether it be with the Yankees or another team, in a market that is thin on fellow closers.
Bednar is one of several free agent relievers who spent time with the Yankees in 2026, and he’s not the only one that the club could retain. Sources told the Daily News that there’s strong interest in re-signing Paul Blackburn, a bullpen breakout in 2026, and some interest in bringing back Tim Hill, who struggled this past season but has largely been effective for the Yankees since 2024. Another source added that the club has checked in on Ryan Yarbrough, a swingman who mostly worked in long relief this year.
The Yankees’ other in-house free agent relievers are John Schreiber and Michael Fulmer, two pitchers who were acquired after the team failed to get bullpen help before the 2026 trade deadline.
Bednar and Blackburn are two backend relievers worth pursuing reunions with, and some of the other names could be serviceable depth pieces in specific roles. But the Yankees also need to think bigger when it comes to their bullpen, even if Bednar and/or Blackburn come back.
At this point, Brent Headrick, another surprise standout who made 81 appearances in 2026, is the only sure thing under contract. Beyond that, the Yankees have a collection of relievers who look like Quadruple-A arms, are prospects, and/or are coming off injury. That includes Fernando Cruz, who mostly pitched well this season but is a non-tender candidate due to a partial tear of his UCL, and Carlos Lagrange, a flamethrowing farmhand whose big league arrival was delayed by a shoulder sprain.
If the Yankees want to build a dominant bullpen for 2027, they’re going to have to bring in some external options. They should also be willing to snap their streak of not committing big money to free agent relievers, which dates back to 2019.
That applies to Bednar, but could also relate to someone like Adrian Morejon, who has been an elite setup man for the Padres the last three years. The Yankees were interested in trading for the lefty over the summer and could try again for him this winter, but there’s been some rumors that Morejon wants to start. He was also extended the qualifying offer by San Diego, attaching draft pick compensation to him if he signs elsewhere.
As for other top free agent relievers, Raisel Iglesias is the only established alternative to Bednar for closer-needy clubs. Meanwhile, longtime Dodgers lefty Alex Vesia, battle tested in the postseason, could be a good fit for the Yankees. The club has also expressed interest in newly-minted World Series champ JoJo Romero, another lefty, in the past.
A few other free agents could make sense for the Yankees, and there’s also the trade market. That’s how they’ve added bigger names to their bullpen in the recent past — that includes Bednar, Devin Williams and Camilo Doval — but those last two didn’t work out in the Bronx.
Whatever path the Yankees take, they need to add some serious weapons — and new faces — as they rebuild a bullpen that saw six players hit the open market this week.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Yankees Have Ideal Free-Agent Fix for Catching Problem Without Giving Up on Austin Wells

item.content:encoded:
While the New York Yankees have multiple holes to fill on the roster, they shouldn't overlook this pressing need.
In the first half of the 2026 season, the Yankees' catching room was a disaster. Austin Wells suddenly cratered into one of the worst qualified hitters in baseball, while J.C. Escarra and Ali Sanchez did nothing to pick up the slack. Despite this, New York failed to bring in another backstop at the trade deadline and was forced to rely on a duo of Wells and Sanchez.
Fortunately, Wells enjoyed a much better second half (.787 OPS) to renew the Yankees' confidence in him. However, Sanchez remained a liability both at and behind the plate, forcing the Bronx Bombers to use Wells nearly exclusively down the stretch and into the postseason.
Wells' improved play and Sanchez's continued ineffectiveness revealed the true weakness of the Yankees' catching room: inadequate depth. Without a capable backstop to either share the starting job with Wells or back him up, the unit becomes significantly more of a liability in case Wells doesn't perform. Nobody expected the 27-year-old to be as bad as he was in the first half, yet having no depth behind him allowed that disastrous scenario to play out.
With this in mind, the Yankees need to pair Wells with a better catcher during the winter. The good news is they can find a perfect fit on the open market—at a reasonable price to boot.
Carson Kelly is the perfect catcher to complement Austin Wells
On October 30, veteran catcher Carson Kelly opted out of the $7.5 million mutual option he had with the Chicago Cubs, which officially makes him a free agent. Kelly spent his past two seasons with the Cubs and posted 5.5 bWAR with a .736 OPS alongside solid defense.
The 32-year-old was Chicago's starting catcher in both 2025 and 2026, but his age and batting splits make him more suitable as part of a catching tandem. In that regard, no other catcher on the market would be a better partner to Wells than Kelly.
Arguably the biggest factor behind Wells' offensive struggles was his inability to hit left-handed pitching. In 99 plate appearances, Wells hit a woeful .122/.192/.244 against southpaws. Against righties, his .209/.326/.365 slash line in 289 plate appearances is closer to league-average production.
In his career, Wells has a .578 OPS against lefties and a .727 OPS against righties. When taking his strong defense into account, getting just average production from Wells makes his contributions a net positive, and that production usually comes against right-handed pitching.
And when a lefty is on the mound, there aren't too many catchers more dangerous than Kelly. In 2026, he hit .298/.375/.496 over 136 plate appearances against southpaws, as opposed to a .239/.318/.320 slash line in 289 plate appearances versus righties. In his 11-year career, Kelly is a .267/.353/.469 hitter against lefties, which is well-above average production.
In terms of defense, Wells grades out as a better defender but Kelly is no slouch either. He won 69% of his ABS challenges in 2026, while Wells had a 63% success rate.
When looking at the catching market in free agency, Ryan Jeffers of the Minnesota Twins is the most coveted option; the Yankees were also frequently linked to him at the trade deadline. But Jeffers would be more inclined to sign with a team in need of a starting catcher, and New York has too much faith in Wells to make him a backup.
In contrast to Jeffers, who would likely want a long-term deal with a high AAV, Kelly could be signed at a very reasonable short- term rate. A two-year, $20 million contract would be a noticeable raise from his previous deal with the Cubs (two years, $11.5 million), yet that should be within the Yankees' budget.
The Yankees should be far from the only team interested in Kelly, as his skillset and market value make him a low-risk signing with a reasonably high reward. But Kelly is the specific catcher the Bronx Bombers are looking for, that being a right-handed catcher who can cover for Wells offensively and keep him fresh over the course of a season. While there are other areas for the Yankees to address, signing Kelly shouldn't prevent them from making other necessary moves, which is all the more reason to make him a priority target in free agency.
Joe Najarian is a writer for Yankees On SI, having previously covered the Yankees both for SI and additional sites since 2023. He also served as Deputy Editor for the Yankees, Mets and Orioles On SI sites, and additionally contributes to Athlon Sports and Men’s Journal covering Major League Baseball and other trending sports news. Joe is a graduate of Rutgers University in 2022, earning a bachelor’s degree in Journalism and Media Studies.
Follow JoeNajarian

item.content:encoded:
As the saying goes, "When Jack Curry speaks, Yankees fans listen," and that much was the case on Wednesday night during an episode of "Yankees Hot Stove" on the YES Network. Curry had some offseason updates for fans as the Bombers navigate these weeks prior to the inevitable lockout.
Where to start? We can get the general news out of the way, and that's Curry saying he expects the Yankees to be "active on all fronts" leading up to Dec. 1. That sounds like a "no duh" situation, but if you remember the month prior to the 2021 lockout, the Yankees did nothing meaningful. Brian Cashman acquired TJ Rumfield from the Phillies and traded Tyler Wade to the Angels, then stood there while a number of contenders ate the Yankees' lunch.
Curry relaying this news is certainly more encouraging than silence, but we'll believe it when we see it. The Yankees famously do not move fast at the start of the offseason and do not get aggressive when they're under the gun with time.
Cody Bellinger could move to center field for Yankees in 2027
And now for the frustrating developments. Curry said it's believed Gold Glove left fielder Cody Bellinger could move to center field next year, which suggests a number of things. The first of which is that they do not believe in Spencer Jones as a legitimate CF option.
The second is that they might be serious about pursuing a corner outfielder who can help upgrade the offense. That could be Randy Arozarena, Seiya Suzuki or Ian Happ. Our rebuttal? Bellinger is the best defensive left fielder in the game. Keep him there or else you lose tremendous value. None of Arozarena, Suzuki or Happ would move the needle much for the New York, and Arozarena and Suzuki will cost significant money and a draft pick since the qualifying offer is attached to them.
Once again, the Yankees roster remains a mess. They're constantly moving players around when it feels like there's little need to do so.
Yankees rumors suggest Ryan McMahon could be on the way out this offseason
Lastly, perhaps the funniest update of all from Curry, involved Ryan McMahon. The veteran third baseman has been terrible during his 1.5 years in New York, registering a 1.1 WAR across 178 games accompanied by a .211/.289/.349 line and declining defense.
Curry said the Yankees organization "has a great deal of respect for McMahon, but see third base as an area of need." This alludes to the reality that the Yankees favor feelings/status over the correct decision making. There's no need to preface the fact third base is a black hole for New York with "well, don't forget, we respect Ryan!". He's barely played a full season's worth of games with the Yankees; it's not like he's been here for five years. His performance has directly harmed the roster and his contract is weighing down the payroll.
Trade McMahon, eat half of his salary, and bring in just about anybody else. That's probably the only sensible approach. And spare us the lip service. Of course McMahon is respected. He's a nice guy and definitely worked hard to contribute to the Yankees. It just didn't work out, and now they have to act on his $16 million salary for 2027.

item.content:encoded:
Luis Garcia Jr. gives the Yankees a valuable bat and an uncomfortable winter question: where does that bat play if New York wants both him and Ben Rice in the lineup?
The Yankees acquired Garcia from Washington in August for four pitchers, according to MLB’s transaction record. He arrived with 23 home runs for the Nationals and, as The Associated Press reported, another year of team control. That makes him more than a short-term rental.
A Yankees infield decision with consequences
Garcia moved to first base with Washington after years at second. The ability to play both spots offers options, but New York should not simply assume his old position remains his best defensive fit. An offseason plan built around second base needs a real assessment of his range and consistency there.
Keeping Garcia at first makes the defensive assignment more straightforward. The cost is that Rice, another left-handed hitter, would need time at designated hitter or elsewhere. Rotating the two can preserve both bats, but it also uses a DH spot that could help the Yankees manage their other regulars.
The second-base alternative might make the lineup easier to construct. It could also create defensive problems that erase part of the offensive gain. New York should test Garcia there in camp instead of making the decision from a depth chart in November.
Keep the bat, verify the fit
Garcia homered in the Yankees’ Wild Card Series clincher, a reminder of the damage his swing can do in a meaningful game. One postseason moment does not settle his long-term position.
The club paid a meaningful acquisition cost and controls him for another season. My choice would be to keep Garcia in the everyday picture, evaluate him at second and leave room for first-base starts if the defense does not hold up.
More about:New York Yankees

item.content:encoded:
He joins Toronto's Dylan Cease and Cleveland's Parker Messick for the honor. The winner will be announced on November 11. This news comes as no shock to Yankees fans. Schlittler dominated the league this year. He led all starters with a 1.95 ERA. That mark trails only Spud Chandler and Ron Guidry in franchise history. It is a rare feat for a pitcher in pinstripes.
The manager saw this coming long before the vote. Aaron Boone called Schlittler an MVP candidate back in September. "He might be the MVP, too," the manager said in mid-September, according to New York Daily News. Schlittler finished with 239 strikeouts and 14 wins. He posted a 6.2 fWAR, not the highest in the league. Yet he did not get enough MVP votes. Bobby Witt Jr. and Yordan Alvarez finished ahead of him. Their fWAR numbers were higher, but Schlittler's pitching was elite. The gap between the pitcher and the hitters was too wide for voters.
A Historic Season for the Yankees
This season ranks among the best pitching years in team history. The league lead in FIP was shared by Cease and Schlittler at 2.56. He allowed just 129 hits in 193.2 innings. His opponent on-base percentage sat at .244. These numbers show total control over the game. If he wins, he becomes the seventh Yankees pitcher to take the trophy. He would join Bob Turley, Whitey Ford, and Roger Clemens. That is a very strong company to keep.
The team celebrated the news on social media. The official post read: "Congratulations Cam Schlittler on being named a 2026 AL Cy Young finalist 🔥", according to Heavy.com. Fans agreed with the praise. One supporter said, "He definitely deserves it! I will be surprised if he doesn't win." Another noted that his performance has been impressive all year. The hype is real, but the vote count is what matters.
What the League Says
Other players have weighed in on the race too. Knicks star Josh Hart made his pick early. "Schlitty is the Cy Young winner, hands down," Hart said in a June 19 social media post, according to MLB.com. Schlittler replied to the compliment with grace. "Josh is a great guy," Schlittler said. "I met him in the playoffs when they were on their way to a championship, and he came to the stadium after they won. I wish those guys the best. Hopefully they can do it again next year."
The race is tight, but the stats favor the Yankees pitcher. He already took home the MLB Players Association award for the league's top pitcher. That honor shows his peers respect his work. The Cy Young voting results will be revealed next week. The results will be revealed on MLB Network. No other Yankee placed top three in any major BBWAA honor besides Schlittler. No Bombers were nominated for MVP or Manager of the Year. This makes the Cy Young spot even more special.
The Final Stretch
Yankees fans will watch November 11 closely. The gap between Schlittler and the MVP finalists was small in WAR, but the voting rules favor hitters. Austin Wells, the Yankees catcher, felt the pitcher deserved a shot. "I think he should definitely get votes, so why not give it to him? He's been the MVP of our team, for sure," Wells said. He added, "I'm not a voter, but I don't see why [Schlittler] couldn't make a case for it."
The season is over, but the awards season just started. Schlittler has done his part. He put up numbers that will be hard to beat. Now he waits for the writers to decide. If he wins, the Yankees add another chapter to their pitching legacy. If he falls short, the 1.95 ERA still stands as a historic mark.

item.content:encoded:
Yankees predicted to finally land $46 million platoon partner for Austin Wells originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The New York Yankees have needed a right-handed-hitting catcher for over a year.
They began last season with Austin Wells and J.C. Escarra, two lefties, as their catching tandem.
Eventually, Escarra was sent to the minors, and Ali Sanchez took over as the club's backup catcher.
But Sanchez provided little on offense, and the Yankees could use more of a threat against left-handers. Wells had a .192 on-base percentage with a .436 OPS in 90 at-bats against lefties last season.
You don't need me to tell you those are poor numbers, and someone like Ryan Jeffers would help tremendously. Bleacher Report's Tim Kelly predicts the Yankees will sign Jeffers to a three-year, $46 million contract.
"The Yankees make sense for Jeffers, as Austin Wells had a meager .436 OPS against left-handed pitching this past season.
"Jeffers could be the 1A catcher in New York, with Wells serving as the 1B. Jeffers could also take some at-bats at DH," Kelly wrote.
Overall, Jeffers hit .256/.353/.461 with 14 home runs and a 127 OPS+ in 92 games with the Minnesota Twins last season.
The 29-year-old's defense behind the plate is not strong, but the Yankees can make some adjustments where they see fit.
"With minus-eight defensive runs saved and a minus-20 fielding run value in his career, Jeffers is a below-average catcher. He's also not a workhorse, with 720.1 frames in 2024 being the most Jeffers has ever caught in a season. Adding in the qualifying offer, some teams just won't be interested in him, even if they need a catcher," Kelly added.
Regardless of his defensive struggles, that shouldn't discourage the Yankees from showing interest.
They need an upgrade badly, and they don't want to miss out on other catchers because they spent too much time deciding how they felt about Jeffers.

item.title: [ｄメニューニュース] MLB 巨人・松井秀喜監督のヤンキース時代の同僚、マーク・テシェイラ氏がテキサス州下院選で初当選（SANSPO）｜ｄメニューニュース
item.description: 米中間選挙が3日（日本時間4日）投開票され、大リーグ（MLB）のヤンキースなどで活躍し、巨人の松井秀喜監督（52）のチームメートでもあったマーク・テシェイラ氏（46）が、テキサス州第21区の下院議員選挙に共和党から立候補し、初当選を果たした。 テシェイラ氏は、共和党現職のチップ・ロイ議員の後継として出馬。3月の党内予備選を61％超の得票率で勝ち上がると、本選でも元科学者で民主党新人のクリスティン・フック氏を約54％の得票率で破った。 当選確実を受け、テシェイラ氏はX（旧ツイッター）に「（議員としての）仕事に取りかかることを楽しみにしている。すべての皆さんのために、そしてこの偉大な国の未来のために祈り続けます」と声明を投稿。選挙戦では国境警備の強化や急進的なリベラル思想教育の終結を掲げており、ドナルド・トランプ大統領への協力の意思を鮮明にしている。 テシェイラ氏は2001年のドラフト全体5位でレンジャーズ入り。ブレーブス、エンゼルスを経て2009年からヤンキースに所属し、本塁打と打点の2冠に輝いて松井監督とともにワールドシリーズ制覇を成し遂げた。14年間の現役生活でオールスター戦に3度選
item.content:encoded:
米中間選挙が3日（日本時間4日）投開票され、大リーグ（MLB）のヤンキースなどで活躍し、巨人の松井秀喜監督（52）のチームメートでもあったマーク・テシェイラ氏（46）が、テキサス州第21区の下院議員選挙に共和党から立候補し、初当選を果たした。
テシェイラ氏は、共和党現職のチップ・ロイ議員の後継として出馬。3月の党内予備選を61％超の得票率で勝ち上がると、本選でも元科学者で民主党新人のクリスティン・フック氏を約54％の得票率で破った。
当選確実を受け、テシェイラ氏はX（旧ツイッター）に「（議員としての）仕事に取りかかることを楽しみにしている。すべての皆さんのために、そしてこの偉大な国の未来のために祈り続けます」と声明を投稿。選挙戦では国境警備の強化や急進的なリベラル思想教育の終結を掲げており、ドナルド・トランプ大統領への協力の意思を鮮明にしている。
テシェイラ氏は2001年のドラフト全体5位でレンジャーズ入り。ブレーブス、エンゼルスを経て2009年からヤンキースに所属し、本塁打と打点の2冠に輝いて松井監督とともにワールドシリーズ制覇を成し遂げた。14年間の現役生活でオールスター戦に3度選出され、ゴールドグラブ賞を5度受賞。2021年にテキサス州へ移住していた。

item.content:encoded:
Los Yankees presentaron una oferta calificada a David Bednar, pero no a Jazz Chisholm Jr., en dos decisiones que empiezan a definir su invierno. El mecanismo permite retener a un agente libre por una temporada a un salario establecido o recibir compensación si rechaza y firma con otra organización. Para Nueva York, afecta tanto al plantel inmediato como al talento que podrá incorporar después.
La prioridad deportiva detrás de Bednar resulta clara: terminó 2026 con 35 salvamentos y efectividad de 2.47. Su continuidad resolvería el puesto de cerrador en un bullpen que también tiene como agentes libres a Paul Blackburn, Tim Hill, Ryan Yarbrough, Michael Fulmer y John Schreiber. Perderlo añadiría otra necesidad a una reconstrucción que ya exige varios movimientos.
- LEER MÁS: Yankees 2027: los cambios de liderazgo que plantea Jorge Posada
- LEER MÁS: ¡Los White Sox fichan talento de los campeones Brewers para 2027!
Cómo afectan las ofertas calificadas al plantel de los Yankees
Si Bednar acepta, regresaría para 2027 por un año y US$23,15 millones. Eso daría certeza sobre quién lanzará la novena entrada, pero también comprometería una cantidad importante del presupuesto en un solo relevista. La oferta representa una decisión real de inversión: el club debe estar preparado para asumir ese salario si el jugador elige quedarse.
Si la rechaza y firma un contrato de Grandes Ligas con otro equipo antes del siguiente draft, los Yankees recibirían, con las reglas vigentes, una selección después de la cuarta ronda del draft de 2027, debido a su condición de pagadores del impuesto de balance competitivo. Esa compensación aporta una oportunidad de sumar talento futuro, pero no resuelve el reemplazo del cerrador para la próxima temporada.
Ver esta publicación en Instagram
Con Chisholm, Nueva York evitó quedar comprometido con ese salario si hubiera aceptado la oferta, a cambio de perder la posibilidad de compensación por su salida. El segunda base bateó .231, con 19 jonrones y 41 robos, en 2026. Anthony Volpe, José Caballero y Luis García Jr. aparecen entre las alternativas internas para la posición, aunque también sigue abierta la posibilidad de negociar un regreso de Jazz.
El mecanismo también encarece las incorporaciones. Por su condición fiscal, si los Yankees contratan a un agente libre de otra organización que haya rechazado una oferta calificada, perderían sus selecciones disponibles segunda y quinta más altas, además de US$1 millón de su bolsa de bonos internacionales. Por eso, al comparar refuerzos deben valorar el salario y las oportunidades de captar prospectos que sacrificarían.
Suscríbete al Newsletter de Unanimo y recibe gratis las últimas noticias. Dale click aquí
Cuándo decide Bednar y qué cambia con Trent Grisham
Bednar tiene hasta el martes 17 de noviembre, a las 4:00 p. m. ET, para aceptar o rechazar. Durante ese plazo puede explorar el mercado y negociar con los Yankees. Rechazar la oferta tampoco impediría acordar después un contrato de varios años con Nueva York: esa decisión mantiene abierta su agencia libre y no equivale a una despedida.
Trent Grisham representa una situación distinta: aceptó la oferta del invierno anterior para jugar en 2026 y no puede recibir otra, porque cada pelotero solo es elegible una vez en su carrera. Ahora vuelve al mercado sin esa compensación asociada. Su situación deja al jardín central entre las posiciones por resolver, junto con la segunda base y el bullpen, mientras los Yankees deciden cuánto invertir para conservar piezas y cuánto destinar a reemplazarlas.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Brewers manager Pat Murphy says he called Yankees GM Brian Cashman to 'explain' profane comment after World Series

item.content:encoded:
Milwaukee Brewers manager Pat Murphy appears to have one thing he regrets after a World Series-winning October.
The baseball veteran drew significant attention following the Brewers' five-game win in the 2026 Fall Classic after a camera caught him receiving the game-ending ball from first baseman Jake Bauers. Murphy embraced Bauers, the club's most notable pending free agent, and then said the following:
"You're going to be a rich f***er. Just remember when you're on that horses*** Yankees team and you guys are all playing for yourself, just remember this is the way we used to do it."
Bauers laughed off the comment and said "You ain't getting rid of me that easy," but Yankees fans were less amused.
Murphy addressed the matter during an appearance on the New York Post's "The Show" podcast published Tuesday and said that he called Yankees general manager Brian Cashman after finding out his moment with Bauers had reached social media, calling it a hot mic moment:
"I called Brian Cashman right away when I heard it got out … I heard the next morning, we're at the parade and everybody was talking about it. I was like, 'What? How did they hear that?' You know, hot mic. I'm like, 'Ah, whatever.' So I picked up the phone and called Brian right away and had a good conversation. The best I could, I tried to explain that I wasn't talking about the 2026 Yankees.
"He's just such a good guy, man. He's just a levelheaded — he's been through so much. I wish I had his demeanor and his way of handling things. I felt horribly if I slandered the Yankees because I was just referring to them as this iconic machine."
It's perhaps worth noting this wasn't really a hot mic moment, which implies Murphy didn't know he was being recorded. A person would have clearly been holding up a camera or phone to document an interesting moment, a player handing his manager a baseball with enormous meaning to both of them. Cameras and media members were all around them.
As for the exact meaning of Murphy's comment, the manager said Bauer's approaching payday had become a running joke between them, and that he only meant the Yankees in sort of abstract way.
"We had a little thing going. After every celebration, I'd shake his hand, I'd say, 'You rich so-and-so.' You're going to leave us, we're not going to be able to pay you. You're going to leave us and you're going to forget how you did things, how you were using the opposite field, taking your walks, all the things that made you great. I would just give him this rhetoric every time, 'You'll forget all about us.'
"I didn't mean to say these Yankees, like the 2026 or whatever Yankees are selfish. I was just referring to the teams that have a lot of high-paid, long-contract players. Sometimes it's harder to get all those guys together to play together. I use the Yankees because I knew Jake was with them before."
It remains to be seen if the non-Cashman members of the organization accept that explanation as well, but it's also hardly the most important thing for both the team and players right now.
Murphy is in his third season as Brewers manager and is overwhelmingly favored to take home a third straight NL Manager of the Year award next week.
Bauers has been playing in MLB since 2018, but this season was the first time playing more than 120 games in a single season. He led the club in homers with 26 during the regular season and won NLCS MVP.

item.title: [The Big Lead] Pat Murphy reveals ‘damage control’ conversation with Brian Cashman after viral Yankees comments
item.dc:creator: Lou Landers
item.description: Milwaukee Brewers manager Pat Murphy is addressing his viral comments about the New York Yankees during his team’s World Series celebration. Murphy revealed that he had a conversation with Yankees general manager Brian Cashman to smooth things over after his remarks about the organization sparked widespread attention around MLB. The comments came during Milwaukee’s championship celebration, when Murphy was caught on video speaking with first baseman Jake Bauers. What started as a private exchang
item.content:encoded:
Milwaukee Brewers manager Pat Murphy is addressing his viral comments about the New York Yankees during his team’s World Series celebration. Murphy revealed that he had a conversation with Yankees general manager Brian Cashman to smooth things over after his remarks about the organization sparked widespread attention around MLB.
The comments came during Milwaukee’s championship celebration, when Murphy was caught on video speaking with first baseman Jake Bauers. What started as a private exchange quickly became a major talking point around MLB.
Pat Murphy explains what he meant by Yankees comments
Murphy’s comments were directed toward Bauers, who previously played for the Yankees and is entering free agency. During their exchange, Murphy told Bauers to remember how the Brewers played together if he eventually joined the Yankees, referring to the New York organization as a team where players were playing for themselves.
The video quickly went viral, generating plenty of reactions from baseball fans and putting Murphy in an uncomfortable position.
However, Murphy has since explained that his remarks were part of a recurring private joke with Bauers. According to the manager, the conversation was not intended as a direct criticism of the 2026 Yankees. Instead, he was making a broader point about organizations with highly paid players on long-term contracts and the challenges of bringing everyone together.
Murphy acknowledged that he regretted making the comments publicly, particularly after realizing how widely the video had circulated.
Murphy reveals conversation with Brian Cashman
Following the attention surrounding his comments, Murphy reached out to Yankees general manager Brian Cashman to address the situation.
Murphy described the conversation as a good one and expressed respect for Cashman, calling him a good guy. However, he did not reveal the specific details of what was discussed between the two.
The conversation represents an effort to put the situation behind them after Murphy’s remarks became one of the biggest talking points from Milwaukee’s championship celebration.
Murphy’s comments were never intended to become a public controversy, but the video quickly made its way around the baseball world. Now, with the conversation with Cashman taking place, the Brewers manager appears ready to move forward from the situation.
For the Yankees, the comments provided another opportunity to become part of the baseball conversation during the offseason. For Murphy, the focus is now on explaining what he meant and putting the viral moment behind him.

item.content:encoded:
Jazz Chisholm Jr.'s tenure with the New York Yankees looks like it's officially over. The Yankees did not extend Chisholm a qualifying offer before Monday's 5 p.m. deadline, and now he is a free agent.
Chisholm played himself off the Yankees in 2026, struggling with a .231/.312/.399 slash line, .711 OPS, 19 home runs, 55 RBI, 41 stolen bases and an underwhelming 1.7 bWAR. He also made a crucial throwing error at second base in the ALDS and then doubled down by saying he would probably make the ill-advised play all over again if given the chance.
What was supposed to be an electric walk year with better playoff results ended up being a disaster for both parties. And it pretty much sums up how the Yankees do business.
Yankees GM Brian Cashman acquired Chisholm from the Miami Marlins at the 2024 trade deadline. Unfortunately for fans, this move wound up aligning with the majority of trades that Cashman makes, where the player is good, but not good enough.
More recently, Cashman landed first baseman Luis Garcia Jr. from the Washington Nationals at this past summer's deadline. Garcia had a 0.6 bWAR, .736 OPS and seven homers for the Yankees in 43 games. This is the latest example of a player being solid, but not enough to make the Yankees a World Series title winner.
At first, it appeared that the decision to bring in Chisholm was the right one. He agreed to shift over to third base and hit .273/.325/.500 with a .825 OPS, 11 homers and 23 RBI down the stretch in 2024.
Chisholm's best season with the Yankees came in 2025, where he posted a 30/30 campaign. In 130 games, Chisholm slashed .242/.332/.481 with a .813 OPS, 31 homers, 80 RBI, 31 stolen bases and a 4.1 bWAR. Even with that showing, his overall postseason numbers drag his regular season numbers down. Chisholm was just 16-for-88 (.182) in his 25 playoff games with the Bombers.
The addition of Chisholm didn't help the Yankees get over the hump, and by the time his team control expired he had seemingly overstayed his welcome in the Bronx. Chisholm's antics, such as taking his position with a lollipop in his mouth, was one of several incidents that rubbed the Yankees and others the wrong way.
Does that type of acquisition sound familiar? Aroldis Chapman. Lance Lynn. Aaron Hicks. James Paxton. JA Happ. Sonny Gray. Anthony Rizzo. Joey Gallo. Rougned Odor. Jameson Taillon. Corey Kluber. Josh Donaldson. Isiah Kiner-Falefa. Harrison Bader. Alex Verdugo. Marcus Stroman. Ryan McMahon. Devin Williams. Camilo Doval. All players who possessed a level of talent that provided some promise that could be acquired for the right price in Cashman's eyes ... but none sufficient enough to push the Yankees closer to a championship. That's a long list of misses that have plagued the Yankees since 2018.
Chisholm now hits the free agent market, where he will likely have to accept a one-year prove-it deal in order to rebuild his value before retesting free agency next year. At this point, it's safe to say that his time with the Yankees is over. The writing appears to be on the wall after the Yankees didn't extend a qualifying offer to him on Monday. The Chisholm trade will go down as on-brand for Cashman's underwhelming and risk-averse acquisitions.

item.title: [MARCA] Yankees' Jazz Chisholm split feels inevitable after $23 million decision
item.dc:creator: Adriano Boin
