item.content:encoded:
- New York Yankees. Aaron Judge surprises fans with appearance at New York City Marathon to support his wife
- Milwaukee Brewers. Cigarettes before the game? The Brewers’ strange ritual on their way to the World Series
The New York Yankees appear increasingly likely to move on from Jazz Chisholm Jr. after deciding against extending him a qualifying offer ahead of the 2027 season.
New York made a different decision regarding closer David Bednar, offering him a one-year, $23.15 million qualifying offer on Monday.
The move gives the Yankees an opportunity to retain an important bullpen piece, but Chisholm's omission suggests the organization isn't convinced he's worth a similar commitment.
Chisholm entered 2026 with considerable expectations after recording 31 home runs and 31 stolen bases the previous season. However, his production declined considerably, finishing the campaign with a .231 batting average, 19 homers and a .711 OPS across 137 games.
Although he stole a career-high 41 bases, his inconsistent offensive performances made it difficult for the Yankees to justify keeping him at a potentially expensive price.
The two-time All-Star has demonstrated plenty of talent throughout his career, but consistency has remained a concern. His occasional defensive lapses and questionable on-field decisions have also attracted criticism, creating additional uncertainty about his long-term future in New York.
Chisholm hasn't hidden his desire to remain with the Yankees. Following the team's postseason disappointment, he expressed his affection for the organization, making it clear that leaving the Bronx wasn't his preferred outcome.
Nevertheless, the Yankees have other priorities, and questions surrounding his consistency and postseason performances could make a reunion difficult.
Yankees could pursue Teruaki Sato as Chisholm's replacement
Former MLB executive Jim Bowden has also questioned whether Chisholm is the type of player the Yankees should build around, suggesting the organization would benefit from younger, more dependable personalities.
Bowden pointed to the additional distractions surrounding certain players, arguing that teams already face enough challenges without having to manage unnecessary clubhouse concerns.
His comments suggest Chisholm's situation could involve more than simply evaluating his offensive production.
Meanwhile, New York has another potential infield problem involving Ryan McMahon. The third baseman hasn't delivered the offensive improvement the Yankees hoped for after acquiring him, finishing 2026 with a .213 average, seven home runs and a .636 OPS.
Consequently, Japanese superstar Teruaki Sato could become an attractive offseason target.
The Hanshin Tigers standout is coming off an extraordinary 2026 campaign, winning the Central League Triple Crown with a .306 batting average, 39 home runs and 106 RBIs. 
His impressive offensive production has made him one of the most intriguing international players potentially available to MLB clubs.
Sato's left-handed power could be particularly appealing at Yankee Stadium, where the short right-field porch offers an inviting target for left-handed hitters. Adding another dangerous power hitter would also take some pressure off Aaron Judge.
However, his defensive position remains something to consider. Although primarily a third baseman in Japan, he has experience playing in the outfield and could eventually move elsewhere in the infield.
Landing Sato wouldn't automatically solve every problem facing the Yankees, but his offensive potential would represent a significant addition.
If Chisholm ultimately departs, pursuing Sato could help reshape New York's lineup and provide another powerful weapon alongside Judge.

That decision does not prevent a reunion; it changes the compensation picture if he signs elsewhere. The Yankees made a calculated bet Chisholm fell fr
item.content:encoded:
Jazz Chisholm Jr. can talk to other clubs without the draft-pick penalty attached to a qualifying offer. For the Yankees, that makes the second-base market more complicated, not necessarily closed.
New York chose not to extend Chisholm the $23.15 million offer by Monday's deadline, while offering it to David Bednar, MLB.com's Bryan Hoch reported. That decision does not prevent a reunion; it changes the compensation picture if he signs elsewhere.
The Yankees made a calculated bet
Chisholm fell from 31 home runs and an .813 OPS in 2025 to 19 homers and a .711 OPS in 2026. He still stole a career-high 41 bases. Both sides of that record belong in the conversation: the bat regressed, but his speed did not disappear.
The Yankees also sat him for two postseason games, including the elimination game. Chisholm later said he wished manager Aaron Boone had communicated the decision directly. A contract is a separate question, but the club should not pretend the relationship needs no attention.
I would keep talking at a price that reflects the down year instead of assuming the no-offer decision means he has to leave. Anthony Volpe, Jose Caballero and Luis Garcia Jr. give New York other infield choices; each comes with a different offensive projection and role.
What the market can change
The alternative is to commit those resources elsewhere and give the internal group a genuine competition. That saves the club from paying for a rebound that may not arrive, but it also risks losing an established power-speed combination for no qualifying-offer compensation.
Chisholm's offers and the Yankees' actual budget are not public. The decision removed one obstacle for a new club; it did not choose his next team.

item.content:encoded:
NEW YORK -- The Yankees can picture a bullpen that would again be anchored by right-handed closer David Bednar, who received a qualifying offer from the club ahead of Monday’s 5 p.m. ET deadline: a one-year deal valued at $23.15 million.
Bednar, 32, has until Nov. 17 to accept or reject the offer, which is calculated annually based upon the average salary of Major League Baseball’s 125 highest-paid players.
The qualifying offer does not prevent the Yankees from negotiating a multi-year contract with Bednar, who was 7-3 with 35 saves and a 2.47 ERA in 64 appearances this past season, setting career highs in wins and innings pitched (69 1/3).
Acquired from the Pirates in July 2025, Bednar has compiled a 2.39 ERA and 45 saves over his 1 1/2 seasons in New York. This past season, Bednar’s 35 saves tied for third in the AL, while his 89.7 save percentage ranked sixth in the AL (min. 10 save opportunities).
“I think it's just trying to do a task, finish a task, and just take it one at a time,” Bednar said during the postseason. “When I'm down there, I'm ready for whenever the phone rings in whatever situation, whatever the team needs me to do. So whenever that may be, I'm always prepared.”
The Yankees’ bullpen was a strength this past season, when Bombers relievers posted a 3.13 ERA that ranked second in the Majors, and they were fourth in WHIP (1.22).
Bednar was one of six Yankees relievers to become free agents on Thursday, along with Paul Blackburn, Michael Fulmer, Tim Hill, John Schreiber and Ryan Yarbrough.
Chisholm presented a more difficult case for the organization to mull. Coming off a 31-homer, 31-steal season in 2025, Chisholm entered a contract year with big aspirations, publicly setting his sights upon joining baseball’s exclusive 50-50 club.
Instead, Chisholm experienced a downturn at the plate, batting .231/.312/.399 with 19 homers and 55 RBIs in 137 games. He stole 41 bases, a career high, but he finished with a .711 OPS, more than a hundred points lower than his .813 OPS in 2025.
Chisholm was left out of the lineup for two postseason games, including the season-ending Game 3 of the American League Division Series against the Rays.
That night, Chisholm expressed frustration about his communication with manager Aaron Boone, saying he didn’t learn of the benching until he arrived at Yankee Stadium.
“I’d always prefer a conversation, so I would at least know what I’m walking into,” Chisholm said then.
Anthony Volpe drew the start at second base instead. The Yankees’ internal choices at second base include Volpe, José Caballero and Luis García Jr.
“This is where I want to be,” he said. “I love it as a Yankee. I grew up as a Yankee fan, being from the Bahamas, watching Derek Jeter and those guys every day. It was a great time being a Yankee. I loved my time as a Yankee.
“I had great years with the Yankees; I had an All-Star year, had a Silver Slugger year. Who doesn’t want to stay with a team that you’ve had such great times with and great years with? To see it maybe end here sucks, but it’s part of the business.”
Last year, the Yankees extended a qualifying offer to outfielder Trent Grisham, who accepted the $22.025 million pact. Grisham, first baseman Paul Goldschmidt and infielder/outfielder Amed Rosario are also currently free agents.

item.content:encoded:
The Yankees have put a $23.15 million decision in David Bednar’s hands. Their next move should be to negotiate a multiyear deal without treating the qualifying offer as a completed reunion.
New York extended the one-year offer to its closer before Monday’s deadline, MLB.com’s Bryan Hoch reported. Bednar has until November 17 to accept or reject it. The two sides can still work out a longer contract.
The Yankees need more than one bullpen answer
Bednar posted a 2.47 ERA and converted 35 of 39 save chances in 2026. He also threw 69 1/3 innings, a career high, giving the club a reliable late-inning option across a long season.
That matters because the bullpen is not a one-player project. Paul Blackburn, Tim Hill, Michael Fulmer, John Schreiber and Ryan Yarbrough also reached free agency. Re-signing the closer would solve the ninth inning, not fill all the innings before it.
The Yankees should make Bednar a serious multiyear offer with a limit that leaves room for at least one more established reliever. The qualifying offer is useful protection: if he accepts, they retain him for one year; if he rejects and signs elsewhere, compensation rules can apply.
One year has a real cost
The alternative is to let the market set his price and pivot if the years climb too high. A one-year commitment avoids a longer contract risk, but $23.15 million is a substantial raise from his $9 million 2026 salary.
There is no public agreement on a longer deal, and neither his decision nor another team’s willingness to pay is known. The Yankees have created an option, not finished their bullpen.

item.content:encoded:
Pretty much anyone who talks about José Caballero will at some point say the phrase "You love him when he's on your team, hate him when he's on the other team." He's probably never going to be an All-Star, but he's a guy who can play a bunch of positions on defense, can use his speed when he's on base, and will generally just be a pest to the other team.
This year, with Anthony Volpe missing the start of the season after undergoing surgery, Caballero got some extended run as a starter. As we continue our look back through the see, let's look back at how he did.
Grade: C+
2026 Statistics: 136 games, 456 plate appearances, .231/.290/.365, 14 home runs, 51 RBI, 6.4 BB%, 24.3 K%, 83 wRC+, 2 OAA, 1.3 fWAR, 2.2 rWAR
2027 Contract Status: First year arbitration eligible
With Volpe on the shelf to start 2026, Caballero was the Yankees' Opening Day starter at shortstop and appeared in all but one of the team's first 42 games, also starting at short in most of them. He made a little bit of history by becoming the first player to use the Automated Ball-Strike System to challenge a pitch. He was unsuccessful on one in the fourth inning of Opening Day.
Following a slow start, Caballero hit a hot stretch around the beginning of May. Through May 11th, he had a .720 OPS, which is perfectly good for a glove first utility man. The argument was out there that he should retain the shortstop position once Volpe came back, and the team did send their former top prospect to the minors once his rehab assignment ended. However on May 10th, Caballero suffered a finger injury while diving back into first base on a pickoff attempt, leading to Volpe's recall. The injury only kept him out close to the minimum amount of time, as he returned on May 22nd.
Upon his return back to the majors, Caballero did mostly return to his previous role as a utility-ish guy. He still ended up appearing in 136 games in the majors, so he wasn't fully benched, but he never locked back up that full-time shortstop position. That wasn't because Volpe returned with a vengeance, it's just that Caballero never quite took the ball and ran with it. Upon his return on May 22nd on, Caballero put up just a .623 OPS.
Caballero did finish his 2026 with career highs in home runs and RBI, but nothing about his offensive year was that notable otherwise. While it would've been extremely unrealistic to expect him to match the 133 wRC+ he put up upon getting traded to the Yankees in 2025, the team would've been hoping for better than 83. In the end, he and Volpe both got overtaken by George Lombard Jr., the new top prospect who got a late season call-up and got the majority of shortstop reps down the stretch.
One weird thing about Caballero's 2026 was his battles with umpires through the medium of the pitch clock. In his role as a pest, Caballero had been deliberately waiting until the last possible second to acknowledge the pitcher, which had been at the eight-second mark on the pitch clock. After some kerfuffles with opposing pitchers, MLB came down on Caballero, giving him a pitch clock violation for waiting to look up. It still seems dumb to me to essentially change a rule mid-season like that, considering that Caballero did seem to be following how the rule was written, but hey, I don't get paid the big bucks to make decisions like that.
As for next season, I would expect Caballero to still be around in a utility role. He's set to be arbitration eligible this season, but it's hard to imagine he would get remotely enough for the Yankees to want to get rid of him. He's still versatile enough and fast enough on the basepaths to be useful to have around.
See more of the Yankees Roster Report Card series here.

item.content:encoded:
New York politician AOC aka Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez had some harsh words for Aaron Boone when asked about the New York Yankees. As a Yankees fan, Ocasio-Cortez was asked about the current state of the Yankees franchise. Another failed MLB season ending without the World Series have fans questioning General Manager Brian Cashman and manager Boone.
AOC joked that Boone must have something on the Yankees to remain manager, when interviewed by Maddy of WAG Talk and Enjoy Basketball at a Buffalo Bills watch part:
“I don’t know what Aaron Boone has on the front office but we gotta shake things up if we’re going to have different results. I’m sorry to hear what Jorge Posada had to say about feeling unwelcomed (at Yankees events.)
We have to bring in the legacy of the team and return to that standard of excellence. I want to see that culture back. I want to see those standards back. I want to see Jeter, Posada, Mariano. I want to see everyone back. That’s what we want. Let’s get back there.”
The Yankees confirmed both Cashman and Boone will be back for the 2027 season, with Cashman even getting an extension. Yankees superstar Aaron Judge basically called out the front office at the end of the season press conference to get more help.
AOC Supported Jorge Posada Vs Yankees
A recent interview with legendary Yankees catcher Jorge Posada revealed his unfiltered thoughts about the franchise. Fans and media have started to question why former players like Posada, Derek Jeter, and Mariano Rivera rarely appear for the team or help out behind the scenes.
The “core four” and other recent legends, like Bernie Williams and CC Sabathia, could provide mentorship due to their pride of being all-time great Yankees. Posada was the first to reveal he feels unwelcome by the franchise after a rift towards the end of his playing career.
Sabathia criticized the Yankees culture and believes that the franchise has declined from his time due to that issue. AOC and many other Yankees fans feel vindicated by these players to question Boone and Cashman. The Yankees will go into next season with World Series hopes to end the 17-year drought.
Aaron Boone’s Job On The Line Next Season
One noteworthy difference for Boone entering next season is that it will be the final year of his contract. A failed season would result in Boone’s contract expiring, and the Yankees looking for a new manager to start the next era.
Fans have questioned whether Boone deserved this chance, but the Yankees have relied on the excuse of injuries. Judge and Giancarlo Stanton both missed most of the season to drastically change the offense with multiple platoon hitters splitting various positions.
The Yankees can no longer trust Stanton to be an everyday hitter, especially with the aging Judge and Ben Rice needing some time at the DH spot. Boone will have a lot of difficult variables in his way as he tries to secure more years as manager. AOC represents many other fans who will be calling for Boone’s job if the Yankees struggle early.

item.content:encoded:
La política neoyorquina Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, conocida como AOC, criticó con dureza a Aaron Boone cuando le preguntaron por los New York Yankees. Como aficionada del equipo, Ocasio-Cortez habló sobre la situación actual de la franquicia. Tras otra temporada fallida sin llegar a la Serie Mundial, los aficionados cuestionan al gerente general Brian Cashman y al mánager Boone.
AOC bromeó con que Boone debe saber algo comprometedor sobre los Yankees para seguir como mánager. Lo dijo en una entrevista con Maddy de WAG Talk y Enjoy Basketball durante una reunión para ver un partido de los Buffalo Bills:
“No sé qué tiene Aaron Boone contra los directivos, pero tenemos que cambiar las cosas si queremos resultados distintos. Me entristeció escuchar a Jorge Posada decir que no se siente bienvenido en los eventos de los Yankees.
Tenemos que recuperar el legado del equipo y volver a ese nivel de excelencia. Quiero que regrese esa cultura. Quiero que vuelvan esos estándares. Quiero ver de nuevo a Jeter, Posada y Mariano. Quiero que regresen todos. Eso es lo que queremos. Volvamos a eso”.
Los Yankees confirmaron que Cashman y Boone seguirán en la temporada 2027; Cashman incluso recibió una extensión de contrato. En la conferencia de prensa de cierre de temporada, la estrella de los Yankees Aaron Judge prácticamente exigió a los directivos más refuerzos.
AOC respaldó a Jorge Posada en su disputa con los Yankees
En una entrevista reciente, el legendario receptor de los Yankees Jorge Posada habló sin filtros sobre la franquicia. Aficionados y medios comenzaron a preguntarse por qué exjugadores como Posada, Derek Jeter y Mariano Rivera rara vez participan en actividades del equipo o colaboran tras bambalinas.
Los “cuatro del núcleo” y otras leyendas recientes, como Bernie Williams y CC Sabathia, podrían orientar a los jugadores gracias al orgullo que sienten por estar entre los más grandes de la historia de los Yankees. Posada fue el primero en revelar que no se siente bienvenido en la franquicia tras un distanciamiento hacia el final de su carrera como jugador.
Sabathia criticó la cultura de los Yankees y cree que, por ese motivo, la franquicia ha venido a menos desde que él jugaba allí. Las declaraciones de estos exjugadores refuerzan los cuestionamientos de AOC y muchos otros aficionados de los Yankees hacia Boone y Cashman. Los Yankees afrontarán la próxima temporada con la esperanza de ganar la Serie Mundial y poner fin a una sequía de 17 años.
Aaron Boone se jugará el puesto la próxima temporada
Hay una diferencia importante para Boone de cara a la próxima temporada: será el último año de su contrato. Si el equipo vuelve a fracasar, su contrato vencerá y los Yankees buscarán un nuevo mánager para iniciar otra etapa.
Los aficionados han cuestionado si Boone merecía esta oportunidad, pero los Yankees han recurrido a las lesiones como excusa. Judge y Giancarlo Stanton se perdieron gran parte de la temporada, lo que alteró drásticamente la ofensiva y obligó a varios bateadores a repartirse distintas posiciones según los enfrentamientos.
Los Yankees ya no pueden contar con Stanton como bateador de todos los días, sobre todo porque Judge, que también suma años, y Ben Rice necesitan turnos como bateadores designados. Boone tendrá que superar muchos obstáculos para conseguir más años como mánager. AOC representa a muchos otros aficionados que pedirán la salida de Boone si los Yankees arrancan mal.

item.content:encoded:
Yankees extend David Bednar $23.15 million qualifying offer appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The New York Yankees got some stability in the bullpen this year from David Bednar. In his first full season with the Yankees, he converted 35 save opportunities for the team. Still, Bednar is a free agent, and the Yankees need to make a decision on the pitcher.
The Yankees have made their first step towards retaining the pitcher, according to Bob Nightengale of USA Today.
The Yankees have submitted a $23.15 million qualifying offer to Bednar. He is one of eight players who received such an offer. Players have a choice to accept the offer, remaining with their current club at the offered salary, or they may reject the offer and become an unrestricted free agent. If the player decides to opt for free agency, then his former team will receive draft compensation.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
Bednar was a 35th-round draft pick by the San Diego Padres in the 2016 MLB Draft. He was brought to the major league roster in September 2019, making his MLB debut that same day. He would go on to make 13 appearances with the Padres that year, with a 6.55 ERA. The next year, he spent most of the season in the minors, but did make four appearances with the Padres.
In January 2021, he was traded to the Pittsburgh Pirates and would go on to have his first full season in the majors. Bednar became an All-Star with the Pirates. He was selected to the All-Star team in 2022 and 2023, while leading the league in saves in 2023. At the 2025 MLB trade deadline, the Pirates traded Bednar to the Yankees.
This past year, he appeared in 64 games for the Yankees, going 7-3 with a 2.47 ERA. He also had 35 saves and just four blown saves for the team.

item.title: [MLB.com] Schlittler named AL Cy Young finalist on heels of dominant season
item.dc:creator: Bryan Hoch

Hart, whose Knicks delivered the franchise’s first NBA title in 53 years, knows a thing or two about championships. We
item.content:encoded:
NEW YORK -- The American League’s Cy Young Award race would still run for more than three months, but at least one observer had already seen enough to make a call.
“Schlitty is the Cy Young winner, hands down,” the Knicks’ Josh Hart said in a June 19 social media post, shortly after the Yankees’ Cam Schlittler dominated the Reds with a 13-strikeout performance at Yankee Stadium.
Hart, whose Knicks delivered the franchise’s first NBA title in 53 years, knows a thing or two about championships. We’ll soon find out if his expertise extends to the Baseball Writers’ Association of America voting.
“Josh is a great guy,” Schlittler said. “I met him in the playoffs when they were on their way to a championship, and he came to the stadium after they won. I wish those guys the best. Hopefully they can do it again next year.”
And by then, Schlittler might have some hardware of his own to showcase.
Schlittler was named Monday as one of the BBWAA’s finalists for the AL Cy Young Award, along with Dylan Cease of the Blue Jays and Parker Messick of the Guardians. The winner will be announced Nov. 11 on MLB Network.
In his first full Major League season, Schlittler went 14-6 with an AL-best 1.95 ERA, pacing the AL in pitching WAR (6.2, per FanGraphs) and opponent on-base percentage (.244).
“He’s going to win the Cy Young,” manager Aaron Boone said. “I think he’s just continued to get better year in and year out. This is largely in line with who we saw down the stretch when he got called up last year.”
Schlittler struck out 239 batters against 49 walks and 129 hits allowed in 193 2/3 innings; those 239 K’s tied Jack Chesbro (1904) for the fourth most by a Yankees pitcher in a single season.
He permitted one run or fewer in a Major League-best 21 starts, and allowed three runs or fewer in 29 starts, tied for the most in the Majors. Since his debut in July 2025, Schlittler has led all Major League starters in ERA.
“There’s been a lot going on the last year,” Schlittler said. “I started the [2025] season in Double-A after I got my first little taste of Spring Training. They gave me an opportunity, and I just kind of ran with it.”
Feeding off hostile environments, Schlittler was especially dominant on the road, going 8-2 with a 1.16 ERA in 17 starts. He led all qualified Major Leaguers in road ERA, strikeouts (129), opponent batting average (.153), opponent OPS (.456) and WHIP (0.74).
“I’ve played with Cam since Double-A, so it’s not shocking to me what he’s doing now,” said rookie shortstop George Lombard Jr. “I’ve always seen the competitiveness and fire in him, and obviously the nasty stuff.”
“I think sometimes you just naturally lock in a little bit more,” Schlittler said. “The goal is to find a way to treat every game the same.”
Now, with a possible Cy Young Award on the horizon, the real question ahead is this -- what will Schlittler do for an encore?
“He’s been the best pitcher in the league,” Boone said. “When you have that going all year at the top of your rotation, that’s massive. And that’s what he’s been.”

item.content:encoded:
Cam Schlittler was officially announced as a finalist for the American League Cy Young Award on Monday night as MLB Network revealed the finalists for all BBWAA end-of-year awards. Schlittler was the lone Yankee to finish in the top three for any of the honors.
The 25-year-old ace, who led the AL with a 1.95 ERA and 6.2 FanGraphs WAR, was named by the BBWAA alongside Dylan Cease of the Blue Jays and Parker Messick of the Guardians. The winner, along with the recipients of each league's MVP, Rookie of the Year, Manager of the Year, and the newly-created Reliever of the Year awards, will be announced next week on MLB Network. The Cy Young voting results in particular will be revealed on Wednesday, November 11th.
The NL Cy Young nominees are World Series champion Jacob Misiorowski of the Brewers, Atlanta's Chris Sale, and Phillies southpaw Cristopher Sánchez.
Seeing as 2026 was not a banner year for the Yankees' position players, no Bombers were nominated for MVP. Presumptive winner and Astros slugger Yordan Alvarez, Rays star Junior Caminero, and the Royals' Bobby Witt Jr. are up for the award on the AL side. There was some hope that Schlittler or slugger Ben Rice might have an outside shot at third, but no dice; they'll instead eye a top-10 finish.
Pete Crow-Armstrong of the Cubs is likely to receive his first career MVP—Shohei Ohtani is nominated in the NL for the third straight year, while Brice Turang of the World Champion Brewers is also on the podium. The only year since 2021 that Ohtani hasn't won an MVP is 2022, when Aaron Judge beat him out with 62 homers; this will almost surely be the second.
As for Rookie of the Year, New York was represented—albeit across town in Queens. Mets outfielder Carson Benge was nominated in the NL, along with JJ Wetherholt of the Cardinals and Sal Stewart of the Reds. The AL nominees are Messick, Tigers infielder Kevin McGonigle, and Red Sox starter Payton Tolle.
Unsprisingly, Aaron Boone was not given the nod as a Manager of the Year finalist, but two of his division rivals were. Kevin Cash, who led the Rays to the World Series, was nominated alongside interim-turned-full-time Red Sox skipper Chad Tracy and upstart White Sox manager Will Venable. Yankee icon Don Mattingly was nominated on the NL side for his interim work in Philadelphia. He is up for consideration alongside Braves first-year manager Walt Weiss and the Brewers' Pat Murphy (who is eyeing a MoY three-peat).
The Reliever of the Year finalists are unsurprisingly all closers: Bryan Baker, Cade Smith, and Louis Varland in the AL; and Jhoan Duran, Trevor Megill, and Mason Miller in the NL. Note that this a brand-new honor that the BBWAA decided to start giving out, and it is fully separate from the Mariano Rivera and Trevor Hoffman Reliever of the Year awards, which are given by MLB itself alongside the Hank Aaron Awards, the Edgar Martinez Awards, the Comeback Players of the Year, and the All-MLB Teams.

item.content:encoded:
El lanzador de los New York Yankees, Cam Schlittler, ya ganó el premio al Lanzador Más Destacado de la Liga Americana que otorga la Asociación de Jugadores de las Grandes Ligas por su desempeño en la temporada 2026 de la MLB.
Ahora podría recibir un premio aún más prestigioso: lo nombraron oficialmente finalista al Cy Young de la Liga Americana.
El lanzador de los New York Yankees Cam Schlittler, finalista al Cy Young de la Liga Americana
Schlittler figura entre los finalistas al Cy Young de la Liga Americana de 2026 junto a Parker Messick, de los Cleveland Guardians, y Dylan Cease, de los Toronto Blue Jays.
Los Yankees también celebraron la noticia en redes sociales con un mensaje de felicitación:
“¡Felicidades a Cam Schlittler por ser nombrado finalista al Cy Young de la Liga Americana de 2026! 🔥”, escribieron los Yankees en X, antes conocido como Twitter.
Los aficionados de los Yankees también reaccionaron a la noticia con mensajes de felicitación.
“¡Sin duda se lo merece! Me sorprendería que no ganara”, dijo un aficionado.
Otro aficionado comentó: “Esa intensidad es justo lo que se necesita para recibir votos al Cy Young de la Liga Americana. ¿Quién más ya está preparando las maletas para la ceremonia?”.
Este aficionado dijo: “El desempeño de Cam esta temporada ha sido impresionante. Da gusto ver que se lo reconozcan”.
Por último, otro aficionado comentó: “Sería una injusticia que no ganara. No hay nada que celebrar por ahora”.
Esta temporada, Schlittler terminó con marca de 14-6, efectividad de 1.95 y WHIP de 0.92, además de sumar 239 ponches.
Los Yankees eligieron a Cam Schlittler en 2022
Los Yankees seleccionaron a Schlittler en la séptima ronda del Draft de MLB de 2022 y poco después le dieron un contrato. Tras avanzar por las ligas menores, ganó el premio al Lanzador del Año de la Liga del Atlántico Sur en 2024 y debutó en la MLB en julio de 2025, después de una lesión de Clarke Schmidt.
Schlittler tuvo marca de 4-3, efectividad de 2.96 y 84 ponches en 73 entradas durante su temporada de novato. También brilló en la postemporada: lanzó ocho entradas sin permitir carreras y ponchó a 12 bateadores ante sus rivales, los Boston Red Sox, en la Serie de Comodines de la Liga Americana.
En 2026 se consolidó como abridor: registró efectividad de 1.95 y 239 ponches, y lideró la MLB en efectividad. Además, permitió una carrera o menos en 22 aperturas. Abrió la postemporada con otra actuación dominante ante los Red Sox: ponchó a 10 en 6⅓ entradas sin permitir carreras.

item.dc:creator: Jason Fray; Unknown
item.description: Jazz Chisholm Jr. is a very polarizing, mercurial player. There are times where he resembles a dominant player — the one that was an All-Star in 2025 for the New York Yankees. However, there are moments when his in-game blunders can crop up and become detrimental to his team. At 28 years of age, Chisholm projects as one of the more gifted players set to hit free agency. The hit tool is certainly there still as is his range as a fielder (ranking in the 98th percentile in range, per Baseball Savan
item.content:encoded:
Jazz Chisholm Jr. is a very polarizing, mercurial player.
There are times where he resembles a dominant player — the one that was an All-Star in 2025 for the New York Yankees. However, there are moments when his in-game blunders can crop up and become detrimental to his team.
At 28 years of age, Chisholm projects as one of the more gifted players set to hit free agency. The hit tool is certainly there still as is his range as a fielder (ranking in the 98th percentile in range, per Baseball Savant).
Could the San Diego Padres potentially be a fit for the Bahamian star? According to Jim Bowden of The Athletic, it's certainly a possibility.
Padres Linked to Jazz Chisholm Jr. in Free Agency
Bowden listed the Padres, Athletics, and Los Angeles Angels as possible fits. The former executive believes Chisholm Jr. could receive a six-year deal worth approximately $128 million.
"Chisholm wasn’t shy in spring training about declaring his goal of hitting 50 homers with 50 steals, numbers he hoped would earn a free-agent contract worth $350 million. Well, he hit 19 homers with 41 steals while hitting just .231, and his dream of a huge long-term contract has gone by the wayside, at least for this offseason. He’ll probably either have to sign a short-term, prove-it deal or a long-term contract with a non-contending team with opt-out clauses," Bowden wrote.
"It feels like the Yankees are going to move on from him even though he’d prefer to stay. He finished the year in the 23rd percentile in batting run value, but in the 85th percentile for defensive run value and 96th percentile in baserunning value."
Chisholm has terrific positional versatility. An outfielder earlier in his career, he can play second and third base at a decent level. This would appear to fit with San Diego's philosophy where it wants to collect as much talent as possible with worrying about positional fit later.
When looking at the Padres as a whole, Manny Machado certainly isn't going anywhere at third base. Chisholm may end up being a strong candidate for the second base spot currently occupied by Jake Cronenworth, who is approaching his 33rd birthday and showing real signs of a decline.
With so much money already tied up to several middle infielders on the roster, coupled with the starting rotation being very ambiguous at the moment, Chisholm might not be a must-get player for the Padres.
However, if he's willing to take a shorter-term deal, or even one with early opt-outs, the likelihood of him ending up in San Diego may increase.
Sign up for our free newsletter and follow us on Facebook and X/Twitter for the latest news.
Jason Fray is a Los Angeles native with 10+ years of professional experience in the sports media world. A graduate of UCLA, Fray has written previously for the likes of Bleacher Report, FOX Sports, Saturday Down South, MSN, Sports Illustrated and Newsweek.

item.content:encoded:
*This content was translated by AI.View Original
Goose Gossage (75), the "legendary closer" of the New York Yankees, unleashed ruthless criticism at Jazz Chisholm Jr. (28) for playing with a lollipop in his mouth during a game.
In an interview with U.S. local media outlet 'NJ.com' on the 1st (Korean time), Gossage pointed out the lax discipline and attitude of the recent Yankees roster. While stating, "The Yankees have many excellent young players. I personally like Ben Rice, Spencer Jones, and Aaron Judge," he criticized, "But the problem is that no one is teaching them how to behave."
The arrow immediately pointed at Chisholm Jr. He had sparked fierce controversy by taking the field for defense with a lollipop in his mouth during a game on June 23. Gossage said, "However, there are players who act like fools. I saw Chisholm Jr. playing with a candy in his mouth," adding sharply, "He is a disgrace to the Yankees. He is nothing but a clown."
Immediately after the incident, Chisholm Jr. displayed a confident attitude, saying, "Baseball is a game for kids, and I am just enjoying it." Yankees manager Aaron Boone, who is usually known for shielding his players, also brushed off the situation with a joking reaction the next day when Chisholm Jr. performed well, stating, "Our 'Candy Boy' did it." Fans also dismissed it as a simple fiasco after one home run.
However, now that the season has ended, even the manager's perspective has completely shifted. Yankees manager Aaron Boone, who recently secured his retention for the 2027 season, revealed an unusually cold attitude regarding the incident at an official press conference, stating, "It was unpleasant and naturally annoying. It was one of the things I tried to correct on the spot." The manager no longer serves as a shield for Chisholm Jr., who has lost the trust of the locker room due to poor performance, postseason errors, and irresponsible behavior.
His performance also hit rock bottom. Although Chisholm Jr. had guaranteed "50 home runs and 50 stolen bases" in the offseason ahead of acquiring free agent (FA) eligibility, he left a dismal record far below expectations with a regular season batting average of .231 and an OPS (on-base percentage plus slugging percentage) of .711. Injuries compounded the issue, squashing any chance of a rebound, and in Game 2 of the American League Division Series (ALDS), faced with a cliffhanger situation, he committed a critical throwing error and maintained an irresponsible attitude, provoking public outrage among fans. Immediately after being eliminated from the postseason, he also lost the trust of his teammates, meaning even the manager no longer serves as a shield for him.
Ultimately, the partnership between the Yankees and Chisholm Jr. appears to be coming to an end. According to Mark Feinendegen, a reporter for the official Major League Baseball website MLB.com, it is known that the Yankees are highly likely not to present Chisholm Jr. with a qualifying offer (QO). This year's QO amount was set at 23.15 million dollars (approximately 31.1 billion won), and eligible players must decide whether to accept by the 18th, but the Yankees are hesitating even about continuing their partnership for just one more year.
Gossage's rough outburst, as a "legendary closer" who led the Yankees' golden era from 1978 to 1983, recording 310 saves in 1,002 career games and being inducted into the Hall of Fame, starkly points out the current state of Chisholm Jr., who had become intoxicated with superficial style while forgetting the weight of the Yankees uniform, a symbol of Major League tradition and discipline.

item.content:encoded:
Este contenido ha sido traducido por IA.Ver original
Goose Gossage (75), el "cierrador legendario" de los New York Yankees, lanzó duras críticas sin piedad hacia Jazz Chisholm Jr. (28), quien jugó con un caramelo de palo en la boca durante un partido.
Gossage señaló en una entrevista con el medio local estadounidense 'NJ.com' el 1 (hora coreana) la disciplina y la actitud relajadas del plantel de los Yankees recientemente. Gossage afirmó: "Hay muchos jóvenes talentosos en los Yankees. Me gustan personalmente Ben Rice, Spencer Jones y Aaron Judge", pero añadió: "El problema es que no hay nadie que les enseñe cómo deben comportarse".
La crítica se dirigió directamente a Chisholm Jr. Este había causado una fuerte controversia al salir a defender con un caramelo de palo en la boca durante el partido del 23 de junio pasado. Gossage declaró: "Sin embargo, hay jugadores que actúan como tontos. Vi a Chisholm Jr. jugar con un caramelo en la boca", y continuó: "Es una vergüenza para los Yankees. No es más que un payaso".
Inmediatamente después de dicha escena, Chisholm Jr. mostró una actitud desafiante al decir: "El béisbol es un juego para niños y yo solo me divierto". El manager de los Yankees, Aaron Boone, conocido por su costumbre de proteger a sus jugadores, también minimizó la situación con una respuesta burlona al día siguiente cuando Chisholm Jr. tuvo un gran desempeño: "Nuestro 'chico del caramelo' lo logró", y los aficionados también lo consideraron un simple incidente tras un jonrón.
Sin embargo, ahora que ha terminado la temporada, incluso la perspectiva del manager ha cambiado por completo. Aaron Boone, quien recientemente aseguró su continuidad para la temporada 2027, mostró una actitud inusualmente fría en una conferencia de prensa oficial al referirse a aquel incidente: "Fue desagradable y, por supuesto, me molestó. Fue una de las cosas que intenté corregir en el momento". El manager ya no actúa como escudo para Chisholm Jr., quien ha perdido la confianza del vestuario debido a su bajo rendimiento, errores en los playoffs y actitud irresponsable.
Su rendimiento también tocó fondo. Aunque Chisholm Jr. había asegurado un "50 jonrones - 50 bases robadas" en la pretemporada antes de obtener la elegibilidad de FA (agente libre), dejó una hoja de servicios decepcionante, muy por debajo de las expectativas, con un promedio de bateo de .231 y un OPS (porcentaje de embasado + porcentaje de slugging) de .711 en la temporada regular. Además de perder oportunidades de recuperación debido a lesiones, cometió un error decisivo en el envío de la pelota en el segundo partido de la Serie Divisional de la Liga Americana (ALDS), disputada en una situación crítica, y mantuvo una actitud irresponsable, lo que provocó la indignación de los aficionados. Tras la eliminación en los playoffs de otoño, perdió incluso la confianza de sus compañeros de equipo, por lo que ni siquiera el manager pudo seguir protegiéndolo.
En definitiva, parece que la relación entre los Yankees y Chisholm Jr. llegará a su fin. Según el reportero Mark Feinberg del sitio web oficial de las Grandes Ligas, MLB.com, se sabe que es probable que los Yankees no ofrezcan una oferta calificada (QO) a Chisholm Jr. El monto de la QO para este año se fijó en 23,15 millones de dólares (aproximadamente 31,1 mil millones de wones), y el jugador debe decidir si la acepta o no hasta el día 18, pero los Yankees están dudando incluso de continuar juntos por un año más.
La dura reprimenda de Gossage, el "cierrador legendario" que fue inductado al Salón de la Fama tras liderar la era dorada de los Yankees desde 1978 hasta 1983 y registrar 310 salvamentos en 1.002 partidos en su carrera, expone sin rodeos la situación actual de Chisholm Jr., quien se dejó llevar por las apariencias olvidando el peso del uniforme de los Yankees, símbolo de la tradición y la disciplina de las Grandes Ligas.

item.title: [شبكة تواصل الإخبارية] "Disgrace to the Yankees": 28YO Star Called a 'Clown' by MLB Legend Over His Inappropriate Mid-Game Actions
item.dc:creator: الكاتب Abdulrahman
item.description: Jazz Chisholm Jr. stepped onto the field with a lollipop in his mouth, and Goose Gossage saw a franchise losing its identity. From strict grooming standards to disciplined public conduct, wearing the pinstripes has traditionally demanded more than just baseball talent. But Chisholm Jr. has never been the kind of player to fit neatly into that mold. His unfiltered personality and flamboyant celebrations make him stand out, yet his bold promises haven’t always translated into results.Watch What’s
item.content:encoded:
Jazz Chisholm Jr. stepped onto the field with a lollipop in his mouth, and Goose Gossage saw a franchise losing its identity. From strict grooming standards to disciplined public conduct, wearing the pinstripes has traditionally demanded more than just baseball talent. But Chisholm Jr. has never been the kind of player to fit neatly into that mold. His unfiltered personality and flamboyant celebrations make him stand out, yet his bold promises haven’t always translated into results.Watch What’s Trending Now!Chisholm had promised to join Ohtani in the 50-50 club before 2026. Instead, he finished with 19 homers, and one moment with a lollipop became the season’s defining image. Per Gossage, that image may have crossed a line. It offered yet another reason to question whether Chisholm truly belongs in pinstripes.“I saw Jazz Chisholm playing with a lollipop. He’s a disgrace to the Yankees. He’s a clown,” Fireside Yankees quoted Goosage’s interview with nj.com.During a game against the Detroit Tigers back in June, the 28-year-old second baseman walked out in the top of the fifth inning with a green apple Blow Pop clearly visible in his mouth. However, Chisholm later explained that it was actually a timing mishap. Chisholm’s ritual was simple: Lollipops kept him locked in. He’d bite off the candy before stepping on the field. Just this time, the new lollipop didn’t crack in time. The television cameras quickly caught the moment.There were no repercussions, though. “That pisses me off,” Yankees manager Aaron Boone later reacted. “I didn’t know about it until after the game. So he and I talked about that, and that won’t be going on.”Per Goosage, that defined the current state of the Yankees. “You would not be a Yankee anymore. You would be gone that day, as soon as George saw it. He would be like, ‘Off the field. I don’t care where he goes. See you later,’” Goosage added about what could have happened back in the seventies.Rich “Goose” Gossage is a Baseball Hall of Fame relief pitcher and an iconic legend for the New York Yankees, where he anchored the bullpen during the team’s late-1970s and early-1980s glory years.Gossage signed with the Yankees in 1978 as a free agent, and recorded the final out for the team in Game 6 of the World Series against the Los Angeles Dodgers. That season, he led the AL in saves (27). He even won the AL Relief Man Award in 1978.The HoFer himself was a style icon, but within limits.He had an exaggerated Fu Manchu mustache that extended below his lip. To stay within the letter of the New York Yankees appearance policy, Gossage shaved the rest of his beard while keeping his signature oversized mustache, walking a fine line between the team’s appearance code and his own rebellious style. With all that, there was his dominance on the mound, his overpowering ~100 mph fastball, and fiery intensity. Gossage routinely pitched multiple innings to lock down games.Chisholm’s 30-homer 2025 season did earn him another chance with the Yankees. Whether that continues may depend on how Hal Steinbrenner defines a Yankee. It is attributed to how Hal is running the show differently from his dad, George.The defining catalyst for this conversation occurred in February 2025, when Hal Steinbrenner officially abolished the Yankees’ historic 49-year facial hair ban. It allowed members of the 40-man roster to grow well-groomed beards. The 1976 appearance policy, instituted by George Steinbrenner, required players to be clean-shaven. For decades, the Yankees gained a cult status with such a look. But with time, the team had to evolve, and Hal chose to focus on winning over everything.Yet the Yankees have been searching for a ring since 2009, and players like Chisholm have made the franchise’s legends wonder if they are in the right direction.Now, as we enter the offseason, it’s time to wait and see whether the Yankees pick Jazz Chisholm Jr. up from free agency.

item.content:encoded:
Jazz Chisholm Jr. has received plenty of heat from fans and the media this year. He underperformed in 2026, posting a below-average 97 OPS+, and many have gotten upset over some of his quotes and on-field antics.
One thing Chisholm did that caused him to receive plenty of discontent from Yankees fans was suck on a lollipop while playing second base. After the incident, manager Aaron Boone made it clear he wasn’t a fan.
“It just bothered me, and it was addressed,” Boone said. “I don’t think that should be a part of what we’re doing.”
Recently, the incident was brought up again by legendary Yankees pitcher Goose Gossage.
New York Yankees Hall of Famer Goose Gossage Rips Jazz Chisholm Jr.
NEW YORK – JULY 19: New York Yankees Hall of Famer Rich ‘Goose’ Gossage looks on during the teams 63rd Old Timers Day before the game against the Detroit Tigers on July 19, 2009 at Yankee Stadium in the Bronx borough of New York City. (Photo by Jim McIsaac/Getty Images)
“They’ve got some good kids. I love Ben Rice. I like Spencer Jones. I like Aaron Judge. It’s too bad they don’t have somebody telling them how to act,” Gossage said to NJ.com’s Randy Miller. “They have some guys who act like fools. I saw Jazz Chisholm playing with a lollipop. He’s a disgrace to the Yankees. He’s a clown.”
Gossage played for nine teams across 22 MLB seasons from 1972 to 1994. Gossage played for the Yankees for seven seasons (1978-83).
NEW YORK – JULY 17: Hall of Famer Rich Gossage looks on during the New York Yankees 64th Old-Timer’s Day before the MLB game against the Tampa Bay Rays on July 17, 2010 at Yankee Stadium in the Bronx borough of New York City. (Photo by Jim McIsaac/Getty Images)
With New York, Gossage made three All-Star teams and posted a 2.14 ERA with 512 strikeouts over 533 innings.
He is a nine-time All-Star, a World Series champion and a Hall of Famer.
Looking at Jazz Chisholm Jr.
NEW YORK, NEW YORK – SEPTEMBER 11: Jazz Chisholm Jr. #13 of the New York Yankees reacts during the eighth inning against the Detroit Tigers at Yankee Stadium on September 11, 2025, in the Bronx borough of New York City. Members of the New York Yankees were given permission by MLB to wear FDNY and NYPD hats tonight, honoring the fallen first responders of 9/11. (Photo by Ishika Samant/Getty Images)
Chisholm is a free agent.
The Yankees can extend Chisholm the qualifying offer, which is $23.15 million. Several reports have suggested the Yankees won’t give him the offer.
NEW YORK, NEW YORK – SEPTEMBER 11: Jazz Chisholm Jr. #13 of the New York Yankees reacts during the fourth inning against the Detroit Tigers at Yankee Stadium on September 11, 2025, in the Bronx borough of New York City. Members of the New York Yankees were given permission by MLB to wear FDNY and NYPD hats tonight, honoring the fallen first responders of 9/11. (Photo by Elsa/Getty Images)
Chisholm began his MLB career with the Miami Marlins in 2020.
Miami traded him to the Yankees during the 2024 season.
After joining the Yankees, Chisholm posted 7.3 bWAR and a 113 OPS+ with 61 home runs, 158 RBI and 90 stolen bases over 313 games.

item.title: [Yanks Go Yard] Anthony Volpe shouldn't be handed keys to Yankees 2B job, but he deserves more grace
item.dc:creator: Matthew Swigonski
item.description: It’s difficult to think of a player in baseball who had as wild of a 2026 season as Anthony Volpe. He began the year on the proverbial hot seat in the eyes of a large portion of the New York Yankees fan base. However, after being exiled to Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre in August to work on his game, he became an unlikely fan favorite when he debuted at second base during the Yankees’ late-season push. item.content:encoded:
It’s difficult to think of a player in baseball who had as wild of a 2026 season as Anthony Volpe. He began the year on the proverbial hot seat in the eyes of a large portion of the New York Yankees fan base. However, after being exiled to Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre in August to work on his game, he became an unlikely fan favorite when he debuted at second base during the Yankees’ late-season push.
For some, his limited time at the position was more than enough to justify penciling Volpe in as the Yankees’ full-time second basemen next season. Perhaps we should pump the brakes just a little bit on that. With multiple options worth exploring for the Yankees this offseason, Volpe shouldn't have locked down the job just yet.
That’s not to say that Volpe couldn’t handle second base in 2027. He appeared to be more than capable of handling the role moving forward. When Jazz Chisholm Jr. went down with a hand injury in September, the Yankees turned to a Volpe to fill in at second. Equipped with a revamped swing, the 25-year-old appeared to relish his second chance at making an impact in the Bronx, and it showed. In just 12 games at second base in the regular season, Volpe performed quite admirably on both sides of the ball.
We just can’t jump the gun here, though. By all accounts, Chisholm Jr. will likely be playing for another team next season. His future with the Yankees is still technically up in the air. General manager Brian Cashman could extend a qualifying option to Chisholm Jr. in the very near future. He could also pull off a trade for another established second baseman such as Xavier Edwards of the Miami Marlins.
Suffice to say, the Yankees have a number of potential routes that they can take to fill their need at second base. And Volpe getting a fair shot to earn the job will be one of the routes.
Anthony Volpe could have an exciting second act for the Yankees
Twelve regular season games at second base is just not enough playing time to really gauge how well Volpe would be able to transition to the position over the course of a full season. Even in Triple-A this past season, Volpe started just 19 games at second. He has the potential to be a very good defensive second baseman, but do the Yankees have the time to wait around for him to develop into that player? That's one big check in the con column for Volpe.
With his below average arm strength, his throws may actually play up at second base, even when turning a double play. Throughout his playing days at short, Volpe was guilty of short-hopping his fair share of throws to first. With less distance to make his throws, that problem could be solved. That's a major check in the pro column.
As a highly-regarded prospect in the New York Yankees’ minor league system, Volpe was thought to be the team’s future shortstop for at least the next decade. The team has always known that he has the talent. So when Isiah Kiner-Falefa began drawing the ire of Yankees fans for his questionable ability as a full-time shortstop, the organization turned to Volpe as their solution in 2023.
With +26 Defensive Runs Saved throughout his four-year career, Volpe is clearly gifted in the field. His Gold Glove in 2023 is proof of that. Despite that impressive ability to field the ball, Volpe has also been plagued by costly errors during his time with the Yankees. Whether it’s attributed to that lack of arm strength or just a classic case of the yips, Volpe fell victim to prolonged stretches of poor defense. That's another check in the con column.
If he produced at the plate, those stretches may have been overlooked. But with a career .661 OPS, Volpe simply failed to meet the lofty standards of a Yankees shortstop set by Derek Jeter. Like it or not, that’s who Yankees fans will usually compare incoming players to. Leaping throws or notable hustle plays from shortstops are almost always referred to as Jeter-esque.
Without the pressures of living up to that standard at short, perhaps Volpe begins to thrive more as a ball player? We already saw George Lombard Jr. deal with glimpses of that pressure when he faced his own defensive struggles this season. Volpe did look just a little more comfortable playing second base in 2026. Another check in the pro column.
Regardless of Volpe’s potential to handle second base for the Yankees, the team must exhaust all of their options at the position heading into 2027. Whether that’s looking at free agency or making a splashy trade, they can’t afford to settle for just good enough.

item.description: Yankees captain Aaron Judge makes his wife's marathon day even more special Aaron Judge is used to being the center of attention in New York. During the baseball season, the Yankees captain draws crowds with towering home runs, clutch hits and the kind of power that has made him one of Major League Baseball's biggest stars. item.content:encoded:
Yankees captain Aaron Judge makes his wife's marathon day even more special
Aaron Judge is used to being the center of attention in New York. During the baseball season, the Yankees captain draws crowds with towering home runs, clutch hits and the kind of power that has made him one of Major League Baseball's biggest stars. On Sunday, however, Judge was perfectly happy to let someone else take the spotlight. With the MLB offseason underway, the 6-foot-7 slugger showed up to cheer on his wife, Samantha, as she ran the New York City Marathon. And when she spotted her family along the course, the race briefly turned into a special family moment — with the couple's young daughter, Nora Rose, adding an especially sweet touch. Wearing sunglasses and a Yankees pullover, Judge was hard to miss among the spectators. His height alone made him stand out, but his role as a supportive husband and father made the moment more memorable than his unmistakable presence in the crowd.

item.title: [Yardbarker] Yankees’ Latest Trade Rumor Dumps Austin Wells in 4-Player Deal
item.dc:creator: Simeon Kotto
item.description: The New York Yankees enter this offseason with a familiar priority at catcher. Their lineup continues to lean left-handed, and the production behind the plate has lagged, even as the rest of the roster shows the pieces of a contender. That combination has kept the club linked to available backstops, and Shea Langeliers stands out as one of the cleaner fits on the trade market. The Athletics’ All-Star is under club control through 2028, offers proven right-handed power, and can slot near the top
item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees enter this offseason with a familiar priority at catcher. Their lineup continues to lean left-handed, and the production behind the plate has lagged, even as the rest of the roster shows the pieces of a contender.
That combination has kept the club linked to available backstops, and Shea Langeliers stands out as one of the cleaner fits on the trade market.
The Athletics’ All-Star is under club control through 2028, offers proven right-handed power, and can slot near the top of a Yankees order that needs more balance.
Christopher Kline of FanSided recently sketched a realistic package that would send Langeliers to the Bronx in exchange for Austin Wells plus pitching prospects Carlos Lagrange and Ben Hess.
From the Yankees’ side, the proposal centers on Wells because New York lacks a true top catching prospect to offer in his place. Wells has held the primary job in the Bronx since 2024 and remains a trusted game-caller and receiver.
His 2026 regular-season offense was a clear disappointment, yet he was one of the more productive Yankees in a short postseason, the kind of late-year spark that often fuels renewed belief heading into the next spring.
For New York, moving Wells would clear everyday at-bats for a hitter with a higher offensive ceiling while still leaving the club with a familiar defensive presence in the deal itself.
Langeliers would give the lineup a right-handed bat capable of driving the ball to all fields, something the current mix has lacked for stretches.
The two pitching prospects soften the cost for the Yankees: Lagrange brings electric stuff that has touched triple digits with a sharp sweeper, even if injuries have clouded his starter path, and Hess profiles as a durable arm with power stuff of his own.
Neither is viewed as untouchable in a deal that upgrades a position of need.
The trade would not solve every Yankees issue, but it would address the most obvious one with a player who has already produced at an All-Star level.
Wells’ defensive reputation and recent postseason showing make him a logical centerpiece for the Athletics, who need arms and a successor behind the plate.
For the Yankees, it is a chance to add impact offense without emptying the top of the farm system, a balance that has defined their more successful winter moves in recent years.
Whether the two clubs can close the gap remains to be seen, but the framework fits the needs on both sides.

item.title: [Heavy.com] Yankees' Aaron Judge Shows Up For Wife's Special Moment With Daughter
item.dc:creator: Billy Heyen
item.description: It’s the offseason for New York Yankees superstar Aaron Judge. On Sunday, that meant he got to switch into supportive fan mode for his wife in a special moment for her. The New York City Marathon was held on Sunday, and Judge was there in the crowd rooting on his wife, who was running. Aaron Judge Supports Wife at NYC Marathon Judge was rocking some sunglasses and a Yankees pullover as he stood behind the barrier when his wife Samantha ran by. Samantha took the chance to stop and see her family.
item.content:encoded:
It’s the offseason for New York Yankees superstar Aaron Judge.
On Sunday, that meant he got to switch into supportive fan mode for his wife in a special moment for her.
The New York City Marathon was held on Sunday, and Judge was there in the crowd rooting on his wife, who was running.
Aaron Judge Supports Wife at NYC Marathon
Judge was rocking some sunglasses and a Yankees pullover as he stood behind the barrier when his wife Samantha ran by.
Samantha took the chance to stop and see her family.
Judge wasn’t hard to miss in the crowd, of course. His 6-foot-7 height helped out here.
Aaron Judge supporting his wife at the NYC Marathon. That’s my captain https://t.co/wQiZVF80eg
— Taylor Ringold (@TaylorRingold) November 1, 2026
Samantha and Judge met in high school and both attended Fresno State together, too.
She’s got a degree in kinesiology and certainly knows a lot about the mechanics of athletics — and clearly, Samantha knows how to push herself to be her best, as well.
Running in a marathon, 26.2 miles, is one of the most impressive feats of will and endurance that there is.
Aaron and Samantha Judge’s Daughter
The couple had their first child in January 2025. She’s a girl, named Nora Rose Judge
The Yankees superstar appeared to hand their daughter to Samantha for her break during the marathon.
It’s actually impressive that Samantha even felt comfortable stopping. It can be hard to maintain running momentum over such a long distance after a stop, but she went for the break to spend time with those who were there to support her.
Judge appeared to turn into a proper fanboy and make sure to get a picture on his phone of his wife and daughter.
@TaylorRingold I can’t believe she stopped that long . I’ve run the marathon and other distance races and once I had my stride there’s no way I’m stopping for anyone or anything .
— Keane (@kranepool) November 1, 2026
One of the coolest parts of a marathon for most of the competitors is that they’re just racing against themselves and pushing themselves. They set goals, to be sure, but just completing the distance is a milestone moment in each of those runners’ lives.
For Samantha, she had the chance to run in front of her family, those that are closest to her heart. It had to be a special day for the whole Judge family.

item.content:encoded:
NUEVA YORK — Brian Cashman ha sobrevivido a otra eliminación en octubre. Los Yankees de Nueva York llegaron a un acuerdo para un nuevo contrato con su director general el 21 de octubre, dos semanas después de que los Rays de Tampa Bay los eliminaran por barrida en la Serie Divisional de la Liga Americana.
El acuerdo mantiene a Cashman al mando por trigésima temporada en 2027, lo que alarga el mandato más largo de un director general en la historia de la franquicia. El socio gerente general, Hal Steinbrenner, echó la culpa de la derrota en los playoffs a los jugadores, no a la directiva.
Desde entonces, exjugadores de los Yankees como Derek Jeter, Alex Rodríguez, Paul O’Neill y Jorge Posada han criticado públicamente la forma en que se gestiona el club. A dos de los asesores principales de Cashman, Brian Sabean y Omar Minaya, no se les renovará el contrato.
Ninguna de las críticas ha sido tan contundente como la que ha lanzado este fin de semana un miembro del Salón de la Fama.
Gossage apunta a los mandamás
Goose Gossage arremetió contra la dirección de los Yankees en una entrevista publicada el sábado en NJ.com, señalando específicamente a Cashman, Steinbrenner y al presidente del equipo, Randy Levine.
Gossage, de 75 años, fue una de las estrellas de los Yankees de 1978 a 1983 y fue el cerrador del equipo campeón de la Serie Mundial de 1978. Entró en el Salón de la Fama en 2008 y tiene una placa en el Monument Park.
Además, lleva una década siendo uno de los críticos más feroces de la directiva, y ha dirigido gran parte de sus críticas al enfoque analítico que ha defendido Cashman. Los Yankees te han mantenido alejado de los eventos del equipo desde 2018.
Gossage, que vive en Colorado Springs, Colorado, empezó hablando con los propietarios de la franquicia.
«Todo empieza por arriba. Un pescado muerto apesta desde la cabeza hacia abajo», dijo Gossage.
Dijo que hace poco vio a Levine en una entrevista en la tele con una foto del difunto George Steinbrenner de fondo. A Gossage le molestó esa imagen.
«Debería avergonzarse de estar ahí sentado con una foto del señor Steinbrenner», dijo Gossage.
A continuación, mencionó al propietario que nombró a Cashman director general y que ganó siete títulos mientras fue dueño del equipo.
«El señor Steinbrenner se estará revolviendo en su tumba», dijo Gossage.
«No malgastaría ni un céntimo en llamarle»
Gossage dejó claro que ya no queda ninguna relación que arreglar con el director general. Cuando le preguntaron si pensaba ponerse en contacto con Cashman, descartó la idea.
«No me gastaría ni un céntimo en llamarle», dijo Gossage.
Relacionó los problemas de los Yankees con el departamento de análisis que Cashman ha creado y sugirió que el director general quiere aún más control sobre las decisiones durante los partidos.
«A Cashman le encantaría que uno de sus frikis de la analítica se encargara de dirigir, pero no tiene las agallas para hacerlo», dijo Gossage.
Gossage se mostró igual de desdeñoso con el entrenador Aaron Boone, que entra en el último año de su contrato.
«Se limita a cobrar el sueldo», dijo Gossage.
Dijo que es el equipo de análisis, y no el entrenador, el que toma las decisiones.
«Los Yankees no necesitan un entrenador. Lo que sea que escupa ese ordenador», dijo Gossage.
Gossage también comentó que los entrenadores despedidos por los Yankees en las últimas dos décadas le han dicho que el trabajo no estaba a la altura de lo que esperaban cuando llegaron.
También criticó la plantilla que ha montado Cashman, señalando especialmente al segunda base Jazz Chisholm Jr., que está a punto de convertirse en agente libre.
«Es una vergüenza para los Yankees. Es un payaso», dijo Gossage.
Gossage le dice a Steinbrenner que venda
Cuando le preguntaron quién era el responsable de las 17 temporadas sin ganar ningún título, Gossage amplió el punto de mira más allá de Cashman hasta el propietario que acababa de renovarle el contrato.
«Todo el equipo directivo. Hal (Steinbrenner) y toda la dirección del club. Hal debería vender el equipo», dijo Gossage.
Afirmó que las prioridades de la propiedad son más económicas que deportivas.
«Todo gira en torno al dinero. Lo único que hacen los Yankees es ka-ching, ka-ching, ka-ching», dijo Gossage.
Insistió en que su enfado va dirigido a la gente que dirige el club, no a la franquicia en sí.
«¡Me encantan los Yankees! ¿Estás de broma? Lo que no me gusta es todo este sistema», dijo Gossage.
El balance de Cashman, dividido en dos
La etapa de Cashman se divide claramente en 2009. De 1998 a 2009, sus primeras 12 temporadas, los Yankees ganaron cuatro títulos de la Serie Mundial.
En las 17 temporadas posteriores, no han ganado ninguno. Han llegado una vez a la Serie Mundial, donde perdieron contra los Dodgers de Los Ángeles en 2024.
Esa sequía iguala ahora el periodo más largo sin ganar un campeonato en la historia del equipo. Los Yankees también estuvieron 17 temporadas sin ganar un título entre 1978 y 1996, un periodo que empezó justo después de la primera temporada de Gossage con la camiseta a rayas.
Cashman sigue al mando de los Yankees
Cashman dirigirá la pretemporada de los Yankees bajo su nuevo contrato. Todavía se está ultimando el cuerpo técnico para 2027, y 10 jugadores se encaminan hacia la agencia libre.
Steinbrenner ha dicho que se avecinan cambios «de arriba abajo, como hacemos todos los años».
¿Qué te parece? Deja tu comentario aquí abajo.

item.content:encoded:
Blue Jays: Seeing how Dylan Cease stacks up against Cam Schlittler for the AL Cy Young award
Photo credit: © Nick Turchiaro-Imagn Images
For the fifth time in seven seasons, the Toronto Blue Jays will have a finalist for the American League Cy Young award.
While not officially announced, Dylan Cease did more than enough to become a finalist for this season’s Cy Young award. He’ll join Hyun Jin Ryu (2020), Robbie Ray (2021), Alek Manoah (2022), and Kevin Gausman (2023) as finalists since the start of the 2020s.
Realistically, it’s a two horse race between Cease and New York Yankees’ ace Cam Schlittler, and calling it a two horse race is a little generous.
The question is, just how close was the race between the two American League East pitchers?
Schlittler’s 2026 season
Schlittler is the front runner to win the award, and for good reason. This past season, the 25-year-old finished with a 1.95 ERA and 2.56 FIP in 193.2 innings of work, with a 31.4 K% and 6.4 BB%.
No American League pitcher with 100 or more innings pitched finished with a better ERA than Schlittler, with Jacob Misiorowski being the only pitcher in Major League Baseball with a better ERA.
His FIP of 2.56 was tied for best among pitchers who finished their season in the American League. Only Misiorowski, Chirs Sale, and Tarik Skubal finished with a better FIP in all of Major League Baseball of pitchers with 100 or more innings pitched.
Where Schlittler excelled was efficiency while still maintaining a high strikeout rate. He was one of just eight starters with 100+ innings pitched and a K% above 30 percent. His 31.4 K% finished fourth in the big leagues, and third in the American League. 
Schlittler’s 6.4 BB% didn’t stand out all that much, barely ranking in the top 30 among pitchers with 100+ innings of work. But when paired with his strikeout rate of 31.4%, Schlittler’s K-BB% of 25 percent ranks fifth-best in MLB, second-best among American League pitchers.
But what about Cease?
Cease’s 2026 season
Schlittler is pretty much a lock to win his first Cy Young award, but Cease had a great season in his own right. Over 169 innings of work, Cease finished with a 2.40 ERA and 2.56 FIP, with a 34.9 K% and 11.4 BB%.
Cease’s ERA ranked third in Major League Baseball and second in the American League. Aside from Misiorowski and Schlittler, Sale was the only other pitcher with 100+ innings of work who finished with a better ERA than Cease.
In the next to impossible chance that Cease somehow does win the Cy Young, a big reason why would be his FIP, or Fielding Independent Pitching. Basically, it measures what the pitchers can realistically control, strikeouts, walks/hit by pitches, and home runs. He matched Schlittler’s 2.56, tied for the best in the American League and tied for third in the big leagues.
The biggest reason why his FIP was so good was his strikeout rate. Only Misiorowski finished with a better K% than Cease’s 34.9 percent. Cease’s 239 strikeouts were tied with Schlittler, but Cease pitched one fewer game and nearly 25 fewer innings. Only Gavin Williams, another starter who’ll likely get votes, finished with more strikeouts among AL pitchers.
Cease had a better strikeout rate than Schlittler, but he walked far more batters. Among pitchers with 100 or more innings pitched, no pitcher had a higher BB% than Cease’s 11.4 walk rate. Cease’s struggles with command is a big reason why Schlittler finished with more innings per start than Cease.
So who wins?
Only one Blue Jay pitcher has won a Cy Young Award since 2005, Ray back in 2021. Cease will probably eventually win one, but it won’t be in 2026. Unfortunately, Schlittler was just the best pitcher in the American League this season, it wasn’t really up for debate after Cease’s final three starts.
Earned run average has been an important metric to determine a winner of the award since 2020. No American League pitcher in the past six seasons has finished with the lowest ERA among qualified pitchers and hasn’t won the award. The last time it happened was in 2019, when Justin Verlander won with a 2.58 ERA, slightly better than Gerrit Cole’s 2.50 ERA.
The last time a player won with a margin nearly as large as Schlittler’s 0.45 lead was back in 2014. Corey Kluber finished with a 2.44 ERA, far worse than Félix Hernández’ 2.14 ERA. It was a different game back then, as Kluber had an 18-9 ERA compared to Hernández’ 15-6 record. Kluber also had three complete games.
While Cease may only finish second, his performance in 2026 was a big reason why the Blue Jays were anywhere near a playoff spot in September. Hopefully, he’ll win the award sooner rather than later.
Cynthia Ryley Delaney is a Nation Network writer for Blue Jays Nation, DFOEdmonton, and DFOCalgary. She can be followed on Twitter @CynthiaRDelaney.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees made a lot of moves during the middle of the 2026 season to bolster their roster.
One of those moves was to acquire John Schreiber.
He had a 1.64 ERA in 11 regular season games for the Yankees.
MLB.com wrote (on August 31): “New York Yankees claimed RHP John Schreiber off waivers from Kansas City Royals.”
Recently Acquired Pitcher Becomes Free Agent
This week, Schreiber officially became a free agent.
He will be available to sign with any team in the MLB this winter.
MLB.com wrote (on October 29): “RHP John Schreiber elected free agency.”
Schreiber also appeared in two MLB playoff games for the Yankees.
Looking At Schreiber
John Schreiber #56 of the New York Yankees throws a pitch against the Boston Red Sox during the ninth inning in game one of the American League Wild Card Series at Yankee Stadium on September 29, 2026 in the Bronx borough of New York City.
Schreiber was picked in the 15th round of the 2016 MLB Draft.
He spent the first two seasons of his career pitching for the Detroit Tigers.
The Red Sox acquired Schreiber in 2021.
MLB.com wrote (on February 18, 2021): “Boston Red Sox claimed RHP John Schreiber off waivers from Detroit Tigers.”
John Schreiber #46 of the Boston Red Sox walks to the dugout after pitching during the seventh inning against the Cleveland Guardians at Fenway Park on April 29, 2023 in Boston, Massachusetts.
Schreiber then pitched three years for the Red Sox.
In 2022, he went 4-4 with a 2.22 ERA in 64 games.
The Royals acquired him in a trade ahead of the 2024 season.
MLB.com wrote (on February 17, 2024): “Boston Red Sox traded RHP John Schreiber to Kansas City Royals for RHP David Sandlin.”
John Schreiber #56 of the New York Yankees delivers a pitch against the Tampa Bay Rays during the sixth inning in game two of the American League Division Series at Tropicana Field on October 05, 2026 in St Petersburg, Florida.
Schreiber (who is 32) will be an intriguing free agent to hit the market.
Looking At The Yankees
Manager Aaron Boone #17 of the New York Yankees walks back to the dugout after a pitching change against the Tampa Bay Rays during the eighth inning in game one of the American League Division Series at Tropicana Field on October 03, 2026 in St Petersburg, Florida.
The Yankees last won a World Series title in 2009.
They were the second-place team in the American League East with a 93-68 record in 161 games.
