item.content:encoded:
Brian Cashman will be back on a new deal, but the front office around him will look differently next season.
The Yankees are not renewing the contracts of grizzled top advisers Brian Sabean and Omar Minaya, as The Post’s Jon Heyman first reported.




Access the Yankees beat like never before

Join Post Sports+ for exciting subscriber-only features, including real-time texting with Greg Joyce about the inside buzz on the Yankees.
Try it free
The behind-the-scenes changes also will include two professional scouts — Tom Wilson and the retiring Pat Murtaugh — not returning, The Post’s Joel Sherman reported.
Meanwhile, the Yankees have hired former major league reliever and Harvard grad Frank Herrmann as supervisor for global evaluation/player development integration.
Herrmann had worked in the Blue Jays’ front office.
Sabean and Minaya had been hired ahead of the 2023 season, the former as executive adviser to Cashman and latter as a senior adviser.
Both had been the lead decision-makers with other organizations — Sabean for the Giants, Minaya for the Mets and Expos — both brought decades of experience in the game and in New York, and both had Cashman’s ear for the past three seasons.
Informing the pair this early in what will be an expedited offseason, given the impending lockout, allows them to seek employment elsewhere.
Sabean’s baseball career began as a scout with the Yankees in 1985 for an organization that Cashman joined as a college intern in 1986.
Sabean rose to vice president of player development/scouting, a role in which he helped bring in the Core Four — Derek Jeter, Mariano Rivera, Jorge Posada and Andy Pettitte — then left for San Francisco in 1993, won three World Series as GM in 2010, 2012 and 2014, eventually was phased out of the front office and returned to the franchise where it all started, a seasoned pair of eyes chiming in on player evaluation for the Yankees.
Minaya, who also began his career as a scout, is best known locally for three different stints with the Mets, including serving as GM from 2005-10.
He also had worked for the Expos, Rangers, Padres, Players’ Association and MLB, a baseball lifer whose established relationships aided the Yankees in several notable pursuits over the past few years: Minaya was influential in the trade for Juan Soto executed with a Padres front office that he knew well, and was part of the teleconference that lured Max Fried to The Bronx.
Fried had been drafted by the Padres when Minaya was San Diego’s senior VP of baseball operations.
Sabean and Minaya, more traditional baseball men, were brought on by Cashman at a time some believed his front office had leaned too heavily toward the analytical side. It will be curious whether, and if so by whom, they are replaced.
The Yankees have not won a World Series since 2009, and frustration from the fan base may be reaching a zenith after the club was swept by the Rays in the ALDS.
For the team’s ultimate failure, Hal Steinbrenner placed the blame on players who he believes underperformed — which may lead to changes within the coaching staff, particularly within their hitting team — rather than issues with the front office or at manager. Cashman has agreed to a new contract, and manager Aaron Boone will be back for the last year remaining on his pact.

item.title: [The Big Lead] Yankees making drastic changes to front office after another failed season
item.dc:creator: Lou Landers
item.description: The New York Yankees are making front-office changes after another disappointing MLB season, with two experienced executives no longer expected to be part of Brian Cashman’s group in 2027. The Yankees aren’t renewing the contracts Omar Minaya and Brian Sabean, who served as special assistants to GM Brian Cashman, via sources. Minaya is the former Mets GM, Sabean the Giants GM in their heyday. — Jon Heyman (@JonHeyman) October 31, 2026 The moves represent a change within the Yankees’ baseball ope
item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees are making front-office changes after another disappointing MLB season, with two experienced executives no longer expected to be part of Brian Cashman’s group in 2027.
The Yankees aren’t renewing the contracts Omar Minaya and Brian Sabean, who served as special assistants to GM Brian Cashman, via sources. Minaya is the former Mets GM, Sabean the Giants GM in their heyday.
— Jon Heyman (@JonHeyman) October 31, 2026
The moves represent a change within the Yankees’ baseball operations department after another season ended without a World Series championship. While Cashman is returning, the organization is beginning to reshape the group around him.
Yankees not renewing Minaya and Sabean, but Cashman and Boone remain
Minaya and Sabean both joined the Yankees before the 2023 season, bringing decades of front-office experience to Cashman’s staff. Sabean previously served as the general manager of the San Francisco Giants, while Minaya held general manager positions with the New York Mets and Montreal Expos.
Sabean spent nearly two decades running the Giants and was in charge during their championship runs in 2010, 2012, and 2014. Before his time in San Francisco, Sabean also spent several years working within the Yankees organization.
Minaya also brought extensive experience to New York after previously running the Mets and Expos. His relationships around the game were viewed as an asset to the Yankees, and he was reportedly involved in the club’s pursuit of Juan Soto and Max Fried.
The Yankees’ own front-office directory currently lists Sabean as an executive advisor to the general manager and Minaya as a senior advisor in baseball operations.
Not enough change despite another disappointing finish to a season
The departures come as the Yankees face increasing pressure to make meaningful changes after another postseason disappointment. New York was eliminated in the ALDS, continuing a stretch in which the franchise has struggled to turn regular-season success into another championship.
Cashman, however, is staying in place after agreeing to a new contract with the Yankees. Manager Aaron Boone is also returning, meaning the organization is making changes around its top baseball decision-maker rather than starting over at the top.
That makes the decisions involving Minaya and Sabean particularly notable. Both executives were brought in as experienced voices to advise Cashman, and their departures will leave the Yankees without two former general managers who have been part of the organization’s baseball operations group since 2023.
More changes could follow as the Yankees continue working through the offseason. For now, the first major front-office moves involve two veteran executives leaving, while Cashman remains in charge of setting the organization’s direction heading into 2027.

item.content:encoded:
The Yankees are not renewing the contracts of Omar Minaya and Brian Sabean, a source confirmed to the Daily News on Saturday.
The longtime baseball executives had been serving as advisors to Yankees general manager Brian Cashman since January 2023. Minaya held the title of senior advisor to baseball operations, while Sabean held the title of executive advisor to the general manager. Both men, with ample experience in the scouting world, were brought in at a time when the Yankees were being criticized for being too analytical.
The New York Post’s Jon Heyman first reported that Minaya and Sabean were not being retained.
Minaya previously held multiple positions with the Mets, including the title of general manager. He also became baseball’s first Hispanic general manager with the Expos in 2002, and he’s filled prominent roles with Major League Baseball and the Padres.
Minaya’s time with San Diego benefitted the Yankees, as his preexisting relationship with Padres GM A.J. Preller played a small part in facilitating the Juan Soto trade in December 2023. Minaya also scouted Max Fried for the Padres before they drafted him in 2012. That familiarity gave Fried some comfort on a Zoom call when the Yankees successfully recruited him ahead of the 2025 season.
Minaya was instrumental in organizing the Yankees’ return to Mexico City in March 2024. The two exhibition games they played against the Diablos Rojos del México marked their first visit to the Mexican capital in over 50 years.
Sabean, meanwhile, was not as visible a presence as Minaya during his second stint with the Yankees. He previously played a vital role in boosting the organization’s farm system while serving as vice president of player development and scouting from 1990-1992; director of scouting from 1986-1990; and as a scout in 1985.
Sabean is best known for his 30-year tenure with the Giants. He won championships in 2010, 2012 and 2014 while leading their baseball operations department.
The Yankees also continued to revamp their international scouting department under director Mario Garza, as a source confirmed that they’ve hired former MLB pitcher Frank Herrmann to the role of supervisor of global evaluation/player development integration. This is a new role but similar to the one already held by Matt Slater, supervisor of global acquisitions.
Herrmann spent several seasons playing in Japan, most recently in 2021, and had been working in the BlueJays’ front office. The Yankees, meanwhile, have made it no secret that they want to increase their presence in Asia, especially when it comes to finding amateur talent.
The Post’s Joel Sherman first reported Herrmann’s hiring.

item.content:encoded:
Two of New York Yankees general manager Brian Cashman's special assistants reportedly won't be back with the organization in 2027.
According to Jon Heyman of the New York Post, the Yankees are not renewing the contracts of Omar Minaya and Brian Sabean.
That news comes on the heels of the Yankees announcing last week that Cashman had agreed to a new deal to remain with the team next season.
TOP NEWS
Yankees Ripped After World Series 😳
Astros Hire Randy Flores as GM
Way-Too-Early 2027 MLB Playoff Predictions 🔮
Cashman, 59, is the longest-tenured GM in Yankees history, having held the title since 1998.
He joined the Yankees organization in 1986, going on to win the 1996 World Series as assistant GM, before winning four more World Series as general manager.
However, the Yankees have not won a World Series since 2009, and they have only made it to the World Series once since then, losing to the Los Angeles Dodgers in 2024.
Although the Yankees have reached the playoffs in three consecutive seasons and nine of the past 10 seasons, success during the postseason has largely eluded them.
Since making it to the 2024 World Series, the Yanks have suffered back-to-back, one-sided losses in the American League Division Series.
Despite that, ownership made the decision to retain both Cashman and manager Aaron Boone for the 2027 campaign.
In Minaya and Sabean, the Yankees are parting ways with two executives who have MLB GM experience.
The 67-year-old Minaya was general manager of the New York Mets and Montreal Expos in the past, while the 70-year-old Sabean was GM of the San Francisco Giants, leading them to three World Series titles from 2010 to 2014.
While the Yankees are losing a ton of experience from their front office, it figures to be business as usual with Cashman trudging toward 30 years as the franchise's GM.
Cashman's biggest orders of business this offseason figure to focus on adding some bats and bullpen arms via free agency or trade, while also figuring out what to do with internal free agents such as closer David Bednar, second baseman Jazz Chisholm and outfielder Trent Grisham.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Yankees Have Issues Up Top That Replacing Aaron Boone Won't Fix

The question of whether Posada feels accepted by the Yankees is less about the organization's courtesy toward its former great
item.content:encoded:
Earlier this week, Jorge Posada mentioned on the New York Post's "The Show" podcast that he hasn't felt welcome by the New York Yankees. At first glance, it's a tough look.
Here is one of the Yankees' better offensive pieces from their glory days in the late 90s and into the 2000s. Posada has multiple World Series rings and a wealth of knowledge when it comes to winning. The question of whether Posada feels accepted by the Yankees is less about the organization's courtesy toward its former greats, though, and more about whether it matters to their future success.
If Posada doesn't feel the team that developed him has shown him much love, the Yankees should look to mend things with him, but overall, it's not relevant to finally winning their 28th championship after a 17-year lull. These are two separate issues.
The Yankees finally getting over the hump and hoisting another trophy in the Bronx has more to do with their process than it does with who the manager is. One thing about this team is that it had a ton of turnover during these years, with Aaron Judge emerging as the best player in baseball.
The core from his first MVP back in 2022 is entirely different than the one they saw this year. It's even much different than the 2024 team that made it to the World Series.
The players seem to change, but the results don't. While it's hard to say for sure that hiring Posada will change the team's postseason success, many of these championship-less years haven't happened under Boone.
Under Joe Girardi, they struggled to make it out of the American League after he finally won the World Series as skipper in 2009. Their inability to win is deeper than who the manager is.
In desperate need of a modern front office
The fact is, teams like the Dodgers, coming off back-to-back championships, and the Brewers, the league's current champions, aren't featuring all-time greats as skippers. Dave Roberts played a small part as a bench piece for the Dodgers before being traded to the Red Sox in 2004. Then, with the Brewers, Pat Murphy never made it out of Low-A.
The one thing the Dodgers and Brewers have in common is their front offices' cutting-edge approach to data and how they apply it. On the Dodgers' end, Andrew Friedman came from the Tampa Bay Rays—a team that always finds a way despite having one of the lowest payrolls.
As for the Brewers, Matt Arnold is their current President of Baseball Operations. He spent nine seasons with the Rays and also worked with Andrew Friedman.
When fans and media say they need to draw from the Rays and Brewers, it isn't about their style of play. It's simply that the front office may need a facelift, and that could come by poaching from the Rays or Dodgers. It wouldn't help taking from the Brewers either.
The thing is, that would mean Hal Steinbrenner would finally have to move on from Brian Cashman. That doesn't seem like something he intends to do.
For Steinbrenner, Cashman has helped the Yankees build a solid foundation, and they're always in the postseason mix, even if they do fall short. He doesn't seem to want to risk the status quo, which helps fill the stadium night after night during the regular season.
This is why hiring someone like Posada as manager might get them similar results to what they have seen since 2010. However, fans could call for Posada's removal as manager, as they have done with Boone for years now.
They could hire Posada, but that shouldn't be the only change. They need more forward-thinking minds running the Yankees behind their manager—Boone or not. This would require the kind of leap of faith Steinbrenner has yet to take as Yankees owner.
Joe Randazzo is a reference librarian who lives on Long Island. When he’s not behind a desk offering assistance to his patrons, he writes about the Yankees for Yankees On SI. Follow him as @YankeeLibrarian on X and Instagram.

The Pittsburgh Pirates are coming off another season where they missed the MLB playoffs.
That said, they have a lot of young talent on the roster (and were competitive for most of the 2026 season).

It’s worth noting that a former Pirates All-Star has officially elected free agency from the New York Yankees.
David Bednar will be available to sign with any team in the MLB this winter.
MLB.com wrote (on October 29): “RHP David Bednar elected free agency.”
Closing pitcher David Bednar #53 of the New York Yankees reacts at the final out as the Yankees defeat the Kansas City Royals 4-3 to win the game at Kauffman Stadium on May 25, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri.
Bednar is coming off a very solid year for New York.
He went 7-3 with a 2.47 ERA in 64 games (with 35 saves).
There is no question that Bednar will be a very intriguing free agent (who the Yankees should want to bring back).
Looking At Bednar
David Bednar #51 of the Pittsburgh Pirates pitches in the ninth inning during the game against the Miami Marlins at PNC Park on June 11, 2025 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.
Bednar was picked in the 35th round of the 2016 MLB Draft.
He spent the first two seasons of his career with the San Diego Padres.
MLB.com wrote (on January 19, 2021): “Pittsburgh Pirates Traded RHP Joe Musgrove to San Diego Padres; New York Mets Traded C Endy Rodriguez to Pittsburgh Pirates; San Diego Padres Traded LHP Joey Lucchesi to New York Mets and San Diego Padres Traded RHP David Bednar, CF Hudson Head, RHP Drake Fellows and LHP Omar Cruz to Pittsburgh Pirates.”
David Bednar #51 of the Pittsburgh Pirates pitches in the ninth inning during the game against the New York Mets at PNC Park on June 28, 2025 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.
Bednar then had a run with the Pirates that lasted part of five seasons.
He made two trips to the All-Star Game in that span.
The Pirates then traded him to the Yankees during the middle of the 2025 season.
Looking At The Pirates Right Now
The Pirates finished the year as the third-place team in the National League Central with an 82-80 record in 162 games.
They last made the MLB playoffs during the 2015 season.

item.title: [Heavy.com] New York Yankees Trade Idea Dumps Jasson Dominguez for Tigers' All-Star Infielder
item.dc:creator: TJ French
item.description: Among the ‘wish list’ of things for the New York Yankees this offseason, perhaps the biggest point of emphasis for Brian Cashman and the Yankees’ front office is finding a replacement for third baseman Ryan McMahon. New York could do this by either signing a notable player in free agency, or the Yankees could look to make a splash in the trade market. A recent trade pitch by SNY suggests that the Yankees should link with the Detroit Tigers in a deal that would net All-Star infielder Zach McKinst
item.content:encoded:
Among the ‘wish list’ of things for the New York Yankees this offseason, perhaps the biggest point of emphasis for Brian Cashman and the Yankees’ front office is finding a replacement for third baseman Ryan McMahon.
New York could do this by either signing a notable player in free agency, or the Yankees could look to make a splash in the trade market.
A recent trade pitch by SNY suggests that the Yankees should link with the Detroit Tigers in a deal that would net All-Star infielder Zach McKinstry for outfielder Jasson Dominguez.
More MLB on Heavy: New York Yankees Release 5 Players From Organization After World Series
Should Yankees Offload Jasson Dominguez for Zach McKinstry?
There is certainly a strong argument to be made that the Yankees might look to offload Jasson Dominguez this offseason, especially after another lackluster campaign at the plate and more uninspiring defense in the outfield, but is Zach McKinstry even a good replacement for McMahon? Or Jazz Chisholm Jr., for that matter??
YanksGoYard.com writer Colin Keane hit on the recent trade idea by SNY, and wrote (about McKinstry):
“Not to say that this deal would be a straight-up swap, but by pitting these two players against each other 1-on-1, we can come to an understanding about their comparative value and the legitimacy of this trade idea for the Yankees. McKinstry’s offensive value rests entirely on his 2025 season, in which he hit .259/.333/.438 with 12 home runs, made the All-Star team, and bagged a Silver Slugger. He was far worse this past season, hitting .199/.288/.294 with just four homers. But in fact, those numbers were closer to his career norms than 2025 was, seeing as McKinstry is a career .225 hitter who has never hit more than nine home runs outside of the 2025 campaign and has also been limited to four homers in two separate seasons beyond 2026.”
In 2026, Zach McKinstry batted .199 over 129 games, with an OPS+ of 64. An MLB veteran of seven seasons, but looking at this potential ‘player-swap’ deal…. the Detroit Tigers might actually be more of beneficiaries than the New York Yankees.
The Tigers would be receiving Jasson Dominguez, who, yes, has struggled in his MLB opportunities, but perhaps that’s because of the pressure in New York.
Dominguez is still just 23, and a change of scenery might actually be a good move for his future. He batted .225 in 2026 with an OPS+ of 75, and six home runs, so you could make the case that he’s actually a more productive offensive player than McKinstry.
As for McKinstry headed to New York in this deal, do Yankees fans really want to replace Ryan McMahon with another infielder who has a small power stroke? Probably not.
More MLB on Heavy: Former Toronto Blue Jays 2-Year Pitcher Quietly Elects MLB Free Agency
Who Says ‘No’ to Potential McKinstry-Dominguez Trade
Honestly, this trade idea doesn’t make much sense from the Yankees’ side.
While yes, they may want to offload Jasson Dominguez this offseason, they may use him as part of a bigger trade to land a higher-quality infielder. Dominguez could also still be a good depth option for New York in 2027, if they opt to keep him on the roster.
That’s not to say McKinstry isn’t a good player, but if the Yankees are serious about upgrading at third base, there are other trade/free agent targets that are much more productive hitters. Just to name a few that “might” be available: Nolan Arenado, Alec Bohm, Isaac Paredes, etc.
Now, if the Tigers were truly interested in Jasson Dominguez, perhaps they could throw in a top-20 prospect or two in order to see if that might entice New York enough to take on McKinstry.
Yankees/Tigers fans, let me know in the comments what you think about this trade idea. Does it make sense for either side??
More MLB on Heavy: Los Angeles Dodgers Trade Prediction Lands Reds’ Elly De La Cruz in 5-Player Deal

item.dc:creator: Maria Aldrich
item.description: The New York Yankees have 10 players who are free agents right now. Between now and 5 p.m. ET on Nov. 2, the organization has the opportunity to make qualifying offers. As for Jazz Chisholm Jr., an MLB writer predicted what his offer could look like and whether he'd accept it during the "quiet period." Yankees' Jazz Chisholm Jr. Prediction Shows Slim Qualifying Offer Opportunity Per Kerry Miller of Bleacher Report, fans shouldn't expect 28-year-old Chisholm to receive a qualifying offer. "There'
item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees have 10 players who are free agents right now.
Between now and 5 p.m. ET on Nov. 2, the organization has the opportunity to make qualifying offers.
As for Jazz Chisholm Jr., an MLB writer predicted what his offer could look like and whether he'd accept it during the "quiet period."
Yankees' Jazz Chisholm Jr. Prediction Shows Slim Qualifying Offer Opportunity
Per Kerry Miller of Bleacher Report, fans shouldn't expect 28-year-old Chisholm to receive a qualifying offer.
"There's no rule prohibiting a team from extending multiple qualifying offers in the same year," Miller wrote. "In fact, the Cubs, Padres and Phillies each had two last offseason. But most in the know seem to believe the Yankees will give David Bednar a qualifying offer while declining to extend one to Chisholm. Simply put, they don't need him with middle infielders George Lombard Jr., Anthony Volpe and José Caballero all returning."
But having said that, it shouldn't be off the table entirely, either.
Miller gives Chisholm a small chance — under 10% — of receiving a qualifying offer.
Not to mention, it's extremely unlikely Chisholm would be forward with it.
Chisholm has been such a bright spot for New York over the years.
During his 2025 campaign, he was hitting .242/.332/.481 with a .813 OPS and 31 homers through 130 games.
Fast forward to this past season, he slashed .231/.312/.399 with a .711 OPS and 19 homers through 137 games.
He registered 16 doubles, three triples and 55 RBIs.
This article was originally published on HEAVY

The New York Yankees have been off for over three weeks.
Their last game was on October 7 when they got swept by the Tampa Bay Rays in Game 3 of the ALDS.
Former All-Star Pitcher Becomes Yankee Free Agent
On October 29, news came out that Yankees pitcher Michael Fulmer had officially elected free agency.
He will be available to sign with any team in the MLB.
MLB.com wrote: “RHP Michael Fulmer elected free agency.”
Relief pitcher Michael Fulmer #43 of the New York Yankees pitches against the Arizona Diamondbacks during ninth inning of the MLB game at Chase Field on September 19, 2026 in Phoenix, Arizona.
Fulmer finished the 2026 season going 0-1 with a 3.29 ERA in 15 games.
He also spent time with the Los Angeles Angels (three games) before signing with the Yankees on August 26.
Gary Phillips of NY Daily News Sports had written (on August 26): “Michael Fulmer was recently designated for assignment by the #Angels. Didn’t allow a run in 3.2 IP for them. Not a whole lot of sample size for him the last 2 years (9.1 MLB IP), but the #Yankees have reached desperation mode after failing to add bullpen help before the deadline.”
Looking At Fulmer’s MLB Career
Michael Fulmer #32 of the Detroit Tigers throws a pitch while playing the Cleveland Guardians at Comerica Park on July 06, 2022 in Detroit, Michigan.
Fulmer was picked in the 1st round of the 2011 MLB Draft.
He pitched 5.5 seasons for the Detroit Tigers at the start of his career.
After winning the 2016 Rookie of The Year Award, he made the 2017 MLB All-Star Game.
Michael Fulmer #32 of the Detroit Tigers and the American League speaks with the media during Gatorade All-Star Workout Day ahead of the 88th MLB All-Star Game at Marlins Park on July 10, 2017 in Miami, Florida.
After the Tigers, Fulmer also had stints with the Minnesota Twins, Chicago Cubs and Boston Red Sox.
He has pitched part of nine seasons at the MLB level.
Looking At The Yankees Right Now
The Yankees are coming off a regular season where they were the second-place team in the American League East with a 93-68 record in 161 games.
They last won a World Series title during the 2009 season when Derek Jeter was still on their roster.

Looking At Goldschmidt’s Run In The Bronx
Paul Goldschmidt #48 of the New York Yankees hits an RBI single during the seventh inning of the game against the Tampa Bay Rays at Yankee Stadium on September 24, 2026 in New York City.
Goldschmidt has now played two seasons for the Yankees.
Despite turning 39 last month, he is coming off a solid year where he appeared in 105 games.
The seven-time MLB All-Star batted .252 with 18 home runs and 52 RBIs.
Paul Goldschmidt #48 of the New York Yankees hits a single against the Tampa Bay Rays during the eighth inning in game three of the American League Division Series at Yankee Stadium on October 07, 2026 in the Bronx borough of New York City.
Goldschmidt will be an intriguing free agent on the market, because he is a former superstar who is no longer in his prime (but is also still valuable).
Looking At His Other MLB Stops
Paul Goldschmidt #48 of the New York Yankees warms up prior to Game One of the American League Wild Card Series against the Boston Red Sox at Yankee Stadium on September 29, 2026 in the Bronx borough of New York City.
Goldschmidt was picked in the 8th round of the 2009 MLB Draft.
He is most known for his eight-year run on the Arizona Diamondbacks that saw him make six straight All-Star Games (2013-18).
Paul Goldschmidt #44 of the Arizona Diamondbacks before the MLB game against the Los Angeles Dodgers at Chase Field on September 11, 2015 in Phoenix, Arizona.

item.title: [Empire Sports Media] Yankees risk losing a defensive strength by moving Cody Bellinger
item.dc:creator: Alexander Wilson
item.description: Moving Cody Bellinger back to center field would solve one problem for the Yankees. It could also create another in left. With Trent Grisham reaching free agency, New York has to decide whether to shop for a center fielder or use the defensive versatility already on its roster. My preference is to keep Bellinger in left unless the club finds a credible replacement there first. The case is not that he cannot play center. He has done it before. It is that his work in left became valuable enough th
item.content:encoded:
Moving Cody Bellinger back to center field would solve one problem for the Yankees. It could also create another in left.
With Trent Grisham reaching free agency, New York has to decide whether to shop for a center fielder or use the defensive versatility already on its roster. My preference is to keep Bellinger in left unless the club finds a credible replacement there first.
The case is not that he cannot play center. He has done it before. It is that his work in left became valuable enough that a positional switch should not be treated as a free upgrade.
The Yankees have two outfield decisions, not one
Bellinger was a Gold Glove finalist in left and led major league left fielders with 21 Defensive Runs Saved, according to a report on the finalists. One defensive measure cannot provide a perfect forecast, but it captures why removing him from the position carries a cost.
Grisham accepted a one-year qualifying offer before 2026 and is again approaching the market. The World Series ended Wednesday, so the offseason is no longer a distant roster exercise. New York needs a center-field plan with or without him.
There is also Aaron Judge’s health to consider. He missed 100 of the Yankees’ 166 games, including the postseason, because of rib and calf injuries. More designated-hitter time could protect his body, but that would require another outfield solution and a plan for a spot Giancarlo Stanton has traditionally occupied.
The other path is worth considering
The alternative is to put Bellinger in center and use left field to add a bat. That could make sense if the best available hitter is a corner outfielder and the Yankees believe Bellinger can handle the larger assignment. A returning Grisham or another center fielder would let them leave Bellinger where his glove stood out.
This roster recommendation is not a report that the Yankees have selected a position or opened talks with a particular player. The market and Judge’s health will shape the final answer.
New York should price both arrangements before moving anyone. Solving center while weakening left would be a poor trade unless the new bat makes up the difference.
More about:New York Yankees

item.content:encoded:
How William Contreras joined Derek Jeter in exclusive MLB postseason club appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Milwaukee Brewers are savoring their World Series win. Meanwhile, catcher William Contreras earned MVP honors.
He posted staggering numbers that earned him the honor and put him alongside Derek Jeter, according to MLB Stats. Jeter and Contreras are the only players to hit .350 in 3 playoff series in the same year.
In 1999, Jeter batted .455 in the ALDS against the Texas Rangers. Then, he batted .350 against the Boston Red Sox in the ALCS. Finally, he hit .353 in the World Series against the Atlanta Braves, and the Yankees swept the series.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
Fast forward to 2026, Contreras batted .375 in the NLDS, .357 in the NLCS, and .381 in the World Series.
Only players to hit .350 in 3 series in the same #Postseason (min. 10 PA):
Derek Jeter – 1999 (LDS .455, LCS .350, WS .353)
William Contreras – 2026 (LDS .375, LCS .357, WS .381) pic.twitter.com/qJmswtfIAi
— MLB Stats (@MLBStats) October 29, 2026
Additionally, Contreras set a franchise record for the most postseason hits in franchise history with 19.
In the regular season, Contreras batted .270 with 153 hits, 18 home runs, and 94 RBIs.
The Brewers finished the season at 103-59 and winning the National League Central Division. Then, they defeated the San Diego Padres 3-1 in the NLDS. Afterward, the Brewers swept the Los Angeles Dodgers in the NLCS, ending their two year reign as world champions.
Along the way, Contreras won his 2nd World Series title, having won in 2021 with the Atlanta Braves.
Jeter is one of the best players of his era, 1996 to 2014. Along the way, the Yankees won five World Series titles (1996, 1998, 1999, 2000, and 2009). In 2000, Jeter won the World Series MVP, batting .409 with 9 hits, two home runs, and two RBIs.
Meanwhile, Contreras join the likes of Gene Tenace, Johnny Bench, and Rick Dempsey as catchers to win the World Series MVP.

item.content:encoded:
CC Sabathia sends huge message to Brewers after World Series win appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
CC Sabathia may not have spent the longest time with the Milwaukee Brewers franchise, but there is so much love between the two parties. And in the aftermath of the Brewers' World Series triumph on Wednesday after grabbing a 4-1 win in Game 5 to seal a 4-1 series win over the Tampa Bay Rays, Sabathia was among the first to give Milwaukee their due praise.
Posting on his official account on X, the former Brewers lefty sent a huge message, congratulating the team on their latest accomplishment that immortalizes them in MLB lore.
"World Series Champions for the first time ever!! Soak it all in Milwaukee!!!" Sabathia wrote.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
Sabathia knows what it's like to win a World Series title, having done so with the New York Yankees back in 2009. He surely must have wanted to win it with the Brewers during his lone season in the Cream City, but they ran into the buzzsaw that was the 2008 Philadelphia Phillies in the NLDS, losing in four games to the eventual World Series champion that year.
Sabathia, of course, was brilliant during his time with the Brewers. In 17 starts following a trade from the Cleveland Indians (now Guardians), Sabathia put up an elite ERA of 1.65 across 130.2 innings, helping Milwaukee clinch a postseason spot via the Wild Card.
However, Sabathia's lone postseason start for the Brewers did not go according to plan. The Phillies roughed him up, scoring five earned runs on him in just 3.2 innings in what would be a 5-2 loss for Milwaukee.
Nonetheless, Sabathia was so good for the team that the Brewers still deemed him worthy to be part of the team's Wall of Honor earlier this year.
Sabathia would sign a seven-year, $161 million contract with the Yankees to leave the Brewers in free agency, and that would result in him winning his first and only World Series title. But at the very least, he saw Milwaukee finally get their breakthrough 18 years after his time with the franchise.
Related: Pat Murphy reveals 'uncommon' demand to players that led Brewers to the top

Chourio aprovechó los extrainnings del Juego 4 para llegar a 10 imparables en el Clásico de Otoño, conectando un doble por el callejón del jardín derecho-central para terminar así una jornada en la que bateó de 6-2
item.content:encoded:
El venezolano Jackson Chourio está teniendo una postemporada de ensueño pues, aun cuando su aporte fue limitado en la Serie de Campeonato, su reciente despertar con el bate ya lo puso al nivel de Babe Ruth durante la Serie Mundial 2026.
¿Qué récord de Babe Ruth empató Jackson Chourio?
Chourio aprovechó los extrainnings del Juego 4 para llegar a 10 imparables en el Clásico de Otoño, conectando un doble por el callejón del jardín derecho-central para terminar así una jornada en la que bateó de 6-2 con una carrera anotada y una producida.
El doble en la entrada número 12 lo hizo alcanzar los 10 hits, convirtiéndose en el segundo jugador en la historia que conecta una decena de imparables en los primeros cuatro juegos de la Serie Mundial. El Gran Bambino, Babe Ruth, era el primero y, hasta ahora, único pelotero que lo había logrado durante el Clásico de Otoño de 1928.
¡HISTORICO!
¡El 10mo imparable de Jackson Chourio en esta #WorldSeries iguala la marca de Babe Ruth (1928) de más hits en los primeros cuatro juegos de un Clásico de Otoño. pic.twitter.com/Dp3vNkwO3W
— MLB Español (@mlbespanol) October 28, 2026
Babe Ruth, disputando la sexta de siete Series Mundiales con los Yankees en ese 1928, terminó conectando de 17-10 con 3 dobles y 3 jonrones, 4 carreras producidas y 9 anotadas, siendo el mejor bateador de ese Clásico de Otoño en el que los Bombarderos del Bronx barrieron a los St. Louis Cardinals.
Chourio despierta en el Clásico de Otoño
Chourio logró replicarlo tras una complicada Serie de Campeonato en la que bateó de 19-3 (.158), solo con un cuadrangular en la barrida de los Brewers sobre los bicampeones defensores, Los Angeles Dodgers.
JACKSON CHOURIO TIES A 98-YEAR-OLD RECORD ????
Chourio's 10th hit this #WorldSeries ties Babe Ruth (1928) for most through the first four games of a Fall Classic! pic.twitter.com/v5FDPeR35H
— MLB (@MLB) October 28, 2026
Pese a la derrota en el Juego 4, Chourio es uno de los contendientes más sólidos para ser elegido como el Jugador Más Valioso de la Serie Mundial junto a su compatriota William Contreras. Antes del Juego 5, el jardinero zuliano bateaba de 20-10 (.500) con 2 dobles, 2 producidas y 4 anotadas.

item.title: [Pinstripe Alley] Responding to The Athletic’s ten-step list for the Yankees
item.dc:creator: Peter Brody
item.description: On Monday, Chris Kirschner of The Athletic compiled a ten-item list to return the Yankees to the World Series. We shared it on the site as part of Tuesday’s news roundup, and it generated a fair bit of conversation. I thought we could take the time today to comb over the ten recommendations with a critical eye, seeing what aligns and what conflicts with our vision for the team and how to get them back into the Fall Classic. First, the list: - Extend the QO to David Bednar - Let Jazz Chisholm Jr.
item.content:encoded:
On Monday, Chris Kirschner of The Athletic compiled a ten-item list to return the Yankees to the World Series. We shared it on the site as part of Tuesday’s news roundup, and it generated a fair bit of conversation. I thought we could take the time today to comb over the ten recommendations with a critical eye, seeing what aligns and what conflicts with our vision for the team and how to get them back into the Fall Classic.
First, the list:
- Extend the QO to David Bednar
- Let Jazz Chisholm Jr. walk in free agency
- Hold a competition between Anthony Volpe and José Caballero for second
- Revisit playing Luis García Jr. at second or third
- Commit to Carlos LaGrange as a reliever full time
- Sign a right-handed catcher
- Pursue reliever Adrian Morejon in free agency
- Check in on Jeremy Peña and Isaac Paredes
- Acquire Steven Kwan
- Don’t overreact to Rays making World Series
Rather than respond to all ten items, I would rather combine elements and sentiments of each to find out how close or far apart Kirschner and I are on our evaluation of the Yankees’ needs and their avenues to address them.
Right off the bat, I’ll say that I agree with points three, five, and ten and don’t have much more to add to what Kirschner wrote. I also want to note the uncertainty over the financial landscape of the league post-CBA negotiations. What we do know based on public comments is that Hal Steinbrenner has been probably the owner most vocal in his support of instituting a salary cap, the most recent offer from the league to the union a $245.3 million cap, $171.2 million floor, and 50-percent revenue sharing. Many fans wondered why the owner of the most valuable franchise in the sport would voluntarily sign away the financial advantage he holds over lower revenue teams, however this presumes his motivations are driven by competitive advantage and not by appreciating his franchise’s value via the greater cost certainty that a cap would bring.
We can agree that Steinbrenner has been consistent in his desire to rein in payroll spending, so as always we have to view future planning through that lens. This affects points one, six, and seven. I certainly agree that the Yankees should extend the qualifying offer to David Bednar. At $23.15 million, the QO sits at the very top of the reliever market by AAV, but with the payoff of just a one-year commitment and possible draft pick compensation should he decline. However, I would simultaneously work towards negotiating a multi-year deal, somewhere in the two-to-three year range to lower AAV, as Bednar finally brought long sought-after stability to the closer role.
That being said, I would not be as willing to commit significant dollars to any reliever beyond Bednar. This includes Morejon, who projects to be the best reliever on the free agent market and a left-handed weapon the Yankees sorely need in their ‘pen. Matt Blake’s continued success in churning out high leverage relievers from pretty much anyone he gets his hands on is an incredible money-saving asset for the Yankees, helping remove the risk of investing substantial money in the most fungible position on the roster.
As for backup catcher, I’m not so much wed to a right-hander so much as literally anyone who’s a viable major league backup after suffering through the dregs of J.C. Escarra and Ali Sánchez. I’m probably more confident than most that Austin Wells is back to himself after recovering from the cervical headaches that plagued his early season — we’ve seen on too many occasions the affect head injuries have had on recent Yankees — and the rehabilitation of his bat along with his ever-elite defense means I’m comfortable with him getting the majority of reps behind the plate. As such, I think you can avoid another expenditure here on an investment in a productive but costly right-handed backup like Carson Kelly or Ryan Jeffers and sign a true second-stringer for a fraction of the cost.
That brings us to the conundrum of second and third base. Here is where I diverge the most from Kirschner. I think the Yankees should bring Jazz Chisholm Jr. back, preferably on the QO. In a league that is scant on high value second baseman and a free agent cupboard pretty bare of impact hitters, Jazz is your best option at the keystone. Even in a down year he generates such a high floor with his solid glove and elite base running, so this is not the same situation as the Trent Grisham QO, who was coming off an anomalous career-year — admittedly with batted-ball data to back it up but worsening defense and hamstrings that were likely already shot. I don’t love the idea of a declining-OBP Luis Arraez in a park that suppresses singles and I’m skeptical that Brandon Lowe is suddenly an able defender at second for the first time entering his age-32 season.
Speaking of defense, I am absolutely not on board with hoping García can man second or third. He is an absolute butcher with the glove at both positions, though proved himself more than capable at first. I would like to see him at first as much as possible given Ben Rice’s struggles at the position with Rice living as your primary DH. This begs the question of what Giancarlo Stanton’s future looks like, and I regret to say that I think there is a strong possibility he could get DFA’d this winter. He’s been my favorite Yankee since joining the team on account of his stoicism in the face of criticism and postseason heroics, but with the Marlins paying $10 million this coming season and the next I could see them eating the remaining $15 million.
Incorporating part of point eight, the two trade targets I believe the Yankees should be pursuing in earnest this winter are Jeremy Peña and CJ Abrams. The Yankees have not had a game-changing slugger up the middle since Robinson Canó and this pair represents two of the best middle infielders in the league. Neither projects long term for shortstop, and their weaker gloves and arms seem destined for second. Kirschner noted Isaac Paredes’ terrible glove and pull-side approach that would suffer without the Crawford Boxes which is why I would stay away from the Astros’ third baseman.
Instead, I’m convincing myself more and more each day on NPB star Teruaki Sato. There are questions about his glove and how his bat would make the adjustment to MLB pitching. However, there were similar questions facing Munetaka Murakami and Kazuma Okamoto and the pair just put up three-win seasons while slugging well over 30 bombs each. Plus, I would love to see the Yankees reestablish a foothold in the Japanese market when you look at the amount of commercial revenue the Dodgers have reaped and the allure their existing Japanese core has for future signees. An ideal scenario for me would see the Yankees acquire one of Peña or Abrams and one of Jazz or Sato, that resulting pair of players significantly raising the floor of the Yankees infield as it currently stands.
That brings me to the point that I hadn’t considered before reading Kirschner’s list and one that seems like a slam dunk. Steven Kwan and his .357 OBP and elite bat-to-ball skills seems like the perfect profile for a prospective leadoff hitter. He’s always been an able defender and acquitted himself well in his first season as a primary center fielder. While I wonder about the sustainability of the four-point jump up in his walk rate in 2026, he’s still never posted below three fWAR in five seasons with a ceiling as a 125-130 wRC+ hitter. I wouldn’t balk at headlining a potential deal with Spencer Jones despite how impressed I was at his mid-season adjustments and growing comfort at the plate, though I question Jones’ fit in an organization that doesn’t seem to prioritize high power at the expense of low contact.
In all, I’d say I’m in more agreement than not with Kirschner’s vision for the Yankees’ offseason. I’d say I’m a little more wary of the budgetary constraints and therefore reallocated those funds to the areas of the roster I feel are more dire needs, though I’d also say my aims are slightly more ambitious. Despite the sting of the sweep in the ALDS, this team is not that far away from the top of the AL and I hope ownership recognizes this and authorizes the necessary reinforcements to get it there.

item.title: [New York Post] Jorge Posada snub proves Yankees have a clubhouse issue: Adam Schein
item.dc:creator: Matt Ehalt
item.description:
Nauseating. Pathetic. Embarassment. Those are just several of the damning words Adam Schein, host of The Post’s daily “Schein Time” show on YouTube, used to describe the exclusive revelation from former catcher Jorge Posada on “The Show” on Tuesday that he does not feel welcome around the Yankees anymore.

item.content:encoded:
Nauseating. Pathetic. Embarassment.
Those are just several of the damning words Adam Schein, host of The Post’s daily “Schein Time” show on YouTube, used to describe the exclusive revelation from former catcher Jorge Posada on “The Show” on Tuesday that he does not feel welcome around the Yankees anymore.




Access the Yankees beat like never before

Join Post Sports+ for exciting subscriber-only features, including real-time texting with Greg Joyce about the inside buzz on the Yankees.
Try it free
And to Schein, when combined with Yankees shortstop Anthony Volpe not connecting with Hall of Famer Derek Jeter amid a career of underachievement, it speaks to an issue among the Bronx Bombers’ 26-man roster.
“So, I think this officially is a clubhouse issue. I think this officially is a player issue,” Schein said Tuesday on his show. “I think that Aaron Judge needs to take control of his own clubhouse. I want to know where Giancarlo Stanton is? Where’s the veteran leadership?
“If Derek Jeter can’t get Anthony Volpe on the phone, if Jorge Posada isn’t welcome, if you don’t want to pick the brain of Tino Martinez, then we’ve got problems. It’s as simple as that.”
Posada, a Yankees legend from 1995-2011, revealed on Tuesday’s show that he feels distant from the only team he played for during his career.
“I don’t think they want me there, to tell you the truth,” Posada said when asked by Joel Sherman about possibly helping the Yankees in the future.
“I don’t feel welcome when I go there, you know? Even in spring training, I don’t feel like — I’m just like, I don’t know, like, I don’t feel welcome. I don’t feel like they want me there, so I don’t go.”
Posada did not pinpoint that feeling to any specific instance or moment, although he called his final season in 2011 “a really tough one.”
The Yankees shifted him away from catcher to designated hitter and reduced his playing time, and Posada posted just a .714 OPS.
“So, it’s just tough to back and feel that again,” he said.
Schein believes that Yankees manager Aaron Boone, general manager Brian Cashman and owner Hal Steinbrenner are absolved of blame in this lingering Posada situation.
He gives Boone a “free pass,” believing a baseball lifer would not turn his back to legends, and doesn’t think Steinbrenner and Cashman would too reject on an esteemed player like Posada.
Posada has indicated in the past that there was some bad beef with top executives about that final season, while he did not blame then-manager Joe Girardi.
Adding this Posada reveal on top of the Jeter-Volpe non-relationship makes Schein believe that the current Yankees are not doing their part to lean on those with championship pedigree.
“Look at Jorge Posada’s resume. Come on? He doesn’t feel welcome at spring training? You’re telling me Austin Wells couldn’t use talking to Jorge Posada?” Schein said. “You’re telling me Anthony Volpe couldn’t use some kind of direction from Derek Jeter? These are guys who just want to be there, because it seems like they care more about winning than the current Yankee players.”
Schein also noted that this group of Yankees having yet to win a title — and has just one World Series appearance in the Aaron Judge era dating to 2017 — only makes this situation worse.
Posada won five titles during his time in The Bronx, including the franchise’s last World Series in 2009.
“If the Yankees of the current group, if they were winning, we’re not having this conversation but they’re losing and they’re fundamentally unsound, and they play at their worse when it matters the most,” Schein said. “The antithesis of Posada and Jeter and those amazing Yankees teams. That right there, that’s painful. … That makes me sick.
“The fact that Jorge Posada, an all-time great Yankee. Blood, guts, sweat, tears, joy, jubilation, a guy who understands what winning is all about, he doesn’t feeling welcome at spring training, the Yankee clubhouse? Man, and you wonder why this team can’t perform in big spots. You wonder why they can’t perform in extra innings. You wonder why they can’t have a lead in a series against the Tampa Rays. What a joke, an embarrassment, that was nauseating. Absolutely pathetic.”

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Brewers' Jackson Chourio Just Did Something Only Babe Ruth Has Done
item.dc:creator: Patrick McAvoy
item.description: We're witnessing one of the best World Series performances in Major League Baseball history by young Milwaukee Brewers outfielder Jackson Chourio. Any time you can put your name next to legendary slugger Babe Ruth, that means that you're doing something right. And that's exactly what Chourio did on Tuesday night as he tied the Hall of Famer for the most hits through four games in a World Series with 10. item.content:encoded:
We're witnessing one of the best World Series performances in Major League Baseball history by young Milwaukee Brewers outfielder Jackson Chourio.
Any time you can put your name next to legendary slugger Babe Ruth, that means that you're doing something right. And that's exactly what Chourio did on Tuesday night as he tied the Hall of Famer for the most hits through four games in a World Series with 10.
To put it into perspective, Ruth set the record back in 1928, 98 years ago. This isn't a record for someone of a certain age to reach this milestone, but simply in general. And that's absurd. The record for the most hits in a single World Series is currently 13, which is held by Marty Barrett, Lou Brock and Bobby Richardson. A big game on Wednesday night in Game 5 could put Chourio in that same category. He has multiple hits in each game so far, including a four-hit explosion in Game 3's blowout of the Tampa Bay Rays.
Jackson Chourio Is A Superstar
We're truly witnessing something special from Chourio. Overall, he has gone 10-for-20 (.500) with two RBIs, two doubles, three stolen bases and four runs scored in four games. Let's also not forget that he's just 22 years old. Milwaukee is just one win away from winning the franchise's first World Series and Chourios is one of the biggest reasons why.
He took a massive leap forward throughout the 2026 regular season and it has continued into the postseason. In the regular season, Chourio slashed .291/.351/.487 with an .837 OPS, 25 home runs, 75 RBIs, 23 stolen bases, 27 doubles and 96 runs scored in 127 games played. He set a new career high with 4.9 wins above replacement, despite missing the first few weeks of the campaign due to injury.
What should get Brewers fans fired up is the fact that he isn't going anywhere anytime soon as well. He's under contract through the 2031 season and then has affordable club options in 2032 and 2033. It would be a shock if he wasn't with the team at least through the 2033 season. That's seven more seasons before Milwaukee should even have to think about whether he'll be in town, or not. He already has developed into a star in Milwaukee and already is becoming a franchise postseason hero. What's next? The sky is the limit.
Patrick McAvoy's experiences include local and national sports coverage at the New England Sports Network with a focus on baseball and basketball. Outside of journalism, Patrick received an MBA at Brandeis University. For all business/marketing inquiries regarding "Milwaukee Brewers On SI," please reach out to Scott Neville: scott@moreviewsmedia.com

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees managed to get by with their bullpen in 2026 by the skin of their teeth. A unit that we repeatedly stated needed reinforcements avoided major catastrophes, but saw Tim Hill unravel to the point that he was left off the postseason roster and Brent Headrick begin to run out of gas following his Herculean workload.
Depth in the unit is absolutely something that needs to be improved, though Brian Cashman hasn't always agreed with that statement, but entering the offseason, the Yankees' relief corps is in even more dire straits.
David Bednar is a free agent and the top-ranked closer on the market. Surely there will be a bidding war for his services. Paul Blackburn was a big reason why Cashman's island of misfit toys actually worked out in 2026, but after revitalizing his career as a reliever, he's also hitting the open market, looking to cash in.
Losing one or both of these arms would be a huge blow. New York really needs to bring them both back, and then make more moves to fully solidify the 'pen. Fortunately, MLB insider Jim Bowden envisions good news on the Bednar and Blackburn fronts for the Yankees this winter.
Jim Bowden predicts the Yankees will spend big to retain David Bednar and Paul Blackburn
Bowden ranked the top 40 MLB free agents this offseason in a piece for The Athletic (subscription required) and also predicted ideal landing spots and contract terms for each player.
While many players have multiple ideal destinations listed, Bowden only has one home in mind for both Bednar and Blackburn, and that would be the Bronx. Should that come to fruition, it would be cause for Yankees fans to rejoice.
Interestingly, Bowden sees Cashman opening up the checkbook for both of these key arms, which is something he's mostly shied away from in recent years. Bednar's contract prediction is based on past contracts for high-end closers like Edwin Diaz, Tanner Scott, and Robert Suarez. The proposed deal comes in at three years, $55 million dollars, which looks like money well spent considering Devin Williams got three years, $51 million from the Mets last offseason. Through that lens, shelling out $18-plus million a year seems like a bargain. Putting the qualifying offer on Bednar should help the Yankees, further suppressing his market.
As for Blackburn, the former MLB GM predicts the Yankees will give him two years and $22 million. That's the same deal the Mets gave Luke Weaver last winter, and it's a bit of a risk given the fact that the 32-year-old only has one year of elite production. Still, paying up is a necessary evil, and the Yankees should feel confident that Matt Blake and company fully unlocked Blackburn.
This hypothetical would be a good start, but more will be needed. This simply returns New York to the status quo. The club will still need to find another arm or two, preferably of the high-velocity, high-strikeout variety, either through free agency or the trade market.
Bowden predicts an old-school bidding war between the Yankees and Red Sox for Teruaki Sato
One of the biggest storylines this offseason will be the market for NPB superstar Teruaki Sato. Sato's club, the Hanshin Tigers, has confirmed that it'll honor the slugger's wishes and post him this offseason.
We heard recently from Joel Sherman of the New York Post that the Yankees will look to dump Ryan McMahon this winter, but that pursuing Sato wouldn't be on the docket for New York, citing defensive concerns at third base.
Bowden sees things differently, believing that Sato can stick at the hot corner rather than being forced to move to left field or first base. As a result, he sees the Yankees and Red Sox engaging in the type of bidding war that used to be commonplace between these two rivals.
Sato brings massive power from the left side to the table, but also has some serious swing-and-miss concerns. The scouting report on him is similar to last year's sensation, Munetaka Murakami. Those worries forced Murakami down from a projected $150-plus million deal to a two-year, $34 million contract with the Chicago White Sox.
Murakami's 35-homer campaign reignited the idea that as long as the power translates, the whiffs are acceptable, and could reinvigorate the market for a player who can threaten the league lead in dingers, while also struggling to break the Mendoza line. As a result, Sato could be in line for a big payday.
That's exactly how Bowden sees things playing out, projecting a five-year, $180 million contract for the 27-year-old. Will the Yankees really go that high in order to wrestle him away from Boston? It might be hard to believe. But then again, the urgency to replace McMahon should be sky-high, and even if he's not the perfect option, he can't be worse than the whiff-happy incumbent.

item.content:encoded:
New York Yankees ace Cam Schlittler has won the 2026 Players Choice Award for AL Outstanding Pitcher.
The recognition follows a dominant 2026 campaign in which he posted a 14-6 record with a 1.95 ERA and 239 strikeouts across 193 2/3 innings pitched.
His sparkling 1.95 ERA also made history as the lowest by a Yankees pitcher since Ron Guidry in 1978. His 239 punchouts tied for the AL lead and also tied for fourth-most in a season in Yankees franchise history. Schlittler held opponents to a .185 batting average.
Every start is a movie. Congratulations, Cam Schlittler, the 2026 Players Choice Awards AL Outstanding Pitcher! @Yankees https://t.co/y18lkMTbNr
— MLBPA (@MLBPA) October 28, 2026
Schlittler is deserving of the award after his Cy Young-caliber season in which he successfully anchored the Yankees' rotation.
He surrendered one run or less in 22 of his 31 starts, illustrating his efficiency on the mound. His clutch and durable performance was a luxury for the Yankees amid their taxed rotation, as Gerrit Cole, Max Fried and Carlos Rodon dealt with injuries.
Schlittler also led the league with a 7.0 bWAR and a 6.2 fWAR. The 25-year-old dazzled with a 0.90 WHIP and a 31 % strikeout rate.
Now he has some hardware for his efforts.
Yordan Alvarez won AL Outstanding player, Pete Crow-Armstrong NL Outstanding Player, Jacob Misiorowski for NL Outstanding Pitcher, Kevin McGonigle AL Outstanding Rookie and Sal Stewart NL Outstanding Rookie.

item.content:encoded:
Following their disappointing setback in the American League Division Series against the Tampa Bay Rays, the New York Yankees have some serious questions to answer this offseason, and Aaron Judge isn’t exactly hiding what he wants to see from the organization.
The Yankees slugger, who has yet to experience World Series glory in his career, has made it clear that another disappointing season isn’t good enough. If the Yankees want to get back to where they believe they belong, some significant changes may be necessary.
New York Yankees Slugger Aaron Judge Gave The Club An Ultimatum For The Offseason
After the devastating loss to the Rays to end their season, Judge made no secret of the fact that he believes the club’s front office needs to do whatever is necessary to upgrade the club into championship contention.
“We’re the Yankees,” Judge said after his club dropped a 4-3 decision to the Rays, sealing their fate. “I feel like they should go all in and do what they need to do and find. If we’ve got holes, if it’s finding certain players or personnel, whatever we need, you’ve got to go out there and get it.
“That’s why I signed back here to play with the Yankees, to fight for a championship every single year, to go all in. That’s what I do every offseason, get ready to give this team and this city everything I’ve got. So I expect them to do the same.”
Does Judge believe the team has already gone “all-in”?
“It’s tough to say,” Judge said. “I want to trade for everybody, sign everybody every single year, but I know that’s not realistic. So they give us a winning team every single year, but that’s not good enough here in New York. We’re the Yankees. You’ve got to go out there and chase championships and go all in every year. So I’m excited to see what they do.”
That puts the pressure squarely on the front office, which now has to figure out how aggressive it wants to be this winter.
Needless to say, Judge isn’t going anywhere, but his latest comments could be viewed as something of an ultimatum for the Yankees: build a team capable of winning a championship around him, or risk wasting another year of his prime.
The Yankees Have Confirmed That Manager Aaron Boone Is Returning
The Yankees announced that manager Aaron Boone, who has been on the job since December of 2017, will be back for the 2027 MLB campaign, putting a major leadership change on hold.
While there was a varied reaction from fans of the Yankees, the move had the full and complete support of right-hander Cam Schlittler.
“He’s someone that’s going to put his players first, and I think that’s very important,” Schlittler said of Boone. “He’s been great to this team and to the guys in here. We trust him. There’s not a single day where I haven’t trusted him or a decision he’s made. I have a great relationship with him, and I’ll back him up.”

The Athletic's Jim Bowden predicted Bednar would sign a three-year, $55 million
item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees have some key players hitting the open market this offseason, but perhaps none are more important than David Bednar.
Bednar was the most important player in the Yankees bullpen this year, and he is bound to get paid in free agency. The two-time All-Star has been great ever since joining the Yankees, posting a 2.39 ERA in 86 outings. He has 45 saves and is arguably the best reliever on the market.
The Athletic's Jim Bowden predicted Bednar would sign a three-year, $55 million deal in free agency and called the Yankees his best team fit.
"Bednar was a lockdown closer for the Yankees this season, saving 35 games with a 2.47 ERA and 2.61 FIP in 69 1/3 innings with 76 strikeouts," wrote Bowden. "His wipeout split-fingered fastball was responsible for 50 of his strikeouts, as opposing batters hit just .149 against that pitch, and he had an elite chase rate. He proved he could handle pitching in the pressure environment in New York."
The Yankees don't usually spend big on relievers like Bednar, but even at 32 years old, he is deserving of a big payday. The Yankees don't really have a replacement for him right now, and a shutdown closer is not easy to find.
Bednar will draw interest from plenty of teams, but especially big markets if Bowden has the right read on his price tag. The Yankees cannot afford to lose him.
More MLB: Brewers' Jackson Chourio Stands Alone As Only Player To Do This Twice In Postseason

item.title: [Yanks Go Yard] Former GM Jim Bowden's hilarious Jazz Chisholm Jr. free agency destinations make it clear he's gone

item.content:encoded:
Jazz Chisholm Jr. has openly admitted that he's bothered by cold weather, which has always made a long stint with the New York Yankees feel unlikely for the Bahamian infielder. Every season in the Bronx, the games begin to really matter just as the temperature begins to drop -- a poor fit for Chisholm, one would deduce.
Chisholm made a name for himself playing in the warm clime of Miami for the Marlins organization. On the other hand, let's not act like Chisholm is rendered completely ineffective in colder regions. He did have a productive season-and-a-half with the Yankees leading up to 2026, which included a career-peaking 30-30 season in 2025 in the Bronx.
Jazz Chisholm's poor fit with Yankees is about more than cold weather
Chisholm's statistical cliff dive in 2026 can't be attributed to the season being bookended by frigid gusts and turtleneck requirements. Chisholm couldn't get his offense going in any temperature this year. When you add in his defensive errors in key moments (and his innate ability to tick off Aaron Boone), Chisholm's exit from the Yanks has felt like a sure thing for weeks.
And that's before any discussion of financials, which also make a Yankees reunion highly unlikely. Chisholm's down year means he won't approach the $350 million payday he was hoping for, but he's obviously still looking to cash in, and Brian Cashman's surely not going to be the GM to oblige.
Speaking of GMs, former MLB GM Jim Bowden just weighed in on Chisholm's potential destinations, and the three "best fits" that Bowden envisioned for Chisholm are hilariously (and somewhat logically) all warm-weather teams.
Jim Bowden names the Padres, Angels, and Athletics as best fits for Jazz Chisholm Jr. in free agency
From a Yankees fan perspective, the first thing that jumps out about these three franchises is that none of them are remotely close to New York City. It's borderline hilarious that Bowden threw the Athletics in there for Chisholm, by the way. It's as if to say that anywhere warm should be seen as appealing to Chisholm, even if nothing is appealing from a baseball fit standpoint or even a competitive standpoint. Going from the game's most historic franchise to the irrelevant A's? Sounds awesome!
Seriously, though, Chisholm grew up a Yankees fan and loves the tradition of the organization, even if he's added some unsavory elements to that tradition, like eating a lollipop while playing second base. Chisholm's said he also likes the high-profile market of New York. And despite his 2026 struggles, we can all see that Chisholm isn't a guy who hides from the spotlight. He relishes it, which is why he'd probably hate playing for a tiny-market club (even if it was warm there).
At any rate, Chisholm's free agency is sure to be an interesting storyline to follow this winter. His time with the Yankees is in the past, and despite the up-and-down performance, it was always entertaining.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Jazz Chisholm Jr. Isn't the Answer at Second Base for the A's

item.description: The Athletics don't have many holes on the position player side of things, with former All-Stars or potential All-Stars around the diamond. item.content:encoded:
The Athletics don't have many holes on the position player side of things, with former All-Stars or potential All-Stars around the diamond. The one spot they don't quite have nailed down is second base.
The Athletic's Jim Bowden made 40 predictions for pending free agents on Tuesday, along with what they would sign for and the teams that would be the best fits for that player. New York Yankees free agent second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. was one of the players listed as a fit for the A's.
Chisholm ended up hitting .231 in 2026 with a .312 OBP and a 98 wRC+ (100 is league average), adding 19 home runs and 41 stolen bases. His defensive grades were a little erratic, with defensive runs saved giving him a -6, while outs above average had him at a +13 and fielding run value gave him a +8.
While his wRC+ was a little below league average, adding value with the glove and finishing with the third-most stolen bases in MLB are true positives for a team like the A's who could use more speed and upgraded defense.
Two Reasons Why Chisholm Wouldn't Fit
The first big red flag for any A's pursuit in free agency is that Bowden also projected Chisholm to receive a six-year, $128 million contract with an opt-out after the second year.
That would easily be the biggest contract ever handed out by the team, and it would be for a nice-to-have upgrade at second base, rather than an area of need. The A's have internal options in that they're comfortable with who will cost the big-league minimum in 2027.
For similar money, the A's could build a pretty solid bullpen.
Athletics Roundtable recently floated the idea of signing Brandon Lowe in free agency. He is coming off a better offensive and defensive season, but given that he's 32, is projected by Bowden to receive three years and $45 million. Lowe hit 35 home runs and drove in 96 in 2026, on top of being one of the best defensive second basemen in baseball.
That's much more within the A's wheelhouse if they're going to address second base with an external option.
The other reason is that Chisholm's 30.9% whiff rate ranks in the 13th percentile, while his 29.5% strikeout rate ranks in the 9th percentile. For a team looking to make strides at the plate and limit strikeouts, those two numbers don't bode well for that trajectory.
Chisholm would add some flair to the A's team, but isn't what they're after if they're going to spend big money. His better fit may be more in line with a club needing a potential big bat in the lineup. The A's have a number of those already and can be a little more picky if they choose to address second base via free agency.

item.content:encoded:
MLB insider reveals Yankees' 'most realistic' free agent target at catcher originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The New York Yankees desperately need a right-handed hitting catcher.
Ali Sanchez was the primary backup behind Austin Wells, but he offers little upside on offense.
The Yankees could keep Sanchez as catching depth, but they would be better off finding a veteran with better offensive numbers.
The Athletic's Chris Kirschner wrote that New York's front office should be looking for a new catcher and it's a "must" for this winter.
He tabbed an 11-year veteran who spent the last two years with the Chicago Cubs as the top candidate.
"The Yankees have options to consider in free agency. Carson Kelly might be the best and most realistic option available," Kirschner wrote.
"He's expected to decline his $7.5 million mutual option with the Chicago Cubs and become a free agent. Kelly posted a 143 wRC+ against left-handed pitching this season and has 123 wRC+ against lefties in his career," Kirschner added.
"He also grades out well in blocks above average, according to Statcast, and is slightly above average in framing, a key metric the Yankees focus on when considering catchers."
Kirschner adds that Wells had a 19 wRC+ against left-handed pitching in 2026, so adding a right-handed platoon partner is necessary.
At the very least, the Yankees would feel confident that Kelly can provide above-average production against southpaws.
Other free agent backstops the Yankees could consider are Ryan Jeffers, Tyler Stephenson, Austin Hedges, or a reunion with Gary Sanchez or Kyle Higashioka.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees are at home for the offseason after losing to the Tampa Bay Rays in the ALDS.
At the end of the regular season, the Yankees honored legendary pitcher CC Sabathia.
The MLB wrote (via X) on September 25: “The Yankees honor CC Sabathia with a plaque in Monument Park and retire his No. 52 👏”
Wife Of Beloved Yankees Star Sends Out Heartfelt Post
On Sunday, Sabathia’s wife (Amber) made a heartfelt post to Instagram.
She wrote: “Prosecco and Frat Parties for Breakfast! Parents Weekend Vibes 🌟Go Blue! 💙💛”
Here’s what people were saying in the comments:
CC Sabathia: “〽️💛💙”
@paul_aversano: “You guys are all in!! Go blue!”
@tammy__gafoor: “Such a STUNNING family🤍💙Go Blue!!!”
CC Sabathia #52 of the New York Yankees walks off the field in the eighth inning and is congratulated by Derek Jeter #2 during Game One of the ALCS against the Los Angeles Angels of Anaheim during the 2009 MLB Playoffs at Yankee Stadium on October 16, 2009 in New York, New York.
Michelle Damon, Gabrielle Union-Wade and University of Michigan were among the people to like her post.
Looking At CC
CC Sabathia #52 of the New York Yankees celebrates striking out Mike Napoli #44 of the Los Angeles Angels of Anaheim to end the seventh inning in Game One of the ALCS during the 2009 MLB Playoffs at Yankee Stadium on October 16, 2009 in the Bronx borough of New York City.
Sabathia was picked in the 1st round of the 1998 MLB Draft.
He spent the first 7.5 seasons of his career with the Cleveland Guardians before a trade to the Milwaukee Brewers.

item.title: [OTIA Sports] Hideki Matsui Returns to the Yomiuri Giants as Manager, Bringing Fresh Attention to His Key Baseball Cards
item.dc:creator: Darryl P
item.description: Hideki Matsui is heading back to the most iconic franchise in Japanese baseball, and the move is giving collectors a new reason to revisit one of the hobby’s most important modern international careers.
