item.content:encoded:
Derek Jeter is one of the best players in all of MLB history.
The New York Yankees legend is still around the game, as he used to run the Miami Marlins (and currently works for FOX Sports).
Derek Jeter Sends Out Viral 10-Word Post
On Thursday, Jeter sent out a post to Instagram that had over 43,000 likes in five hours.
He wrote: “They said let’s go to the zoo, it’s not hot!”
Here’s what people were saying in the comments:
@alby_ray: “Leave the hoodie home next time😂”
@frankieturn2: “Imagine running into the goat at the zoo 😂🙌”
@lil_ledgy: “Lmao damn 2, look like you were fielding ground balls on an early July day in the Bronx”
American League All-Star Derek Jeter #2 of the New York Yankees stretches before the 83rd MLB All-Star Game at Kauffman Stadium on July 10, 2012 in Kansas City, Missouri.
@clyderivers: “Imagine being the GM of the Yanks instead! 😂”
@sean.byrd7: “My favorite player as a kid. I copied his swing”
@dverello: “Worked harder in two hours at the zoo than Cashman has in over a decade. That’s my CAPT.”
Derek Jeter hugs Aaron Judge #99 of the New York Yankees during commemorations for the 25th anniversary of 9/11 before the game between the New York Yankees and the New York Mets at Yankee Stadium on September 11, 2026 in The Bronx borough of New York City.
Jorge Posada, David Ross, Ken Griffey Jr., Shane Greene, Miguel Rojas and Andruw Jones were among the people to like Jeter’s post.
Looking At Jeter
Derek Jeter #2 of the New York Yankees in action against the Tampa Bay Rays at Yankee Stadium on July 28, 2013 in the Bronx borough of New York City.
Jeter was picked in the 1st round of the 1992 MLB Draft by the Yankees.
He spent all 20 seasons of his Hall of Fame career in the Bronx.
During that time, Jeter made 14 All-Star Games (and won five World Series titles).
Derek Jeter #2 of the New York Yankees celebrates after a game winning RBI hit in the ninth inning against the Baltimore Orioles in his last game ever at Yankee Stadium on September 25, 2014 in the Bronx borough of New York City.
The Yankees have been unable to win a title since the 2009 season (with Jeter).

item.content:encoded:
The 2025 season provided ideal outcomes for fantasy managers who invested in elite starting pitchers. That season, Tarik Skubal, Paul Skenes, Garrett Crochet and Zack Wheeler were the top four pitchers drafted. Per our Fantasy Player Rater, Skubal ($35.5), Crochet ($32.8) and Skenes ($30.8) finished 1-2-3 among starting pitchers in all roto formats. Wheeler finished 14th ($22.6) despite his season being cut short. As is the case every single year, to varying degrees, there were mid-round arms who produced elite roto seasons (Bryan Woo, Hunter Brown, Max Fried), as well starters such as Nathan Eovaldi, Matthew Boyd, and Trevor Rogers who provided hefty profit a as late-round picks and free agent acquisitions.
As is also the case every season, there were early-round landmines. Cole Ragans, Blake Snell, and Corbin Burnes all missed at least two-thirds of the season due to injuries. Logan Gilbert investors certainly weren’t thrilled about his abbreviated season with only six wins. Nevertheless, dream seasons from the Crème de la crème instilled an illusion of tranquility at the top of the SP pool for 2026 drafts despite the position’s inherent risks and volatile history.
The calm ominously turned to storm on Opening Day. Paul Skenes couldn’t get out of the first inning against the Mets, allowing five earned runs, as droves of social media melodramatics scolded us: “…and that’s why you never draft pitchers early!” Skenes (174 IP – 200 K – 10 W – 3.82 – 1.12) inevitably lost “fantasy god” status as his price dropped a couple of rounds for 2027 drafts. Skubal was a top 10 pitcher with elite ratios, but did not have his usual season of dominance due to missing 5-6 starts. Crochet was an injury landmine and one of many early-round busts.
There were some wins in the second tier (Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Chris Sale) as well as disappointments (Bryan Woo, Hunter Brown, Ragans again), but what may be most memorable about last season’s starting pitcher pool was that leagues were won without having to invest in early starting pitchers at all. Of course, that only happened to managers who side-stepped the early-round hitter landmines like Aaron Judge, Ronald Acuña Jr., Vladimir Guerrero Jr., Francisco Lindor and Cal Raleigh. The two top producers – Jacob Misiorowski and Cam Schlittler – were post-100 ADP picks. Of the 19 starters who earned $14 or more in 12-team leagues, 13 had an ADP of 100+, including six with an ADP of 250 or greater.
| # | Player | Team | ADP | Min Pick | Max Pick | SP Rank | $ Earned |

SP Rank and $ Earned from the FanGraphs Fantasy Player Rater (12-team)
A quick review of this group shouldn’t elicit much bewilderment besides maybe Nick Martinez. Most of the other top performers with a post-100 ADP were former prospects with breakout and profit potential. Let’s run through each set of five rounds by 2026 NFBC Online Championship (OC) 12-team ADP to review results in relation to draft price. Expect some takeaways for 2027 drafts along the way. Pitchers who were traded are listed with the team they were on in March.
| Player | Team | ADP | SP Rank | $ Earned |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Shohei Ohtani | LAD | 1.8 | 22 | $13.5 |
| Tarik Skubal | DET | 6.9 | 8 | $22.8 |
| Paul Skenes | PIT | 9.8 | 30 | $9.9 |
| Garrett Crochet | BOS | 12.0 | 113 | -$7.7 |
| Cristopher Sánchez | PHI | 25.3 | 10 | $21.8 |
| Yoshinobu Yamamoto | LAD | 26.5 | 3 | $30.6 |
| Bryan Woo | SEA | 35.3 | 32 | $9.5 |
| Logan Gilbert | SEA | 36.4 | 21 | $13.7 |
| Hunter Brown | HOU | 36.8 | 57 | $2.8 |
| Chris Sale | ATL | 39.1 | 4 | $28.5 |
| Cole Ragans | KC | 47.7 | 112 | -$7.6 |
| Jacob deGrom | TEX | 49.1 | 37 | $8.0 |
| Max Fried | NYY | 50.7 | 35 | $8.3 |
| Freddy Peralta | NYM | 56.9 | 86 | -$3.6 |
| Logan Webb | SF | 58.6 | 77 | -$0.5 |
SP Rank, $ Earned: FanGraphs Fantasy Player Rater
These are the pitchers with ADPs in the first five rounds of OCs. Ohtani could technically be excluded since he was mostly used as a hitter in NFBC formats last season. He did earn nearly $14, producing sparkling ratios (1.79 ERA, 0.95 WHIP) with 95 strikeouts in 85.2 innings (14 starts). Ohtani should pitch again next season, but will be a top-three consensus fantasy pick regardless. No matter where he signs, Skubal will be the first or second SP off draft boards, along with Misiorowski. Sale, Yamamoto and Cristopher Sánchez will likely live in the Round 2 range. Sale was the SP3 in 2024, SP20 in 2025 and SP4 in 2026. Yamamoto was the SP7 and SP3 in his first two full Major League seasons. Sánchez has posted consecutive seasons of 200+ innings and a sub-3.00 ERA. Hunter Brown will be a polarizing pick in the Rounds 4-7 range coming off a 20-start season where he produced a strong 3.19 ERA, but saw his WHIP and walk rate balloon from the previous season — from 1.03 and 7.8% to 1.27 and 12.2%.
A fantasy bust in 2026, Freddy Peralta is quickly surging back up confidence meters and draft boards with his dominant playoff performances. Bryan Woo and Logan Gilbert will be slightly discounted coming off disappointing seasons, but T-Mobile Park in Seattle remains advantageous to starting pitchers (30-of-30 in MLB Park Factor for hits in 2026) and bounce-backs wouldn’t be shocking, assuming good health. Ragans underwent UCL repair surgery in July and has a 10-12 month return timetable, so he’s off our radars for the forseeable future. Jacob deGrom was slightly more human in his age-38 season, posting a career-worst 4.20 ERA, albeit with a 3.11 FIP, 3.14 xFIP and 3.15 SIERA.
Fried’s UCL is “in a good place” according to NY Daily News writer, Gary Phillips. Logan Webb is no longer the position’s Iron Man and could fall out of the top 100 ADP, though he will always have supporters. A healthy Webb could provide profit at a reasonable cost.
| Player | Team | ADP | SP Rank | $ Earned |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| George Kirby | SEA | 65.8 | 111 | -$7.6 |
| Jesús Luzardo | PHI | 71.5 | 7 | $22.9 |
| Kyle Bradish | BAL | 72.3 | 119 | -$8.2 |
| Dylan Cease | TOR | 76.0 | 6 | $23.5 |
| Joe Ryan | MIN | 76.8 | 48 | $4.3 |
| Eury Pérez | MIA | 80.0 | 54 | $3.4 |
| Framber Valdez | DET | 83.7 | 87 | -$4.1 |
| Nolan McLean | NYM | 88.5 | 20 | $13.9 |
| Nick Pivetta | SD | 96.0 | 78 | -$0.6 |
| Chase Burns | CIN | 107.0 | 13 | $18.1 |
| Zack Wheeler | PHI | 112.8 | 11 | $20.8 |
| Tyler Glasnow | LAD | 114.7 | 46 | $5.2 |
| Kevin Gausman | TOR | 115.0 | 84 | -$2.4 |
| Emmet Sheehan | LAD | 115.1 | 81 | -$1.7 |
| Jacob Misiorowski | MLW | 115.8 | 1 | $43.2 |
| Cam Schlittler | NYY | 119.2 | 2 | $37.1 |
SP Rank, $ Earned: FanGraphs Fantasy Player Rater
The 61-120 ADP range was quite the mixed bag.
Dylan Cease and Jesús Luzardo were studs and will be drafted in the top 50 in most formats.
Wheeler recovered thoroughly from his thoracic outlet procedure and produced yet another $20+ season: 162 IP (28 starts) – 193 K – 14 W – 3.00 – 1.05. He has been the best pitcher in the Majors since 2021, leading in wins (79), ERA (2.92) and second in strikeouts (1,234) behind Cease’s 1,345.
Chase Burns will be highly coveted after his masterful performance over his first full season (154.1 IP – 185 K – 15 W – 2.86 – 1.17) and will be drafted among the top 12 to 15 starters. Nolan McLean will be slightly cheaper than Burns after his first full and successful season in the Majors. Cases made against either this offseason will start with concerns about their lack of elite control and potential WHIP damage at Tier 2 SP prices. Eury Pérez is in this boat as well after posting a 10.3% walk rate and a 1.21 WHIP, though don’t expect to pay anything but a premium for the coveted fireballer who will turn 24 in April.
Joe Ryan should be a solid pick among the top 100 as well. Though he may never have that 180+ IP dream season where good health and all the cards align, Ryan has been a dependable fantasy stud, posting a K-BB% over 20% for four straight seasons and has made between 23 and 30 starts over his first five full seasons.
There were quite a few negative value guys in this range, which was quite shocking for some: George Kirby, Kyle Bradish, Framber Valdez, Kevin Gausman and Emmet Sheehan. Kirby is quickly becoming persona non grata in the fantasy community, posting a painful 1.40 WHIP last season and two straight years with a 4.00+ ERA. Bradish’s WHIP (1.42) was even worse than Kirby’s as he did most of his damage after the All-Star break, posting a 5.29 ERA and a .398 wOBA in those final 10 starts before getting shelved due to lower abdominal pain and being diagnosed with a sports hernia. Gausman compiled 30+ starts for a sixth consecutive season. Despite nearly all of his rate stats and underlying metrics matching last season’s, Gausman posted a 4.51 ERA, with an xFIP and SIERA over a full run lower. I’ll remind myself of how solid everything looked under the hood for Gausman and would consider targeting him again in 2027 drafts. Sheehan isn’t going to fly under the radar this draft season despite last year’s poor results. The key here, of course, is Sheehan having a rotation spot. He dominated in his time down in Triple-A and fired three gems for the Dodgers in September (0.53 ERA, 24:3 K:BB in 17 innings/3 starts).
| Player | Team | ADP | SP Rank | $ Earned |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Spencer Strider | ATL | 123.2 | 93 | -$5.6 |
| Michael King | SD | 129.5 | 25 | $11.0 |
| Nick Lodolo | CIN | 130.5 | 150 | -$14.8 |
| Ryan Pepiot | TB | 132.6 | 164 | N/A |
| Brandon Woodruff | MLW | 134.9 | 73 | $0.6 |
| Nathan Eovaldi | TEX | 135.5 | 56 | $2.9 |
| Drew Rasmussen | TB | 137.4 | 5 | $28.4 |
| Sonny Gray | BOS | 138.1 | 12 | $20.1 |
| Gavin Williams | CLE | 144.3 | 15 | $16.9 |
| Sandy Alcantara | MIA | 145.2 | 49 | $4.3 |
| Bubba Chandler | PIT | 149.7 | 125 | -$8.6 |
| Trevor Rogers | BAL | 149.9 | 53 | $3.6 |
| Shota Imanaga | CHC | 160.7 | 28 | $10.3 |
| Tatsuya Imai | HOU | 162.9 | 94 | -$5.6 |
| Blake Snell | LAD | 163.6 | 61 | $2.2 |
| Robbie Ray | SF | 164.8 | 58 | $2.6 |
| MacKenzie Gore | TEX | 167.5 | 97 | -$6.0 |
| Luis Castillo | SEA | 171.3 | 159 | -$20.0 |
| Edward Cabrera | CHC | 176.7 | 143 | -$12.7 |
SP Rank, $ Earned: FanGraphs Fantasy Player Rater
The 120-180 ADP range was Landmine Central — pitchers like Castillo, Imai, and Chandler decimated our ratios. There were likely some folks who were duped for another round of category destruction when Castillo joined the White Sox. Castillo’s 5.85 ERA was third-worst among the 94 pitchers who threw at least 130 innings. The only ones worse were Kyle Freeland (6.65) and Jeffrey Springs (6.18). At least both of them had bad home parks as an excuse.
Rasmussen and Gray sported matching 2.72 ERAs and finished as top 12 starters. Both will be highly coveted by drafters and I’m sure that the Rasmussen helium will take soar him into the third round of 12-teamers, especially with the glow of playoff glory. Gray dazzled with a below-average strikeout rate of 21.8%, which was 6-7% lower than his two previous seasons in St. Louis. Because of some peripheral drop-offs and his age (36), don’t be surprised to see Gray fall into some offseason bust articles.
Imanaga had three massive disaster starts in the second half of May, but his overall production was strong and his control is on the border of elite. He posted a 5.2% walk rate and a 24.6% strikeout rate and owns a 19.4% K-BB% over three Major League seasons. He’s a free agent who the Cubs would love to re-sign, though we should expect the Padres to show strong interest. I’m definitely interested in Imanaga next season.
Robbie Ray is also a free agent who should generate offseason interest. He will certainly experience a price dip from the 100s to the 200s after a visit from the control boogie man (12% BB) last season.
Gavin Williams led the AL in strikeouts, fueled by an impressive 15% swinging-strike rate. More importantly, he reduced a near-12% walk rate down to below nine percent last season. Williams won’t be cheap in drafts, and rightfully so.
| Player | Team | ADP | SP Rank | $ Earned |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cade Horton | CHC | 180.1 | 92 | -$5.2 |
| Ranger Suarez | BOS | 182.8 | 44 | $6.5 |
| Trey Yesavage | TOR | 183.0 | 70 | $1.1 |
| Tanner Bibee | CLE | 187.9 | 88 | -$4.1 |
| Shane Baz | BAL | 189.6 | 106 | -$6.9 |
| Shane McClanahan | TB | 190.1 | 40 | $7.6 |
| Kris Bubic | KC | 195.3 | 83 | -$2.0 |
| Carlos Rodón | NYY | 199.7 | 42 | $7.6 |
| Aaron Nola | PHI | 206.2 | 116 | -$8.0 |
| Hunter Greene | CIN | 211.6 | 124 | -$8.6 |
| Jack Flaherty | DET | 212.8 | 109 | -$7.2 |
| Matthew Boyd | CHC | 217.3 | 62 | $1.8 |
| Andrew Abbott | CIN | 220.3 | 148 | -$13.9 |
| Zac Gallen | ARZ | 223.0 | 162 | -$21.3 |
| Kodai Senga | NYM | 231.2 | 153 | -$16.3 |
| Jack Leiter | TEX | 232.0 | 131 | -$10.8 |
| Ryan Weathers | NYY | 237.1 | 67 | $1.2 |
SP Rank, $ Earned: FanGraphs Fantasy Player Rater
There were some stretches of fantasy usefulness from several in this tier, but no big payoffs. Ryan Weathers’ first season in the AL was a roller coaster ride, but mostly positive. He finished the season with a 3.60 ERA aligned with peripherals (3.50 SIERA, 3.44 xFIP), a 1.22 WHIP, and a 18.5% K-BB%. His roto value was weighed down by just five victories. Carlos Rodón was a properly discounted stash who was activated on May 10 and pitched nine starts before elbow inflammation reappeared and he missed two months of the summer. The end-of-season line was good (2.67 ERA, 1.06 WHIP, 26.8% K in 16 starts). His 11.2% walk rate wasn’t and it was his first season over 10% in the post-Covid era. An air of trepidation will likely always remain for Rodón because of his elbow, which may result in a 2027 discount, with profitability a likely outcome if his UCL stays intact.
Jack Flaherty and Zac Gallen are falling semi-stars who were unmitigated disasters last season. Gallen finished with a 3-9 record and a 6.07 ERA in 105.1 innings. Flaherty threw just 88.1 innings and had a 4.48 ERA with his typical high strikeout rate (26%). Flaherty and Gallen are both free agents. They’ll be more appealing to real-life teams than to fantasy managers.
Tanner Bibee makes 30 starts a season, but is essentially just a thrower now. He has posted an ERA over 4.00 for a second straight season and has seen his strikeout rate reduced in three consecutive seasons — from 26.3% to 21.3% to 19%. Bibee has three years left on his 5yr, $45M deal.
Trey Yesavage was certainly trending toward Miz and Schlittler range this winter and early spring, earning a minimum pick of 113 in Online Championships. Yesavage ADP helium was quickly popped a week before Opening Day because of right shoulder impingement. In the Too Early Meatball draft in August, Yesavage was drafted in the 15th round, and this is a 15-team format. It would hard to imagine Yesavage not rising up boards back into the top 150 overall. He has a spot in the Jays rotation so all he needs know is to stay healthy.
| Player | Team | ADP | SP Rank | $ Earned |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Gerrit Cole | NYY | 241.1 | 36 | $8.3 |
| Braxton Ashcraft | PIT | 246.6 | 19 | $14.0 |
| Mike Burrows | HOU | 248.0 | 156 | -$17.5 |
| Shane Smith | CWS | 248.3 | 135 | -$11.1 |
| Ryne Nelson | ARZ | 254.0 | 126 | -$8.7 |

A long list of names, so we’ll just touch on a few of them. Among the studs who provided tremendous profit were Cade Cavalli, Reid Detmers, Nick Martinez, Payton Tolle, and the impenetrable Eduardo Rodriguez, who pulled off 17 wins with a 2.89 ERA despite a much higher xFIP (4.44) and SIERA (4.62) and the lowest BABIP (.274 of his career). I don’t usually mess with the peripheral gods and will stubbornly skip over him in early drafts. Cade Cavalli had an epic run after the All-Star break, posting a 90:16 K:BB and a 1.90 ERA over his final 12 starts. Reid Detmers was having a decent season, but really began to shine when the Angels fired pitching coach Mike Maddux. Over those final 8 starts, Detmers posted a 4-0 record with a 1.62 ERA and an impressive 55:5 K:BB. Angels fans are hoping that the new regime under new owner Stan Kroenke will bring the organization from the basement to at least the living room. Interim GM John Mozeliak will stay in the role for now and help the Angels find a permanent GM and a new manager, since Kurt Suzuki is one-and-done.
A $1.20 earning shouldn’t detract from the admiration that Clay Holmes should receive after Round 15 in 12-teamers. He produced a respectable 3.29 ERA, but his low value was impacted by a low strikeout rate (18.6%), six wins, and time spent on the IL, which led to just 18 starts on the season. Michael Wacha was stellar yet again, earning $10 in 12-team NFBC roto leagues as the SP29. Taj Bradley, Troy Melton, Ian Seymour, Justin Wrobleski, and Michael Soroka all had some strong stretches of production that helped fantasy managers, especially those who got out of the Wrobleski business before that ship began to sank. Seymour and Melton are already earning some early 2027 draft love, getting scooped up among the top 50 starters in the 150-175 ADP range — a price that is likely to surge as we move through the heart of draft season.
Finally, a shout out to FAAB stud Sean Burke who broke out in a big way. He produced a 3.34 ERA, a 1.20 WHIP and punched out 185 batters over 172.1 innings. Burke had a scorching-hot nine-start run from June 18 through August 11 where he rocked a 1.60 ERA and struck out 79, with just 11 walks over 62 innings. He had some rough starts, but was still worth every free agent penny. Based on some of the prices (2-5% of budget), it almost felt like pennies were what were being spent.
It’s always a good idea to dig into player stats not long after the season has ended. It helps avoid building biases that may fester, resonate, and solidify within our draft tendencies for the coming draft season. When we wait too long into the winter to review individual player profiles, we increase the likelihood of outside influences manipulating our valuations of players — whether it’s articles that do a good job of convincing a player is a boon or a bust, social media bandwaggoning, or ADP data itself. We don’t have to decide between Ashcraft and McLean now, but if we’re equipped with the details of their stats, underlying metrics, velocity trends, pitch mix changes, Stuff, and healthy history, we can limit emotion and bias from our decision-making and make optimal, objective decisions during the heart of draft season.
Vlad writes for RotoGraphs and is the head of fantasy baseball content at FTN Fantasy. He is a Tout Wars Expert League champ, member of the CDM Fantasy Sports Hall of Fame and has been nominated for FSWA writing awards six times. Vlad has been playing fantasy baseball since 1995, winning 42 NFBC leagues since 2012 and ranking in the top percentile in NFBC’s Online Championship contest (33% win rate, 52% cash rate; 64 leagues). Much to the chagrin of his colleagues and most baseball aficionados, Vlad is a lifelong Dodgers fan who claims his first gut call at age 9 was Kirk Gibson’s 1988 World Series home run. You can follow him on X and BlueSky @RotoGut.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Max Fried’s elbow news is good, but Yankees still need cover
item.dc:creator: Alexander Wilson
item.description: Max Fried's follow-up imaging brought the Yankees encouraging news. I would take the relief without allowing it to become the argument against adding another credible starter this winter. Aaron Boone said Fried was recently re-imaged after dealing with a left elbow bone bruise and described the ligament as being in a good place, MLB.com's Bryan Hoch reported Wednesday. No surgical procedure was scheduled for him in that update. The Yankees got quality, but only 20 starts Fried finished 2026 with
item.content:encoded:
Max Fried's follow-up imaging brought the Yankees encouraging news. I would take the relief without allowing it to become the argument against adding another credible starter this winter.
Aaron Boone said Fried was recently re-imaged after dealing with a left elbow bone bruise and described the ligament as being in a good place, MLB.com's Bryan Hoch reported Wednesday. No surgical procedure was scheduled for him in that update.
The Yankees got quality, but only 20 starts
Fried finished 2026 with a 2.80 ERA, 0.99 WHIP and 104 strikeouts against 33 walks in 112 2/3 innings. Those aren't the numbers of a pitcher whose ability needs rescuing.
He also made 20 starts. The Yankees needed other pitchers to cover the rest of the schedule, and a reassuring October examination can't guarantee how much work any starter will handle next year. The quality and the workload belong in the same evaluation.
Depth doesn't require a headline signing
I'd want New York to add a pitcher it would be comfortable actually starting, rather than count a collection of emergency options as a finished depth plan. That could come through a modest acquisition or a legitimate internal competition. It doesn't have to be an expensive name or a trade that creates a different weakness.
The practical goal is a sixth starter with a believable path to useful innings. Such a pitcher could cover an absence, make it easier to manage workloads or prevent the club from rushing another arm simply because the schedule needs someone that night.
0What do you think?Post a comment.
There is a sensible case for spending most of the available resources on hitting and trusting younger pitchers to supply the extra starts. That approach becomes more attractive if the internal options show enough to deserve it. I wouldn't rule it out before seeing the actual cost of an addition.
What I wouldn't accept is substituting good health news for that evaluation. We don't have the medical records, and this isn't a prediction that Fried will get hurt again. His 2026 performance supports counting on his talent; his 20-start workload supports preparing for the possibility that the club needs more innings elsewhere.
An improved offense and a properly stocked rotation are compatible winter goals. Fried shouldn't have to make every scheduled turn for both plans to work.

item.content:encoded:
Needing reinforcements at third base and behind the plate, the New York Yankees acquired Luis Garcia Jr. from the Washington Nationals at the most recent trade deadline. All of this so he could play first base, even though Ben Rice and Paul Goldschmidt were already in those positions.
This means the Yankees still have a surplus at third base heading into the 2027 season—even if Goldy is no longer on the roster.
And that's why, during a media session yesterday (Wednesday), manager Aaron Boone said it's possible that Garcia Jr. could play some second base next year.
Yankees Notes: Giancarlo Stanton's status, Luis Garcia Jr. is a possibility at second base https://t.co/wlB0wxVlAm
— SNY (@SNYtv) October 21, 2026
That would solve quite a few problems in the Bronx, since with Jazz Chisholm Jr.'s departure and the surplus at first base, the Yankees were left with a problem in the infield.
Admittedly, Garcia won't be as solid defensively at second base. In fact, the 26-year-old posted +2 defensive runs saved and +3 above-average outs in 985 and two-thirds innings at first base this year. Conversely, he posted a dismal -29 DRS and -18 OAA in 4,189 career innings at second base.
However, it wasn't defense that sank the Big Apple's team in 2026, but rather a lack of offense. And having García in the lineup at a position other than first base would help spark a strong comeback in that area.
After joining the Yankees, García batted .264 with seven home runs and 16 RBIs in 43 regular-season games. He then added four hits and a home run during the postseason.

item.content:encoded:
Yankees' Aaron Boone, Brian Cashman returns lead insider to admit 'change was necessary' appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The New York Yankees lost to the Tampa Bay Rays in the ALDS, marking another year under manager Aaron Boone and GM Brian Cashman in which the team failed to win a World Series. The team has not won the World Series since 2009 and, while they have made the playoffs in eight of nine seasons under Boone, they have been to just one World Series. Still, owner Hal Steinbrenner is backing Boone and Cashman, while blaming the players for the latest early exit.
Now, MLB insider Ken Rosenthal is saying maybe it was time for a change, speaking on Foul Territory.
"I understand the frustration of Yankees fans who are asking, 'What are we doing? Why are we doing this over and over again when it's the same ending every year?' Hal Steinbrenner, the owner, put it on the players, blaming the hitters yesterday. Well, who picks the hitters? That's Cashman. Who manages the hitters? That's Boone," Rosenthal said. "I don't know. I don't advocate, or I don't like to advocate for people getting fired, but in this particular case, it just seemed like change was necessary, and it sure seemed like at some point, you can't let the fans run the team, but their fans are so exasperated by what has happened in recent years, maybe their voice needs to be heard in a greater way than it has been."
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
With the lack of a World Series title this year, the Yankees have tied their longest streak between World Series wins. The Yankees went from 1979 through 1995 without a title, 17 seasons. The current streak is from 2010 through 2026, another 17 seasons. Now, fans are getting tired of the same thing every season. Steinbrenner still says his goal is a World Series, but his actions are saying something different.
Related: Aaron Boone hoping Yankees will 'bully' their way to 2027 World Series

item.title: [La Prensa Panamá] Calicho Ruiz y Mariano Rivera están en el equipo ideal de la Serie Mundial del siglo XXI
item.dc:creator: Humberto Cornejo
item.description: El Clásico de Otoño comenzará este viernes en el American Family Field, y los nombres de Carlos “Calicho” Ruiz y Mariano Rivera vuelven a destacar entre las figuras históricas del béisbol de las Grandes Ligas. Los dos panameños fueron incluidos por FOX Sports en su selección ideal de la Serie Mundial del siglo XXI, una nómina de 26 jugadores que reúne a peloteros de la Liga Americana y la Liga Nacional por sus actuaciones en el Clásico de Otoño. Ruiz aparece como el receptor titular de la alinea
item.content:encoded:
El Clásico de Otoño comenzará este viernes en el American Family Field, y los nombres de Carlos “Calicho” Ruiz y Mariano Rivera vuelven a destacar entre las figuras históricas del béisbol de las Grandes Ligas. Los dos panameños fueron incluidos por FOX Sports en su selección ideal de la Serie Mundial del siglo XXI, una nómina de 26 jugadores que reúne a peloteros de la Liga Americana y la Liga Nacional por sus actuaciones en el Clásico de Otoño.
Ruiz aparece como el receptor titular de la alineación, mientras que Rivera fue elegido como cerrador. La presencia de ambos en este listado reconoce el impacto que tuvieron con los Filis de Filadelfia y los Yankees de Nueva York, respectivamente, durante una época marcada por sus éxitos en la postemporada.
La selección de FOX Sports se conoce en la antesala de la Serie Mundial de 2026, que comenzará este viernes 23 de octubre con el primer partido entre los Rays de Tampa Bay y los Cerveceros de Milwaukee, en el American Family Field, a las 7:00 p. m., hora de Panamá.
Ruiz, el receptor titular
El portal deportivo destacó la actuación de Ruiz durante la etapa más exitosa de los Filis en la postemporada. El panameño fue el receptor de cinco equipos consecutivos de Filadelfia que disputaron los playoffs entre 2007 y 2011, periodo que incluyó dos apariciones consecutivas en la Serie Mundial, en 2008 y 2009.
En la edición de 2008, los Filis vencieron a los Rays en cinco partidos para conquistar el título. Durante aquella postemporada, Ruiz también registró una destacada producción ofensiva. En la Serie Mundial de 2009, Filadelfia cayó ante los Yankees de Nueva York. En ambas finales, el istmeño acumuló un promedio de bateo de .353, dos jonrones y cinco carreras impulsadas en 11 partidos.
El receptor jugó 12 temporadas en las Grandes Ligas, 11 de ellas con los Filis. También vistió los uniformes de los Dodgers de Los Ángeles y los Marineros de Seattle, equipo con el que puso fin a su carrera en 2017.
Rivera, el cerrador de la selección
En el caso de Rivera, FOX Sports resaltó su dominio como relevista en el escenario más importante del béisbol. El panameño registró una efectividad de 0.99 en 36 entradas y un tercio de labor en la Serie Mundial, una cifra que refleja su consistencia en sus apariciones en el Clásico de Otoño.
Rivera participó en siete Series Mundiales y acumuló 11 salvamentos, según las estadísticas consignadas en el texto original. Su efectividad de 0.99 en 36 entradas y un tercio lo sitúa entre los relevistas más dominantes en la historia de estas finales.
El legendario cerrador disputó 19 temporadas en las Grandes Ligas, todas con los Yankees de Nueva York, y terminó su carrera con 652 salvamentos, la mayor cantidad en la historia de las Mayores. En 2019 ingresó de manera unánime al Salón de la Fama del Béisbol.
La inclusión de Ruiz y Rivera en esta selección vuelve a poner de relieve el lugar de Panamá en la historia de las Grandes Ligas. Ambos fueron piezas determinantes en equipos campeones y dejaron una huella que trasciende sus estadísticas individuales.
Los otros 24 jugadores seleccionados por FOX Sports son Freddie Freeman, Chase Utley, David Freese, Derek Jeter, George Springer, Barry Bonds, Hideki Matsui, David Ortiz, Madison Bumgarner, Yadier Molina, Alex Rodríguez, Pablo Sandoval, Justin Turner, Corey Seager, Juan Soto, Jayson Werth, Curt Schilling, Jon Lester, Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Gerrit Cole, Chris Carpenter, Josh Beckett, Walker Buehler y Tim Lincecum.

item.dc:creator: Michael DeRosa

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees have multiple pending free agents heading into the offseason. However, there is no question that second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. is their most notable one.
Chisholm has been a very polarizing player for Yankees fans. At times, he was a major difference-maker for New York. This was especially the case during the 2025 season, as he posted 31 home runs and 31 stolen bases in 130 games.
Yet, Chisholm took a major step in the wrong direction and struggled badly this season. Because of this, there is a real expectation that the Yankees will let him leave in free agency.
Now, with Chisholm's future with the Yankees looking very murky, he is being predicted to sign with another American League team this offseason.
Yankees' Jazz Chisholm Jr. Predicted to Sign With AL Rival
In a recent article for Bleacher Report, Zach Buckley predicted that the Yankees will let Chisholm walk, and he will sign with the Los Angeles Angels in free agency this year.
"Jazz Chisholm Jr. has already expressed his desire to remain with the New York Yankees. Unfortunately for him, it continues to sound like that interest is not mutual," Buckley wrote. "Maybe if Chisholm was coming off of a stronger season, New York would have interest in keeping him around. But just about everything that could go wrong did, as his power regressed, his contact decreased and he battled both inconsistency and injury. He is a good bounce-back candidate for someone, but that someone won't be the Bombers. Prediction: Chisholm signs with the Los Angeles Angels."
It is not very difficult to understand why the Yankees are being predicted to let Chisholm leave in free agency. He had an ugly 2026 season, and it would make sense if New York let him leave because of it.
However, Chisholm choosing the Angels as his next team would be a surprising decision. The Angels were once again one of the worst teams in baseball this season. They also missed the playoffs for the 12th consecutive season. Thus, Chisholm would be joining a far worse team if he signed with the Angels.
Why Chisholm & the Angels Could Be a Great Match
Although the Angels are a lot worse than the Yankees, they could actually be a very good landing spot for Chisholm. Joining a team with far lower expectations and pressure could benefit Chisholm. This would allow him the opportunity to focus on bouncing back and get a fresh start.
Perhaps joining a team like the Angels could help Chisholm regain his elite form. If he signed with Los Angeles and had another 30-30 season, he would be a fantastic addition for them. Thus, it will be interesting to see if the Angels target the Yankees star from here.
This article was originally published on HEAVY
The post Yankees' Jazz Chisholm Jr. Predicted to Sign With AL Rival in Shocking Move appeared first on HEAVY.

We’ll have coaches potentially on expiring contracts, front office, all those things. That’s life. That’s part of it.” After a second c
item.content:encoded:
Aaron Boone isn’t uncomfortable with the uncertainty.
For the second time in four seasons, Boone is set to manage the Yankees on an expiring contract, leaving his future beyond 2027 very much up in the air.
“Doesn’t bother me at all,” Boone said Wednesday during an end-of-season video call.
“We’ll have players that are free-agents-to-be at the end of the season. We’ll have coaches potentially on expiring contracts, front office, all those things. That’s life. That’s part of it.”
After a second consecutive ALDS loss to a division rival, the Yankees decided to bring Boone back next season for the final year of his contract but have not discussed an extension with their longtime manager.
In the final guaranteed year of his previous deal, Boone took the Yankees to the 2024 World Series. The Yankees then picked up his 2025 club option before signing him to an extension through the 2027 season.
Pressure has only mounted since then, with the Yankees now on a 17-year championship drought, including the past nine years under Boone.
This was the sixth year in a row that the Yankees failed to defeat a higher-seeded playoff opponent.
“I believe it can happen with me at the helm, but any answer I give in defense of that isn’t going to be a great one or satisfy people,” Boone said.
“I think I’m good at my job,” he said. “I think we have a lot of the right people in the building, but at the end of the day, we haven’t won a championship with me at the helm, and ultimately that’s what has to happen to satisfy, certainly, myself — like, that’s why I’m doing this — but to answer those questions.”
Owner Hal Steinbrenner acknowledged Wednesday that team brass had a week-long discussion about Boone following this month’s playoff loss to the Tampa Bay Rays and determined he wasn’t responsible for this season’s shortcomings.
Instead, Steinbrenner largely pinned the Yankees’ issues on an underperforming offense.
“I thought Boone managed a good season, especially with the pitching staff,” Steinbrenner said on a separate call.
“We had a lot of additions and subtractions in the rotation throughout the course of the season. Our bullpen was absolutely exhausted by the end of the season. He got through all that and he got us to the playoffs, and the bottom line is the players didn’t live up to their end of the bargain in the playoffs.”
Boone boasts a .583 winning percentage and eight playoff berths in his nine years on the job, including 2026, when the Yankees went 93-68 despite the prolonged injury absences of Aaron Judge and Giancarlo Stanton.
Judge and ace Cam Schlittler were among the prominent Yankees to vouch for Boone after their ALDS defeat.
Still, Boone is aware that the public’s perception of him hinges on whether he can finally win that elusive World Series.
“I want to be the best I can be at my job. That’s where my focus lies,” Boone said.
“If we don’t win a championship while I’m here, I’m sure that will be a frontline story of it all and how people think of me and how a fan base reacts. I understand that. I understood that when I took this job. I don’t define myself by how people look at me and judge me in my job. My job is to go be the best I can possibly be and try and get the most out of this club.”

item.content:encoded:
Wednesday was an eventful day for the New York Yankees as Hal Steinbrenner and Brian Cashman sat before reporters (well, via Zoom, anyway), followed by Aaron Boone. The trio's press conferences brought plenty of revelations (including Cashman's new deal), as well as injury updates on key Yankees players Aaron Judge, Max Fried, and Giancarlo Stanton.
We'll start with Judge, who took a dig from Steinbrenner on Wednesday when the owner not-so-subtly suggested that his superstar slugger fell below the expectations of a dutiful employee at the end of the campaign. But anyway ... how's Judge's body (that kept him out of the postseason) feeling these days?
Aaron Judge scheduled for follow-up appointment regarding rib injury; expected to be ready for Spring Training
Cashman revealed that Judge has a follow-up appointment scheduled with Dr. Gregory Pearl to inspect the healing process of the rib injury that cost Judge the bulk of the 2026 regular season. Cashman reiterated his prior stance that Judge wasn't physically capable of competing in the postseason, while also asserting that the offseason should allow Judge to heal fully, rest, and be ready for 2027.
Max Fried won't need surgery to address bone bruises
According to Boone on Wednesday, no Yankees player is in need of surgery this offseason, including Judge and Fried, the latter of whom increasingly suffered from left elbow bone bruises in 2026. Fried recently had the elbow re-imaged (per Boone), and the ligament is apparently in a good place.
Fried did undergo Tommy John surgery back in 2014, which presented a reason to fear that his recurring elbow problem this season might lead to another going-under-the-knife. He spent two separate stints on the IL this season (in May and August) for the same bone bruise issue. But according to Boone, Fried is all in the clear heading into the winter!
Giancarlo Stanton is healthy, but his future Yankees role sounds uncertain
Of course Stanton is healthy now that the Yankees' season isn't happening! Stanton appeared in just 24 games out of 162 for the Yanks in the 2026 due to multiple calf ailments. He made a couple of cameos as a pinch hitter in the postseason but wasn't able to deliver (not an easy ask, given how much time he spent away from game action).
Beyond discussing Stanton's health status, Cashman also interestingly noted that the Yankees' designated hitter spot is up for grabs. It sounds like the Yankees have finally opened themselves up to the possibility that Stanton should be cast aside ... or at least not prioritized.
The 36-year-old slugger is entering the final guaranteed year of his contract in 2027. The Yankees figure to have something of a logjam at DH if Stanton remains healthy. Ben Rice, Luis García Jr. (provided he's still on the team), and Judge will all needs reps at DH next season.

item.content:encoded:
When the Yankees announced they were bringing back Paul Goldschmidt for 2026, it went down somewhat like a lead balloon. He had gotten off to a nice start in 2025, but fell off down the stretch. That along with Ben Rice’s emergence seemingly made him expendable for 2026.
However, the Yankees opted to give him another year. In fairness, he did hit lefties quite well. He just ended up playing a bit more than ideal, dragging down his overall numbers. That being said, he was more than servicable in 2026 and hardly the roster’s main problem.
Grade: B
2026 Statistics: 105 games, 380 plate appearances, .252/.313/.452, 18 HR, 52 RBI, 111 wRC+, 1.6 fWAR
2027 Contract Status: Free agent
Initially, Goldschmidt was used mainly in just a platoon fashion. Through the end of May, he had appeared in 34 of the Yankees’ 59 games. Once again, he got off to a very nice start, posting a .261/.354/.496 slash line. Between injuries elsewhere in the lineup and the Yankees relying on him more after that hot start, he ended up appearing in 71 of the final 102 games.
In the end, the breakdown of his number of plate appearances against different handed pitchers didn’t end up being that drastic a difference. Of his 380 PAs, 183 were against lefties and 197 against righties. He was never going to only ever face lefties because that’s generally just not feasible, but the ideal plan probably wouldn’t have included that many against righties. Further evidence of that is that he posted a genuinely very good .967 OPS against lefties, compared to .590 against righties.
Goldschmidt had his moments over the course of the season. On June 13th in Toronto, he hit a go-ahead home run off the Blue Jays’ Louis Varland that ended up providing the final difference in a win.
It should be noted that Varland is a righty, so while his splits were drastic this season, playing him against righties wasn’t completely irredeemable. Additionally, Varland was also one of the best relievers in all of baseball this season and will probably get a non-zero number of votes in the AL Cy Young Award race this year. In general, Goldschmidt was a perfectly fine bench bat/platoon guy to have around. He just ended up getting used more than the Yankees planned on.
Now as we look ahead to the future, it’s difficult to make any legitimate argument to bringing Goldschmidt back again. His contract for 2026 was only one year. Goldschmidt himself wants to play on past this season. Between the way he hit lefties and the fact that he’s still a perfectly solid defender at first base, there will still probably be teams out there willing to give him another one-year contract for 2027.
However, when it comes to the Yankees, they got an even bigger breakout season from Ben Rice. They also acquired Luis García Jr. at the Trade Deadline. While García has opposite splits to Goldschmidt, he’ll also be getting games at first base. The team still hasn’t made a decision in regards to Giancarlo Stanton, and they’re also coming off a season when Aaron Judge missed a lot of time, so they might use him more at the DH spot. While the Yankees figured it out in 2026, there will be more to figure out in regards to Goldschmidt’s playable spots for 2027. I could totally picture Goldy OPSing .800+ against lefties again next year, but it’s probably for the best if he does so elsewhere.
Paul Goldschmidt is a likely future Hall of Famer. While his time with the Yankees was far too brief and far too insignificant compared to the rest of his career for him to go in as one, he’s been nice to have around for the past two seasons.

item.title: [Empire Sports Media] Yankees can move Luis Garcia back to second, with a catch
item.dc:creator: Alexander Wilson
item.description: Second base is an option again for Luis Garcia Jr., but the Yankees would be making a defensive bet, not simply finding a spot for 30 home runs. A return is worth exploring before buying another infielder. His bat shouldn’t win him the job by itself. Aaron Boone acknowledged that possibility during Wednesday’s season-ending news conference, according to SNY’s Phillip Martinez. He also made clear that winter acquisitions could change the thinking. The Yankees haven’t announced a position change o
item.content:encoded:
Second base is an option again for Luis Garcia Jr., but the Yankees would be making a defensive bet, not simply finding a spot for 30 home runs. A return is worth exploring before buying another infielder. His bat shouldn’t win him the job by itself.
Aaron Boone acknowledged that possibility during Wednesday’s season-ending news conference, according to SNY’s Phillip Martinez. He also made clear that winter acquisitions could change the thinking. The Yankees haven’t announced a position change or settled their 2027 infield.
The Yankees wouldn’t be teaching him a new position
Garcia played 508 games at second, including 480 starts, from 2020 through 2025. He spent 2026 at first base and designated hitter. His 37 starts at first for New York don’t erase that earlier experience, although a full season away makes the defensive evaluation important.
The offensive appeal is easy to see. Across Washington and New York, he hit .277/.309/.521 with 30 home runs in 543 plate appearances. His Yankees portion was less explosive: .264/.302/.434 with seven homers in 169 plate appearances.
Both lines belong in the discussion. New York would be moving a productive hitter, not guaranteeing that the most exciting stretch of his season follows him to another position.
I’d want the club to evaluate his lateral movement, double-play work and throwing from second before organizing the rest of the winter around this idea. Familiarity with the position helps. It doesn’t answer how well he can play it now.
A position switch moves the next decision, too
Garcia at second would create more room at first, rather than eliminate the need to decide who plays there. The Yankees would have to compare the whole infield they could assemble, including the defensive cost of the move, against keeping him at first and acquiring a second baseman.
That alternative may win. A dependable defender at second could be worth paying for if Garcia’s work there isn’t convincing. Conversely, a successful return would give the front office more freedom to improve another position without sacrificing his offense.
Boone’s opening is useful because it gives the Yankees something concrete to investigate. I would make the glove earn the move before letting the savings determine the answer.
More about:New York Yankees

Hal placed the blame for a disappointing season at the feet of the players on the roster, especially a "de
item.content:encoded:
New York Post | Grace McCarron: Hal Steinbrenner held court yesterday with members of the Yankee beat, albeit by Zoom which in and of itself is an interesting decision. The managing partner of the Yankees publicly backed GM Brian Cashman and manager Aaron Boone, proclaiming that both men did their jobs in the 2026 season and publicly announcing that Cashman's new contract is all but signed. Hal placed the blame for a disappointing season at the feet of the players on the roster, especially a "detrimental" offense.
New York Daily News | Gary Phillips: Continuing with the Steinbrenner Address, Hal was asked directly about comments made by current and former Yankees regarding the now-17 year World Series drought. In particular, he seemed to be a little chesty about Aaron Judge's remarks that the team hasn't gone "all in" and should, with George's son pointing to the richest payroll in franchise history as evidence of his commitment. If Judge was more of an extrovert he might point across boroughs to another team that spends like mad and doesn't have the results expected as an example that money misallocated is as bad as money unspent.
SNY | Danny Abriano: Finally, Mr. Steinbrenner set the table as one of the more powerful owners in baseball, admitting that he'd like to see a salary cap implemented in this round of CBA negotiations. It's the most important thing for the group of thirty monopolists, and it needs to be the most important thing for the union to remember too.
NBC Sports | Eric Samulski: We also got news that Aaron Judge's rib is still a bit of a question mark. The Yankee captain will have followup tests and surgery seems unnecessary, Brian Cashman telling us that he expects Judge to be ready in time for Spring Training, whenever that is.
FanGraphs | Ben Clemens: We get a final piece that's a little more pan-baseball, with the Fielding Bible Awards being announced today at 3 p.m. Eastern. Clemens gives us the breakdown of his ballot, with Cody Bellinger being his winner in left field, as a more-statistically-driven recognition of the best defender at each position.

New York Marathon’s 50th Anniversary Brings Out Hollywood Stars
A star-studded lineup of Hollywood actors, reality TV favorites, and sports legends is lacing up to tackle the New York City Marathon.
Organizers announced that this year's landmark 50th-anniversary race will feature a massive celebrity roster.
Among the famous runners are Academy Award winner Jennifer Connelly, Vinny from the Jersey Shore, New York Giants legend Tiki Barber, and former AEW world champion Darby Allin.
“The TCS New York City Marathon brings together people from around the globe, and our incredible lineup of celebrity runners helps shine a spotlight on the sport and the power of movement to inspire and connect people,” New York Road Runners CEO Rob Simmelkjaer stated.
Other notable names include Dylan Efron, Zach’s brother, who made a name for himself on Traitors (a show I love) and Dancing with the Stars, ABC News anchor Liz Cho, Nev Schulman, the creator of MTV’s Catfish, and Survivor winner Kyle Frazer.
I mention Kyle because he just recovered from a torn Achilles, which he tore last June during his second season on the hit show.
I tore my Achilles recently; a major milestone of my recovery was running in a local charity 5K.
60,000 Expected Runners
This year, 60,000 will participate in the 26.2-mile journey through the five boroughs on Nov. 1

item.title: [KTVN] Steinbrenner blames Yankees players for lack of World Series title, defends Boone and Cashman
item.dc:creator: RONALD BLUM
item.description: Yankees owner Hal Steinbrenner blamed New York's players for the team's failure to win the World Series and defended manager Aaron Boone and general manager Brian Cashman, who is getting a new contract as he enters his 30th season in charge of baseball operations. “I thought Boone managed a good season, especially with the pitching staff," Steinbrenner said Wednesday. "The bottom line is the players didn’t live up to their end of the bargain in the playoffs.” New York has gone 17 seasons without
item.content:encoded:
Yankees owner Hal Steinbrenner blamed New York's players for the team's failure to win the World Series and defended manager Aaron Boone and general manager Brian Cashman, who is getting a new contract as he enters his 30th season in charge of baseball operations.
“I thought Boone managed a good season, especially with the pitching staff," Steinbrenner said Wednesday. "The bottom line is the players didn’t live up to their end of the bargain in the playoffs.”
New York has gone 17 seasons without a World Series title. That matches the Yankees' longest drought since winning their first championship in 1923, a gap between titles in 1978 and ’96.
“If we don’t win a championship while I’m here, I’m sure that will be a frontline story of it all and how people think of me and how a fanbase reacts,” Boone said. "I understand that.”
Steinbrenner spoke alongside Cashman during a joint Zoom news conference from team's spring training ballpark in Tampa, Florida, and Boone followed with a video news conference from Yankee Stadium.
New York went 93-68 and finished second in the AL East to Tampa Bay. After sweeping Boston 2-0 in an AL Wild Card Series, the Yankees were swept 3-0 by the Rays in a Division Series.
“In the end, the majority of the responsibility — I’ll say it for the fifth time — in my mind, my opinion, lies with the position players and the inability to score on a consistent basis throughout the course of the entire season for the most part,” Steinbrenner said. “Not on the shoulders of Aaron Boone does the blame lie.”
Captain Aaron Judge was limited to 66 games and hit .241 with 18 homers and 41 RBIs. The three-time AL MVP was sidelined from June 1 through Sept. 7 by a fractured rib, returned for seven games, then had a season-ending calf injury.
Giancarlo Stanton's regular season ended with a calf injury on April 24.
“Look, losing Stanton and losing Judge for 80-plus percent of the season in the offense’s defense was not part of the plan and it certainly had an effect," Steinbrenner said. “We just have to figure out how much of it was that.”
He doesn't feel a need to publicly pressure players in the manner of his father, George Steinbrenner.
“I'm not convinced that with this team, in this day and age, that that’s as big of a motivator as you think it is,” Hal Steinbrenner said. “Twenty, 25 years ago, different generation, just a different scenario.”
Boone heads into last season of contract
Boone finished his ninth season as manager and has one season left on a two-year contract extension agreed to in February 2025. The 53-year-old former third baseman has led New York to a 790-565 regular-season record and three first-place finishes in the AL East but a 27-30 postseason mark.
"At the end of the day, we haven’t won a championship with me at the helm," he said. "Ultimately that’s what has to happen to satisfy certainly myself — that's why I'm doing this — but to answer those questions ultimately.”
Steinbrenner and the Yankees front office evaluated Boone after the season-ending loss.
"We had a weeklong conversation about Aaron Boone and was he part of the problem this year, and I don’t believe he was. I think he had a good year managing-wise," Steinbrenner said. “But, yes, I would consider, of course, moving on from Aaron Boone if I thought he was a huge part of a problem.”
Boone defended not calling out players publicly for mistakes.
“I know I get accused sometimes of being too positive in the media and I would say if you watch my post(game) conferences this year, there were a lot of days where I was talking about our struggles. But does that mean I’m calling individuals out in a public way?” Boone said. "There is probably a time and place for that, but generally speaking to me that’s not leadership. That’s me giving red meat to people that want to be upset with somebody.”
Cashman will stay on as GM
Cashman, who turns 60 in July, said he and the team have agreed to a new contract and are working on minor details. He became general manager in February 1998 and is the most senior head of baseball operations in the major leagues — San Diego’s A.J. Preller, hired in August 2014, is second.
When Cashman took over from Bob Watson in 1998, it was the 15th change at GM since George Steinbrenner bought the Yankees in January 1973. Cashman has been the only GM under Hal Steinbrenner, who succeeded his father as controlling owner in November 2008.
New York has won four World Series, seven AL pennants and 15 AL East titles since Cashman became GM. He had been working under a four-year contract announced in December 2022.
“Cash is great every season,” Steinbrenner said. “The roster he put together, the team that we rolled out of spring training with was as good as any in baseball in my opinion. We had a lot of bumps and bruises along the way, but the team was fantastic and it was a world championship-caliber team.”
Financing with affiliat
e of Apollo Global Management
Yankee Global Enterprises, the team's parent company, announced a $2.6 billion financing agreement in August with Apollo Sports Capital, an affiliate of Apollo Global Management. The deal included debt and equity.
“It is not a precursor to fully selling the team,” Steinbrenner said. “The whole goal of the Apollo deal was to bring in capital into the company that would be there for us, to give us more financial stability for years and years to come, including the years when I’m out of here and the third generation is running the team.”

item.title: [New York Daily News] Hal Steinbrenner responds to Aaron Judge’s insinuation Yankees haven’t been ‘all in’ enough: ‘We did that this year’
item.dc:creator: Gary Phillips
item.description: Shortly after the Yankees were swept by the Rays in the ALDS, Aaron Judge was asked how owner Hal Steinbrenner and general manager Brian Cashman should react to the team’s latest postseason failure. “We’re the Yankees,” said the back-to-back MVP, who was sidelined for the playoffs by a calf strain. “I feel like they should go all in and do what they need to do. If we got holes, it’s finding certain players or personnel, whatever we need, you gotta go out there and get it. That’s why I signed bac
item.content:encoded:
Shortly after the Yankees were swept by the Rays in the ALDS, Aaron Judge was asked how owner Hal Steinbrenner and general manager Brian Cashman should react to the team’s latest postseason failure.
“We’re the Yankees,” said the back-to-back MVP, who was sidelined for the playoffs by a calf strain. “I feel like they should go all in and do what they need to do. If we got holes, it’s finding certain players or personnel, whatever we need, you gotta go out there and get it. That’s why I signed back here to play with the Yankees, to fight for a championship every single year. We go all in. That’s what I do every offseason: get ready to give this team and the city everything I got. So I expect them to do the same.”
The captain’s response demanded a follow-up: does Judge feel the organization has gone all in enough during his 11-year, championship-less tenure?
“It’s tough to say,” Judge, 34, said after a long pause. “I want to trade for everybody and sign everybody every single year, but I know that’s not realistic. So they give us a winning team every single year, but that’s not good enough here in New York. We’re the Yankees. You gotta go out there and expect championships and go all in every year, so I’m excited to see what they do.”
On Wednesday, Steinbrenner addressed Judge’s pointed comments while conducting an autopsy of the Yankees’ shortcomings via Zoom. The owner said that he did not watch Judge’s full postgame interview after Game 3 of the ALDS, but a few of the slugger’s quotes were brought to his attention.
His reaction?
“Was I upset about it? No,” said Steinbrenner, who has a close relationship with Judge. “If I was a player, I would have expectations that my ownership group would do everything in their power every offseason to field a team that could win a championship. There’s nothing wrong with expectations. We did that this year. We had the highest payroll in the history of the organization. We got to a point later in the [last] offseason where we still felt we weren’t good enough, so we went out and signed [Cody] Bellinger to a huge contract. Glad we did. He’s a good player, so I definitely think we went all in this season. I definitely think we had a team that was every bit capable of winning a championship. No, it did not work out.
“And by the way, I have expectations of my players. I expect them to obey the rules, to work hard, to listen to their coaches and the trainers and the strength guys. Expectations are a good thing. Any relationship in life is a two-way street, and part of that is having expectations of each other. So no, I wasn’t bothered by it at all.”
As Steinbrenner alluded to, he financed a franchise record competitive balance tax payroll, projected to be $341.8 million, in 2026. That ranked third in baseball behind the Mets ($359.4 million) and Dodgers ($432.8 million), per Cot’s Contracts.
Judge, meanwhile, didn’t specify what he wanted the Yankees to do differently — or what he wants them to do going forward — after Game 3. He did, however, seem to take a shot at the Yankees’ so-called “run it back” approach — they retained a largely similar roster after getting bounced in the 2025 ALDS — despite endorsing the tactic in spring training and at the end of last year.
“The toughest thing is each year, besides us, every other team gets better,” Judge said. “Every other team’s adding new players, getting new coaches, new philosophies, things they can do to improve their team. So it’s not like, ‘Hey, we’re just going to run it back and we’ll be in the postseason.’”
While Judge didn’t vocalize his vision to reporters, Steinbrenner said that he and the right fielder had a “great conversation” on Tuesday that covered “a number of subjects.” The early offseason chats between owner and superstar have become an annual tradition, just like the Yankees’ premature playoff exits.
While Steinbrenner didn’t detail their most recent talk, he did say, “We’ve got some decisions that need to be made right after the World Series is over, essentially, and then some we have more time on. And [Judge is] going to be a part of all that. So, yeah, that’s the deal.”
Steinbrenner, speaking for himself, did take exception to the Yankees’ inconsistent offense this season, which he called “detrimental.” Of course, Judge’s injuries played a part in the lackluster performance, as he missed 99 days with a fractured rib and then the playoffs with his calf strain. But Steinbrenner believes the Yankees had enough talent to cover for Judge’s absences — Bellinger, Trent Grisham and Giancarlo Stanton also missed significant time — and so the club is going to look at potential changes to its coaching staff and hitting philosophies.
Some lineup turnover is also expected with Grisham and Jazz Chisholm Jr. headed for free agency.
“As a whole, they were very inconsistent when it came to run scoring,” Steinbrenner said, “and they were inconsistent for long periods of time.”
As for Judge’s injuries, those also became a point of contention between the player and the organization this year.
He repeatedly pushed to skip a rehab assignment when he returned from his rib injury and got his wish, but he only lasted seven games before suffering a moderate calf strain. Judge then seemed to take issue when Aaron Boone revealed the severity of his strain, and he said he wanted to make what would have been an expedited return for the Wild Card Series and ALDS.
Judge was left off both rosters. On Wednesday, Cashman said that there were no regrets on the Yankees’ end, as “he just wasn’t physically able to post for us” due to the calf strain.
Cashman, also on Wednesday’s Zoom, added that Judge underwent an end-of-season physical and that his rib “came out fine.” Judge has a follow-up scheduled with a specialist, Dr. Gregory Pearl, but the Yankees believe he’s in a strong spot health-wise.
“As of right now, we feel like we’re in a good place,” Cashman said, “and he can take advantage of the rest of the winter and be ready to go when spring training starts.”

item.title: [Heavy.com] Yankees Should Target 3 Free Agent Catchers To Pair With Austin Wells
item.dc:creator: Maria Aldrich
item.description: The New York Yankees continue to stand behind Austin Wells, who sputtered endlessly at the plate early on in his 2026 campaign. According to Joel Sherman of the New York Post, the organization isn’t planning to part ways with Wells. However, that doesn’t mean they won’t be looking for added insurance. Bearing this in mind, here are three free agents the Yankees could target. Yankees Should Target 3 Key Free Agent Catchers Ryan Jeffers This one shouldn’t come as a surprise — Ryan Jeffers has been
item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees continue to stand behind Austin Wells, who sputtered endlessly at the plate early on in his 2026 campaign.
According to Joel Sherman of the New York Post, the organization isn’t planning to part ways with Wells.
However, that doesn’t mean they won’t be looking for added insurance.
Bearing this in mind, here are three free agents the Yankees could target.
Yankees Should Target 3 Key Free Agent Catchers
Ryan Jeffers
This one shouldn’t come as a surprise — Ryan Jeffers has been floating in rumors for quite some time.
The 29-year-old Minnesota Twins catcher just wrapped up his seventh season in the major leagues.
His entire career has been spent with the Twins after they selected him with the No. 59 pick in the second round of the 2018 MLB draft. He made his debut in August 2020.
During Jeffers’ 2026 campaign, he slashed .256/.353/.461 with a career-high .814 OPS and 14 homers through 92 games.
Along the way, he posted 19 doubles, two triples and 56 RBIs.
Now an impending free agent, he’s considered one of the top catchers on the market after displaying productivity over the years.
It’s worth noting that he faced a drop in numbers after returning to the lineup. As for Wells, he improved as the season went by, not the other way around.
Of course, there’s still a chance Jeffers will remain in Minnesota as their homegrown player, but given New York’s situation, exploring the opportunity is worth it.
William Contreras
If the Yankees were to land 28-year-old William Contreras, they’d be in good hands.
The Milwaukee Brewers‘ catcher is gearing up for his World Series appearance this year.
In the postseason alone, he’s hitting .367/.457/.700 with a 1.157 OPS and three homers through eight games.
Looking at his regular season stat sheet, he slashed .270/.341/.417 with a .758 OPS and 18 homers through 147 games.
Wells’ defensive stats aren’t New York’s top concern — his offensive numbers are.
This is where having Contreras on board helps. His All-Star title backs him up.
But to land him, the Yankees will need to knock out their competition.
Gary Sánchez
Picking on Milwaukee again, 33-year-old Gary Sánchez is also approaching free agency.
With two Brewers catchers on the market as soon as the postseason concludes, New York has a glaring opportunity to bolster its roster with a catcher fresh out of the World Series.
Sánchez holds a few years over Contreras. He has 12 years under his belt, while Contreras has only seven.
Adding to the temptation, Sánchez is already familiar with New York’s organization.
He spent seven seasons with the Yankees after making his debut in October 2015.
Once March 2022 rolled around, they traded him to the Twins alongside Gio Urshela.
In return, New York received Josh Donaldson, Isiah Kiner-Falefa and Ben Rortvedt.
Having a recent World Series competitor combined with prior New York experience certainly wouldn’t hurt the ballclub.
Bottom line, the Yankees need to supplement Wells.
As always, their hot stove season is expected to be chaotic as they navigate free agency.

item.title: [Sporting News] Aaron Judge's front office statement should influence Yankees' offseason | Sporting News
item.dc:creator: Conor Liguori
item.description: Aaron Judge made his opinion clear after the New York Yankees were swept by the Tampa Bay Rays in the ALDS. "We're the Yankees. I feel we should go all-in and do what they need to do," Judge said. "If we got holes, if it's finding certain players or personnel, whatever we need, you got to go out there and get it. That's why I signed back here, to play with the Yankees, is to fight for a championship and go all in." Judge clearly wants the Yankees' front office -- mostly owner Hal Steinbrenner an
item.content:encoded:
Aaron Judge made his opinion clear after the New York Yankees were swept by the Tampa Bay Rays in the ALDS.
"We're the Yankees. I feel we should go all-in and do what they need to do," Judge said. "If we got holes, if it's finding certain players or personnel, whatever we need, you got to go out there and get it. That's why I signed back here, to play with the Yankees, is to fight for a championship and go all in."
Judge clearly wants the Yankees' front office -- mostly owner Hal Steinbrenner and general manager Brian Cashman-- to go "all-in" and make significant moves this winter.
A possible lockout may alter New York's plans. Without a salary cap, the Yankees are usually one of the top spending organizations in the Majors.
That might not be enough to appease Judge. Perhaps the Yankees are making the wrong decisions when it comes to roster construction.
Spending money is great, but it won't matter if the players on the field don't make sense as a unit.
"Externally, the Yankees have a great one-two punch in their starting rotation with Cam Schlittler and Max Fried, but adding another ace wouldn't hurt," Bleacher Report's Kerry Miller wrote. "Also, adding a right-handed corner infielder to pair with Luis Garcia Jr. and Ryan McMahon would make a lot of sense."
Of course, the Yankees have major decisions to make with impending free agents, including Jazz Chisholm Jr. and David Bednar. How will they handle the rest of Giancarlo Stanton's contract?
Almost 35, the clock is ticking for Judge to win a World Series before his career comes to an end.
Now more than ever, the Yankees must be aggressive in their pursuit of top free agents and make smart decisions in the trade market.

item.content:encoded:
Yankees general manager Brian Cashman said that “Aaron Judge has a follow-up coming with Dr. Gregory Pearl regarding his rib.”

In the same press conference, Yankees manager Aaron Boone said that he doesn’t anticipate offseason surgery for any Yankees player, which would include Judge. Cashman added that “We feel like we’re in a good place. He can take advantage of the rest of the winter and be ready to go when Spring Training starts.” While it does seem like Judge will be healthy heading into 2027, the bigger question is whether or not the Yankees will utilize the DH spot to take some stress off his body during the season and help him remain healthy for the full season as he gets older.

item.content:encoded:
Aaron Boone hoping Yankees will 'bully' their way to 2027 World Series appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The New York Yankees are bringing Aaron Boone back as manager for the 2027 season. With Boone leading the way, New York has consistently reached the postseason but has yet to win a World Series. In fact, the ball club has not earned a championship since 2009. Hal Steinbrenner defended Boone on Wednesday, but the reality of the situation is that Boone's leadership has not translated to World Series victories. Boone is hoping the Yankees can "bully" their way to a Fall Classic victory sooner rather than later.
"Hopefully we are that bully and we're the best team throughout the season next year, and bully our way through the postseason," Boone said Wednesday, via SNY Yankees. "… I believe it (the Yankees winning the World Series) can happen with me at the helm. But any answer I give in defense of that isn't gonna be a great one or satisfy people. I think I'm good at my job, I think we have a lot of the right people in the building. At the end of the day we haven't won a championship with me at the helm.
"Ultimately, that's what has to happen to satisfy certainly myself — that's why I'm doing this — but to answer those questions ultimately. Haven't been able to do it yet."
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
Boone has found no shortage of regular season success. For many teams around the sport, he'd be considered a tremendous manager given how often the Yankees have reached the postseason. Since he took over the manager job in 2018, the Yankees have reached the postseason in eight out of the nine years, earned two 100-win seasons, and reached the World Series in 2024.
With all of that being said, Aaron Boone happens to manage a team that leads all of MLB with 27 total championships. A personal 790-565 regular season record isn't good enough to satisfy Yankees fans. Rather, the city of New York will look at Boone's 27-30 postseason record and zero World Series championships.
Perhaps Aaron Boone will finally help the Yankees reach their goal in 2027. Only time will tell.

One could say that Boone deserves American League Manager of the Year votes. Why? item.content:encoded:
NEW YORK -- Aaron Boone will be back for a 10th season as manager of the New York Yankees.
That’s a good thing because he is coming off his best season as the field boss. One could say that Boone deserves American League Manager of the Year votes. Why? The 2026 Yankees dealt with a lot of injuries and still won 93 games before succumbing to the Tampa Bay Rays in the American League Division Series.
This is what Boone had to deal with in 2026: Eighteen players made a total of 24 appearances on the injured list. It started with right fielder Aaron Judge, who missed 93 games because of a fractured right rib and right calf strain. Let’s not forget Giancarlo Stanton missing 135 games with calf injuries.
While Cam Schlittler was a steady presence on the mound, four of the Yankee starters – Gerrit Cole, Max Fried, Carlos Rodon and Clark Schmidt spent time on the IL.
With his veterans out of commission for a lengthy period or not producing, Boone relied on much younger players besides Schlittler. It turned out that Ben Rice was New York’s best hitter, hitting a career-high 41 home runs, while shortstop George Lombard Jr. and outfielder Spencer Jones saw significant playing time after the All-Star Break.
Anthony Volpe seemed more comfortable at second and third base than he did at shortstop. Volpe even went 17-for-51 (.333) with runners in scoring position. Right-hander Will Warren, who spent most of the season in the rotation, was second behind Schlittler in victories (11).
Boone lucked out with relievers Brent Headrick, Paul Blackburn, John Schreiber and Ryan Yarbrough, who saw a lot of action before closer David Bednar saw the ninth inning. Blackburn was arguably Boone’s best reliever, winning seven games with a 1.59 ERA in 62 games.
During his tenure with the Yankees, Boone has won 790 games, guided the team to the postseason eight of the last nine seasons and went to the World Series in 2024, only to lose to the Dodgers in five games.
Prior to ‘26, Boone received plenty of criticism because the team never won a World Series title under his watch and relied heavily on analytics. This year, the team was flawed. There were times when small ball had to be in play because the Yankees ranked 26th in the major leagues in hitting and sixth in strikeouts.
New York was near the middle of the pack in defensive runs saved. But it was defense that hurt the Yankees in the ALDS. Who can forget the three errors they committed in the first inning of Game 2, a contest they lost 5-2 and that put them in a 2-0 hole in the series.
"Look, obviously we dealt with a lot of adversity throughout the year … from the injury front, but guys stepped up all year, and we were able to win a lot of games and give ourselves an opportunity and then just came up short," Boone said after the Yankees were eliminated from postseason play.
All quotations obtained firsthand unless otherwise noted.

item.content:encoded:
Brian Cashman will continue his tenure as the New York Yankees' general manager after agreeing to a new contract. The 59-year-old has been with the team for 29 seasons, during which the Yankees have won four World Series titles and 15 American League East titles. However, the team has not claimed a world title since 2009 and was recently swept out of the AL Division Series by the Tampa Bay Rays.
Despite the team's recent struggles, Cashman remains a central figure in the Yankees' management. According to Yahoo Sports, fans have expressed frustration over the team's performance, particularly after an embarrassing ALDS loss to the Toronto Blue Jays last October. Critics have pointed to Cashman's limited roster changes during the offseason, including the acquisition of Ryan Weathers and the re-signing of Cody Bellinger, as insufficient to address the team's issues.
The Yankees face several pressing questions, including decisions about Aaron Boone's future as manager and how to handle players like Giancarlo Stanton and Ryan McMahon. The Sporting News reports that McMahon, who has struggled offensively, may be traded, with the Yankees potentially covering part of his salary to facilitate a deal.
As the Yankees look to the future, Cashman will need to navigate these challenges and make strategic decisions to strengthen the team. His ability to find value in trades and manage the roster will be crucial as the Yankees aim to return to the top of the baseball world.
