item.content:encoded:
NEW YORK (AP) — The price of a qualifying offer for this year’s major league free agents rose 5.1% to $23.15 million from $22,025,000.
The figure is determined by the average of the top 125 major league contracts this year. The price dropped by $100,000 to $17.8 million in 2019, then rose to $18.9 million in 2020, fell $500,000 in 2021 and rose to $19.65 million in 2022, $20,325,000 in 2023 and $21.05 million in 2024.
Qualifying offers began after the 2012 season, and only 18 of 157 offers have been accepted.
A free agent can be made a qualifying offer only if he has been with the same team continuously since opening day and has never received a qualifying offer before.
Among the top players who can become free agents after the World Series and are eligible to receive qualifying offers are Seattle outfielder Randy Arozarena, New York Yankees left-hander David Bednar, Minnesota catcher Ryan Jeffers, Pittsburgh second baseman Brandon Lowe, San Diego left-hander Adrian Morejon, Baltimore left-hander Trevor Roger and Chicago Cubs outfielder Seiya Suzuki.
A record four players accepted last year from among the 13 who received offers: Chicago Cubs left-hander Shota Imanaga, Milwaukee right-hander Brandon Woodruff, New York Yankees outfielder Trent Grisham and Detroit second baseman Gleyber Torres.
Other potential free agents ineligible for qualifying offers this offseason include Philadelphia second baseman Luis Arraez, Baltimore right-hander Chris Bassitt, New York Mets third baseman Bo Bichette, Arizona right-hander Zac Gallen, San Diego right-hander Michael King, Padres left-hander Robbie Ray, Los Angeles Dodgers left-hander Tarik Skubal and Toronto outfielder George Springer.
Bichette and King must decide on player options.
A qualifying offer can be made through the fifth day after the World Series, and a player has a week after that to accept.
If a team makes a qualifying offer to a player who signs a major league contract with another club before the amateur draft, his former club would receive a draft pick as compensation at the end of the first round or at the end of competitive balance round B. The placement depends on the amount of the new contract and the revenue-sharing and luxury tax status of the team losing the player.
Qualifying offers began at $13.3 million. Other players who accepted are Baltimore catcher Matt Wieters, Houston outfielder Colby Rasmus and Dodgers left-hander Brett Anderson ($15.8 million for 2016); Mets second baseman Neil Walker and Philadelphia right-hander Jeremy Hellickson ($17.2 million for 2017); Dodgers left-hander Hyun Jin Ryu ($17.9 million for 2019); Chicago White Sox first baseman José Abreu and Minnesota right-hander Jake Odorizzi ($17.8 million for 2020); San Francisco right-hander Kevin Gausman and Mets right-hander Marcus Stroman ($18.9 million for 2021); Giants first baseman Brandon Belt ($18.4 million for 2022; Texas left-hander Martín Pérez and Giants outfielder Joc Pederson ($19.65 million for 2023); and Cincinnati Reds right-hander Nick Martinez ($21.05 million for 2025).

item.title: [CBS Sports] Aaron Boone to return as Yankees manager in 2027: Why New York is sticking with skipper for 10th season
item.dc:creator: Mike Axisa

"That's for another day," Boone said when asked about his job status after the Yankees were swept by the AL East rival Tampa Bay Rays in the
item.content:encoded:
Aaron Boone will return as manager of the New York Yankees in 2027, the Bergen Record reports. Next season is the final season on Boone's contract and will be his 10th season as Yankees manager. New York is 790-565 (.583) in nine seasons under Boone. The Yankees have reached the postseason eight times in those nine seasons but have not won the World Series.
"That's for another day," Boone said when asked about his job status after the Yankees were swept by the AL East rival Tampa Bay Rays in the ALDS. "Right now is about trying to reflect on this, trying to connect with guys right now as much as I can. Appreciative of a lot of things, but those conversations and things are for another day."
Unless the Yankees give Boone a contract extension, he will enter next season as a lame duck, and that season could come with a World Series or bust mandate. The Yankees have had only three managers in the last 30 years: Joe Torre from 1996-2007, Joe Girardi from 2008-17, and Boone since 2018. Torre and Girardi both won the World Series within their first two seasons.
Why the Yankees are sticking with Boone
The Yankees have not fired a manager who was under contract since Stump Merrill after the 1991 season (Torre and Girardi were let go after their contracts expired). Hal Steinbrenner is much more patient than his father, perhaps to his detriment, but Steinbrenner and GM Brian Cashman are supportive of Boone. That all made Boone's return more likely than not.
Furthermore, this is a bad offseason to need a new manager. Team personnel, including managers, can not communicate with players during a lockout, which is considered likely when the collective bargaining agreement expires on Dec. 1. Relationship-building with players is most of the job, and it will be difficult for a new manager to foster those during the lockout.
Only the Los Angeles Dodgers have won more games than the Yankees since Boone was named manager in 2018. This is a franchise that is judged on championships, however, and New York has not won a World Series since 2009. The Yankees have won just one pennant since then (2024), and their 17-year title drought is tied for the longest in franchise history with their 1979-95 stretch.
Aaron Boone as Yankees manager
| Season | Record | Playoffs |
| 2018 | 100-62 | Lost ALDS |
| 2019 | 103-59 | Lost ALCS |
| 2020 | 33-27 | Lost ALDS |
| 2021 | 92-70 | Lost AL Wild Card |
| 2022 | 99-63 | Lost ALCS |
| 2023 | 82-80 | N/A |
| 2024 | 94-68 | Lost World Series |
| 2025 | 94-68 | Lost ALDS |
| 2026 | 93-68 | Lost ALDS |
Cashman is currently without a contract, though he is expected to return for what would be his 29th season as their head baseball operations executive. .
The Yankees went 93-68 in 2026. It was their 34th consecutive winning season. The Houston Astros and Seattle Mariners are the only two teams with a managerial vacancy at the moment.

item.title: [The Big Lead] Yankees make decision about Aaron Boone for 2027
item.dc:creator: J P Hoornstra

The offseason before a contract expires is often decision time, and no manager likes to go into the final year with limited certainty about his future. item.content:encoded:
In Major League Baseball, the length of a manager’s contract is treated more like a rough suggestion rather than a firm timeline for a man to hold a job title. The offseason before a contract expires is often decision time, and no manager likes to go into the final year with limited certainty about his future.
New York Yankees manager Aaron Boone will enter the last year of his contract in 2027. For now at least, the Yankees have no plans to let him go.
Pete Caldera of the Bergen Record was the first to report on Monday, Oct. 19, that Boone will return to the bench in the Bronx next season. Whether he is offered—or signs—a long-term extension is another matter.
Boone, 53, led the Yankees to 93 wins and a second-place finish in the American League East in 2026. They defeated the Boston Red Sox in a two-game wild-card sweep and then lost to the Tampa Bay Rays in the Division Series round.
Closing in on a decade
In nine seasons as the Yankees’ manager, Boone is 790-565 (.583). Among active managers, only Los Angeles Dodgers skipper Dave Roberts boasts a better regular-season winning percentage. Only 15 other men have a better winning percentage in MLB history, and 10 of them are in the Hall of Fame.
Those eye-popping factoids do little to satisfy fans for whom anything less than a World Series title is seen as a failure. Whether a different manager could have piloted the Yankees on a deep postseason run without injured star Aaron Judge (who wasn’t active in October or for most of the regular season) is up for debate.
One thing is clear: The Yankees’ front office has an excellent working relationship with Boone, and neither party is eager for it to end.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Aaron Boone reportedly set to return as Yankees manager in 2027 after latest postseason exit, speculation
item.dc:creator: Sean Leahy
item.description: The New York Yankees are sticking with Aaron Boone next season after all. After speculation that the team would move on following their latest postseason exit, Boone will return as the Yankees manager in 2027, according to USA Today's Pete Caldera and the YES Network's Jack Curry. Boone signed a two-year extension through the 2027 MLB season in Feb. 2025, months after the Yankees lost the World Series to the Los Angeles Dodgers. After two straight eliminations in the ALDS, many expected his time
item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees are sticking with Aaron Boone next season after all.
After speculation that the team would move on following their latest postseason exit, Boone will return as the Yankees manager in 2027, according to USA Today's Pete Caldera and the YES Network's Jack Curry.
Boone signed a two-year extension through the 2027 MLB season in Feb. 2025, months after the Yankees lost the World Series to the Los Angeles Dodgers. After two straight eliminations in the ALDS, many expected his time would be up in New York after nine seasons. Instead, Boone will now manage through the end of his current deal.
The 2026 season saw the Yankees finish second in the AL East for the second straight season and win 90 games for the seventh time over a full season under Boone. It's been the postseason where the Yankees fell short more often than not under the 53-year-old.
Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Basketball league for the 2026-27 NBA season
The Yankees hold a 27-30 playoff record under Boone, which included three trips to the ALCS and one World Series appearance. His teams were 18-5 as the higher seed in a series and 9-25 as the lower seed. The Yankees were the No. 4 seed in 2026 and beat the No. 5 seed Boston Red Sox in the wild-card round before being swept by the top-seeded Tampa Rays in the ALDS.
Without Aaron Judge and with Giancarlo Stanton only available as a pinch-hitter, the Yankees batted .130 in the ALDS, and three of their five RBI came from Ben Rice. Their pitching was what kept them in games, as evidenced by a 1.88 team ERA, 0.81 team WHIP and a .173 opponent batting average.
Other teams picked up on the weaknesses of Boone's Yankee teams. The Dodgers told their players their 2024 World Series opponents were "talent over fundamentals" and were bound to self-destruct. Toronto Blue Jays announcer Buck Martinez labeled the AL East rivals as "not a good team" last season, saying they were mistake-prone in the field and on the bases.
Those criticisms were only hardened after seeing Austin Wells' baserunner mistake in Game 1 against the Rays and then the Yankees' defensive breakdown in Game 2.
General manager Brian Cashman has been in charge for 29 seasons. Boone is just the third manager to work under him. The Yankees last won the World Series in 2009 and are in the midst of a 17-year championship drought. The boos heard after Trent Grisham's series-ending strikeout against the Rays showed how frustrated the fanbase is with the team's current state.
But regardless of their feelings, Cashman isn't ready to hire a new manager just yet. It's unclear what changes he will make this winter, if any major ones at all, in hopes of returning the franchise to contender status.

item.title: [The Times of India] Yankees all-star CC Sabathia helps fund $11 million ‘Harlem Field of Dreams’; renovated Brigadier General Charles Young Playground field now serves five sports
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk
item.description: CC Sabathia, the former New York Yankees pitcher, has helped transform a dilapidated dirt field in Harlem into a place where children can play. Through his PitCCh In Foundation, Sabathia joined public agencies and sports organisations to fund the $11 million Harlem Field of Dreams at Brigadier General Charles Young Playground. The renovated field now accommodates five sports, offers free youth programming, and honours a remarkable figure in American military history. Here is how the project was
item.content:encoded:
CC Sabathia, the former New York Yankees pitcher, has helped transform a dilapidated dirt field in Harlem into a place where children can play. Through his PitCCh In Foundation, Sabathia joined public agencies and sports organisations to fund the $11 million Harlem Field of Dreams at Brigadier General Charles Young Playground. The renovated field now accommodates five sports, offers free youth programming, and honours a remarkable figure in American military history. Here is how the project was paid for, what the new field offers local families, and why the history of the playground and its surroundings matters to the neighbourhood.
How the $11 million Harlem Field of Dreams was funded, asset forfeiture money and foundation donations
According to a 2025 press release from the Office of the Mayor of New York City, the $11 million project drew on several funding sources. Roughly $7.5 million came from law enforcement asset forfeiture funds from the New York and New Jersey High Intensity Drug Trafficking Area program, in partnership with the New York City Police Department and the New York City Police Foundation. Additional contributions came from Sabathia's PitCCh In Foundation, Major League Baseball, the Major League Baseball Players Association Youth Development Fund, the National Football League Foundation Grassroots Program, the Cal Ripken Senior Foundation, the Manhattan Borough President's Office, and the New York City Council.
The release does not say how much each partner gave, so Sabathia's exact share is not specified.
Five sports, more than 800 young players, and new amenities on the renovated Harlem athletic field
The project turned a dilapidated dirt field into a 150,000 square foot synthetic turf field built for multiple sports. Eric Adams, then mayor of New York City, told the public in the release that more than 800 young people can now play baseball, football, soccer, and lacrosse there. The city says the field accommodates five sports in total, with softball completing the list. Upgrades include improved drainage and water detention, drinking fountains, fencing, backstops, benches, dugouts, and a sports mister. The release describes a $9 million transformation, while the mayor's remarks and later sections cite $11 million for the full project. Sabathia told the public that giving back has always been at the heart of everything he does, and that New York has become his second home.
Sabathia in July 2018 (Image: Wikipedia)
Free Saturday Night Lights programming and a public safety approach that keeps young people engaged
The city plans to offer free youth sports on the new field through the New York City Department of Youth and Community Development's Saturday Night Lights program, which the release describes as a way to give young people safe places to play while building trust between law enforcement and communities. The field is part of an upstream approach to public safety that invests in free programming to keep young people engaged when they are not in school. Earlier improvements in 2023 included new asphalt and fencing for the main basketball court, repairs to three basketball courts, and the conversion of one court into a soccer pitch. The field house bathrooms are also set for upgrades with $2.5 million in public funding.
Brigadier General Charles Young, the history behind the Harlem playground and the Hellfighters armoury
The playground is named for Brigadier General Charles Young, who was born into slavery in Kentucky in 1864 and became the third Black graduate of the United States Military Academy at West Point. According to the release, he served more than 30 years in the United States Army and became the first African American colonel before being forced into medical retirement in 1917. To prove his fitness, he rode 497 miles on horseback to Washington, though his appeal failed, and he was posthumously promoted in 2022. The playground sits just north of the 369th Regiment Armoury, home to the Harlem Hellfighters, a regiment that saw more combat than any other unit during World War One. Cal Ripken Junior told the public that the field is the 125th Youth Development Park, opened by the Cal Ripken Senior Foundation.

item.title: [pinstripealley.com] Ask Pinstripe Alley: Yankees mailbag questions request
item.dc:creator: Madison Pavich
item.description: Unfortunately, it’s time to ponder what comes next already. The Yankees were eliminated in the ALDS by their division rivals for the second straight year, and it’s safe to say that allowing that process to play out a third consecutive year would cause some nuclear-reactor level meltdowns. item.content:encoded:
Unfortunately, it’s time to ponder what comes next already. The Yankees were eliminated in the ALDS by their division rivals for the second straight year, and it’s safe to say that allowing that process to play out a third consecutive year would cause some nuclear-reactor level meltdowns. The immediate aftermath of their elimination was handled by my colleague Jake in our last mailbag while the team was still active, but now that the team is officially in offseason mode it’s time to start picking apart what went wrong and what the team can do going forward.
There’s a lot of moving parts in the Yankees’ roster turnover this year, with 10 free agents to be, though there’s still a lot of money tied up to the superstars of the roster making some big swings unlikely. Still, there’s room for a sizeable makeover if Brian Cashman and company can get creative. How can the team revamp its offense after struggling to put rallies together for most of the year and when it mattered most? What will come of Aaron Judge’s lost year and his frustrations with how the team is currently looking? What bright spots can they build around from an otherwise lost year? If you have questions like these, or anything else on your mind, send ‘em in for a chance to be featured in our Yankees mailbag.
Answers will run on Friday afternoon. All questions received by the night of October 22nd will be considered. You can leave your submissions in the comment section below or by e-mail to pinstripealleyblog [at] gmail [dot] com.

item.title: [Sportsnaut] Rumor Opens Door For NY Mets to Address Major Need in Trade With NY Yankees This Winter: What Would a Deal Cost?

Top star Juan Soto is still in the early stages of his prime. Francisco Lindor had a
item.content:encoded:
A new rumor offers the New York Mets a chance at a young, high-upside starting pitcher in a rare trade with in-city rivals, the New York Yankees.
There is no other way to say it than that the 2026 season for the Mets was one of the worst they’ve had in quite some time. And that is saying something considering their devoted fanbase has seen many underwhelming years. However, there is hope for better days in 2027.
Top star Juan Soto is still in the early stages of his prime. Francisco Lindor had a strong finish to the year. But more than anything, prospects Carson Benge, AJ Ewing, and Nolan McLean showed they have the talent to be key members of a new-look core going forward for President David Stearns to build around.
New York Yankees expected to shop Luis Gil
The Mets will look to upgrade first, second, and third in the offseason, but improving their starting staff will be a far bigger priority. They will surely be linked to superstar free agent Tarik Skubal, but if there is a new salary cap for 2027, the two-time Cy Young may not be a realistic option. That is why Stearns will also need to be crafty and find players that make them better, but who are also cost-effective and under team control for a few years.
Interestingly enough, the Yankees are expected to make a player just like that available soon. According to the New York Post’s Joel Sherman, “The Yankees are going to try like heck to trade Luis Gil.”
The Yankees have a wealth of talent in their starting rotation, and after posting a career- worst 4.61 ERA in nine appearances after dealing with shoulder inflammation, he probably isn’t in their plans to start next season. He could be moved to the bullpen, but that is a big if for the 28-year-old. Furthermore, he is out of minor league options. So they need to come up with a plan or trade him.
What could a Luis Gil trade cost the New York Mets
While Gil struggled last season in limited action and has dealt with injury woes the last two seasons, it can’t be forgotten that he was the American League Rookie of the Year just two years ago. Posting a 15-7 record with a 3.50 ERA and 171 strikeouts to 77 walks. He is also under arbitration control for two more seasons and is expected to make just over $2 million in 2027.
The Yankees don’t have much leverage since Gil’s value is at a low point and they don’t have a clear role for him next season. That could help the Mets in potential trade talks. So what might a deal cost the team from Queens?
The Yankees have a need at catcher after another awful season at the plate for Austin Wells. Would a swap of Gil for Francisco Alvarez interest the Yankees? The Mets may be open to finding a new platoon mate with Gold Glove finalist Luis Torrens. Brett Baty and/or Mark Vientos (along with a prospect) would also be intriguing low-cost options for the team from the Bronx at second or third. Two other positions they will need to address in the winter.
Is a trade likely? Probably not, but Stearns loves a good project. The former ROTY is an affordable option with a ton of upside that he should consider.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] The Yankees’ 10 Longest Home Runs of 2026
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Farrar
item.description: There is just something different about those no doubters, when a slugger digs into the box and really gets a hold of a pitch unleashing that wooden thunderclap like the legend of Thor. Watching the ball arch towards the sky and then seeing gravity finally win the fight and bring it back down to earth still sends a childlike joy through my bones. Despite only getting 327 at-bats from biggest sluggers Aaron Judge and Giancarlo Stanton, the Yankees still had their fair share of no doubters in 2026
item.content:encoded:
There is just something different about those no doubters, when a slugger digs into the box and really gets a hold of a pitch unleashing that wooden thunderclap like the legend of Thor. Watching the ball arch towards the sky and then seeing gravity finally win the fight and bring it back down to earth still sends a childlike joy through my bones.
Despite only getting 327 at-bats from biggest sluggers Aaron Judge and Giancarlo Stanton, the Yankees still had their fair share of no doubters in 2026. Before we dive into the top ten home runs, I want to clarify this list ranks each long ball by distance.
There is one honorable mention I want to give out before we get started. On April 21st, Stanton launched a 368-foot home run with a 41-degree launch angle. This moonshot in Boston was the Yankees' highest-arching home run of the season. It did not go far, but it was a fun one to watch as it had hang time like Vince Carter!
10. Ben Rice: 431 feet (August 8th vs. Atlanta)
I hope you are not hungry, because this top ten list contains as much Rice as your favorite takeout place's menu! There is your dinner plan, as Rice keeps serving us even after the season ends. This early-August blast came off the bat at just over 105 miles per hour (mph) and had the highest launch angle of the top ten at 35 degrees.
9. Ben Rice: 433 feet (June 19th vs. Cincinnati)
The team leader in home runs stakes his second claim on the list quickly, also claiming the nine-hole. This bullet traveled 109.1 mph off Benny's barrel and had a 26-degree launch angle. The three-run job was one of those long home runs that reminds you center field at Yankee Stadium is no joke.
8. Ben Rice: 438 feet (August 16th @ Toronto)
Starting the list off with a turkey, Rice keeps cooking. Unlike his first two appearances, this one came in Toronto. Number 33 on the season for Rice came off Braydon Fisher in the top of the 10th inning, making it the latest inning long ball on the list. What would prove to be the game-winner jumped off the bat at 108.5 mph and launched at a 27-degree angle.
7. Spencer Jones: 443 feet (June 9th @ Cleveland)
The rookie's first home run in the show was an absolute missile. Jones jumped all over this pitch from Slade Cecconi and produced the second-highest exit velocity on the list at 112.2 mph, with the lowest launch angle of the top ten at just 25 degrees. Do not blink, or you will miss this straight-line shot that got out of play in a hurry.
6. Ben Rice: 444 feet (September 4th @ San Diego)
Despite a lower exit velocity of 108.6 mph, the one-degree difference in launch angle, at 26 degrees, was enough for this Rice home run to travel one foot farther than the previous entry. This ball ran away from the camera operator as it decided it would rather check out the San Diego Zoo than stick around for peanuts and Cracker Jacks.
5. Giancarlo Stanton: 446 feet (April 16th vs. LA Angels)
Big G gets more than just his honorable mention with this home run that landed 446 feet from home plate in the Bronx, earning him a spot in our top five. Stanton muscled this ball at 111.1 mph off the bat and into the air at a 27-degree angle. This was a frustrating season for Stanton, and at this stage of his career, there might not be many more of these moments left for us to enjoy.
4. Ben Rice: 447 feet (August 19th @ Baltimore)
Making his fifth and final appearance is Rice with this home run down at Camden Yards. This one got a few extra shakes of Old Bay seasoning as it traveled at 110.2 mph and lollipopped toward the harbor at a 33-degree angle. All hail the Yankees' home run king of 2026!
3. Spencer Jones: 448 feet (September 20th @ Arizona)
With a build similar to Judge and a left-handed swing, Jones is sure to send a few moonshots each season that will be impressive enough to land him on this list for years to come. This home run claims the title of highest launch angle on the list at 34 degrees. The towering drive traveled at 109.8 mph before falling like a meteor out in the desert.
2. Amed Rosario: 450 feet (July 31st @ Chicago Cubs)
Imposter alert! Surprise, surprise, surprise. Who would have believed it at the start of the season, but at 6-foot-1 and 227 pounds, Rosario hit a home run good enough for second-furthest of the season. Perhaps aided by the Chicago wind, this home run tried its best to make it to the rooftop seats, coming off the bat at 108 mph with a 30-degree launch angle. Another whacky surprise, it was off a lefty!
1. Aaron Judge: 456 feet (April 13th vs. LA Angels)
Almost as surprising as Rosario, Judge finally makes his first appearance on the list, and of course, the best power hitter since the steroid era takes the top spot. Why waste swings, right? This home run by Judge is truly a piece of art. At 116.2 mph, it was the hardest-hit Yankees home run of the season in addition to being the furthest. Its 26-degree launch angle helped it get over the fence quicker than a little leaguer retrieving a home run ball in the sandlot. Please be healthy next season, Captain. We missed you this year.
That concludes the top ten longest Yankees home runs of 2026. Did anyone see any of these in person? What was the biggest surprise in your eyes? I was most surprised that Bellinger didn't crack the top ten, or even the top 20 longest home runs in 2026!

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Yankees Trade Pitch Lands 111-Home Run Catcher for Will Warren, 2 Prospects
item.dc:creator: TJ French
item.description: The New York Yankees should consider making a big splash this offseason in the trade market for a catcher. One option that stands out as a potential target is Athletics' catcher Shea Langeliers. Langeliers might be in a limbo spot this offseason with the Athletics bringing in a new GM and president of baseball operations. Considering nobody has been hired yet, that puts all non-signed players in jeopardy of being moved, and a team like the Yankees could greatly benefit from the Athletics moving
item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees should consider making a big splash this offseason in the trade market for a catcher.
One option that stands out as a potential target is Athletics' catcher Shea Langeliers.
Langeliers might be in a limbo spot this offseason with the Athletics bringing in a new GM and president of baseball operations.
Considering nobody has been hired yet, that puts all non-signed players in jeopardy of being moved, and a team like the Yankees could greatly benefit from the Athletics moving on from their All-Star backstop.
Full Details of Potential Yankees-Athletics Trade Idea for Shea Langeliers
MLBTR.com's Mark Polishuk recently outlined why Langeliers could be a prime trade target:
"The incoming PBO/GM might think the club's pitching simply has too many holes to patch up this winter, or that it's impossible for any rotation to post passable numbers in Sacramento. If 2027 is another rebuilding season, then that eats up one of Langeliers' remaining two years of control. By that logic, trading Langeliers for some younger talent (particularly pitchers) who could be ready for the majors as early as 2028 would be the better long-term play for the organization."
A package the New York Yankees might be able to offer the Athletics that would be strong enough could include pitcher Will Warren and 2 pitching prospects: LHP Kyle Carr and RHP Cade Smith.
Remember, the Athletics are very pitching-hungry, and Warren is already a certified starter who could make as many as 30 starts in 2027, and those two prospects are already past the early stages of their professional career, so they could be able to see big-league action as early as a couple of years.
Taking a Quick Look at Shea Langeliers
In 541 total games played across five MLB seasons, Langeliers has 111 career home runs, 100 doubles, 295 RBI, and a lifetime OPS+ of 112.
He came up with the Atlanta Braves but never actually made his MLB debut with Atlanta; he was instead traded to the Athletics in 2022 and quickly made a major impact with the bat.
In 2025, Langeliers clubbed 31 home runs and 32 doubles, and if an injury didn't limit him to just 106 games in 2026, it's likely he could have had another 30/30 season, especially considering where the Athletics play their home games.
This article was originally published on HEAVY
The post Yankees Trade Pitch Lands 111-Home Run Catcher for Will Warren, 2 Prospects appeared first on HEAVY.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Yankees Need To Replace Austin Wells With This Free Agent

However, one of their reported targets is now a free agent, and the Yankees need to go after him. item.content:encoded:
Austin Wells has not established himself as a reliable contributor on offense yet, and the New York Yankees could use an upgrade at catcher.
The Yankees reportedly explored catching upgrades at the trade deadline, but were unable to land anyone. However, one of their reported targets is now a free agent, and the Yankees need to go after him.
Ryan Jeffers was ultimately not moved by the Minnesota Twins at the trade deadline, but as a free agent, he is free to sign with any team. This season, Jeffers had an .814 OPS in 94 games. He hit 14 home runs and had a total of 35 extra-base hits.
Jeffers has a .753 career OPS and has played in 607 career games. He has been to the postseason twice, and on the Yankees, he could play on a true contender. In four seasons, Wells has a .697 OPS, but has been a steady defender.
Jeffers has not been a good defender recently, but he would be such an upgrade offensively that the Yankees may be willing to put up with it. However, the Yankees' defense as a whole is a concern, so perhaps they will be wary of adding a poor defender behind the plate.
At the same time, the offense completely disappeared in October, and efforts to improve need to be made. Surprisingly enough, Wells was one of the Yankees only hitters to perform well in the postseason. However, that is not enough to cover up four years of offensive woes.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees are currently home for the offseason.
They had a strong regular season and swept the Boston Red Sox in the Wild Card Series.
That said, the Yankees had their season come to an end when they got swept by the Tampa Bay Rays in the ALDS.
Luis Gil Rumors
Recently, Joel Sherman of The New York Post (via Pinstripe Post) reported that the Yankees are looking to trade Luis Gil.
He finished the 2026 season going 1-2 with a 4.61 ERA in nine games (four starts).
@NYYWorldwide wrote (on October 18): “Joel Sherman believes the Yankees will try to trade Luis Gil ahead of the tender deadline in November. Gil had a 4.61 ERA with 18 walks and 17 SO as both a reliever and starter in 2026.”
Gil Posts IG
 Luis Gil #81 of the New York Yankees reacts during the third inning of the game against the Los Angeles Angels at Yankee Stadium on April 15, 2026 in New York City. All players are wearing the number 42 in honor of Jackie Robinson Day.
Following the report, Gil made a post to Instagram on October 19.
He wrote: “HOME 🏡 🙏🏻”
Looking At Gil
Luis Gil #81 of the New York Yankees walks off of the field after being removed from the third inning of game one of the Division Series against the Toronto Blue Jays at Rogers Centre on October 04, 2025 in Toronto, Ontario.
Gil has spent part of five seasons in the Bronx.
He had gotten off to a strong start to his career when he won the 2024 American League Rookie of The Year Award.
That season, the 28-year-old went 15-7 with a 3.50 ERA in 29 starts.
It will be interesting to see if another team is willing to take a chance on him.
Looking At The Yankees
Manager Aaron Boone of the New York Yankees looks on during batting practice before the game against the Boston Red Sox in game two of the American League Wild Card Series at Yankee Stadium on September 30, 2026 in the Bronx borough of New York City.
The Yankees finished the 2026 regular season as the second-place team in the American League East with a 93-68 record in 161 games.
They last won a World Series title during the 2009 season when Derek Jeter was still on the roster.

item.title: [yanksgoyard.com] Yankees Rumors: Luis Gil trade buzz, bullpen targets revealed, Nationals CF option
item.dc:creator: Stephen Parello
item.description: We're not quite at the point in the year where the rumor mill is churning in full force, making this current wave of New York Yankees rumors something of an appetizer and a sign that things are going to get much crazier very soon. The looming lockout sets a transaction deadline of December 1, unless the league and the players' union miraculously come to an agreement before then. That means the month of November is going to be fast and furious. We've already heard about the Yankees' supposed inte
item.content:encoded:
We're not quite at the point in the year where the rumor mill is churning in full force, making this current wave of New York Yankees rumors something of an appetizer and a sign that things are going to get much crazier very soon. The looming lockout sets a transaction deadline of December 1, unless the league and the players' union miraculously come to an agreement before then.
That means the month of November is going to be fast and furious. We've already heard about the Yankees' supposed interest in trading for Xavier Edwards, as well as a possible connection to Randy Arozarena. Now, we've got a stack of more fresh rumors to sort through.
Yankees are expected to shop Luis Gil ahead of the November 20 non-tender deadline
It's amazing how far Luis Gil has fallen. The 28-year-old went from 2024 AL Rookie of the Year to a potential centerpiece of a Kyle Tucker trade ahead of the 2025 season to a guy on the roster bubble.
Now, according to Joel Sherman of the New York Post, New York is expected to explore trading Gil before the November 20 non-tender deadline. At this point, he's a reclamation project who, at best, could fetch a change-of-scenery candidate or a lottery-ticket-type prospect or two.
"Keep in mind, Gil and [Clarke Schmidt] are guys, they do not have minor league options left," Sherman explained. "So, they're either on the team next year, or they have to go through waivers. So, if the Yankees feel like they can't help in the rotation, they can't help in the bullpen, there's going to be a thought about either non-tendering or trying to trade one or both."
Sounds like Schmidt is very much in the same boat as Gil, though his recent injury woes might make him even more likely to be non-tendered.
A pair of bullpen arms appear to be in the Yankees' crosshairs on the trade market
After making mostly addition-by-subtraction moves to the bullpen last offseason and failing to address it aside from trading away Camilo Doval at the trade deadline, it sounds like maybe, just maybe, Brian Cashman is going to get serious about revitalizing the relief corps.
On a recent episode of the Pinstripe Post Podcast, Sherman revealed a pair of reliever trade targets that he says the Yankees have liked for a long time, right-handers Jeremiah Estrada and Anthony Bender.
Estrada of the San Diego Padres is a high-octane arm with a big strikeout rate, though he's not without concerns. The 28-year-old hit the IL thrice in 2026, starting with right elbow tendonitis in April, followed by right knee inflammation in June, and finally a right shoulder impingement ended his season early on August 26. His average fastball velocity fell to 95.8 miles per hour this year from 97.9 miles per hour in 2025, and while he struck out 30.2% of batters he faced, he also issued walks at a 12.7% clip.
Marlins reliever Anthony Bender has been someone who has been linked to the Yankees before. He'd also add a much-needed strikeout punch to the 'pen, but in a different way. The 31-year-old is very much an East-West pitcher, with his slider dominating his pitch usage coming in at 65% this year. He pairs that with a sinker that he goes to 32% of the time. Bender's season was impacted for a second straight year with a right shin stress reaction. He tossed 34 1/3 innings in 2026, posting a 2.62 ERA with a 29.3% strikeout rate and an 8.6% walk rate.
It should be noted that Estrada is controllable through the 2029 season, while Bender hits free agency at the end of next season.
Yankees could eye a potential center field platoon partner for Spencer Jones
Lastly, Sherman reported that the Yankees have had past interest in Washington Nationals center fielder Jacob Young, and thinks that they could revisit a trade for the 27-year-old again this offseason to partner with, or even ensure against, Spencer Jones and possible regression.
Young is a glove-first, right-handed hitting outfielder with speed. His bat is very much a work in progress, with him posting a .648 OPS in 2024 and a .583 OPS in 2025 before turning in a career-best .707 performance in 2026. The biggest development in his offensive game has been his ability to hit lefties, slashing .282/.353/.423 against southpaws this year.
It's an interesting fit because, despite being a left-handed hitter, Jones performance against left-handed pitching was one of his biggest strengths. There are questions about his defense, though, and Young would be a nice hedge there. Young also feels like a Yankees kind of player in the Harrison Bader mold.
He has three years of team control remaining, meaning he won't come cheap, especially since his skill set and position could have some viewing him as a starting-caliber player rather than a fourth outfielder. This could make sense, but it all depends on cost.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Why David Bednar Reunion Looks Unlikely for Pirates
item.dc:creator: Danny Demilio
item.description: One need the Pirates will look to address this winter is adding to the bullpen. Among the many relievers set to hit the market is a familiar face. David Bednar, who pitched for the Pirates from 2021-25, will be a free agent this offseason. Bednar established himself as one of the better closers in baseball during his tenure in Pittsburgh. He earned two National League All-Star selections and tied for the league lead in saves in 2023. The Pirates dealt Bednar to the Yankees at last year's trade d
item.content:encoded:
One need the Pirates will look to address this winter is adding to the bullpen.
Among the many relievers set to hit the market is a familiar face. David Bednar, who pitched for the Pirates from 2021-25, will be a free agent this offseason.
Bednar established himself as one of the better closers in baseball during his tenure in Pittsburgh. He earned two National League All-Star selections and tied for the league lead in saves in 2023.
The Pirates dealt Bednar to the Yankees at last year's trade deadline, and the 32-year-old is coming off a fine '26 season. Bednar saved 35 games for New York this year and won a career-high seven games while posting a 2.47 ERA. He struck out 76 batters in 69.1 innings, walked 20 and held opponents to a .205 batting average.
On the surface, a possible reunion makes sense. Bednar would give the Pirates another high-leverage option alongside Mason Montgomery and Luke Weaver. A "Yinzer" to his core, Bednar would certainly have interest in returning to his hometown.
But Bednar is likely going to price himself out of Pittsburgh, and a recent development makes the possibility of a reunion even less likely.
The Yankees are expected to extend a qualifying offer to Bednar, according to Jon Heyman of the New York Post. This year's qualifying offer is valued just north of $23 million. If Bednar accepts the one-year qualifying offer, he will return to the Yankees instead of signing elsewhere in free agency.
Should he reject the offer, the team that signs Bednar would have to part with draft compensation to make the move official. If Bednar turns down the offer, he will still pay him well on a multi-year deal. The Pirates won't want to break the bank on a reliever and losing draft capital would also be undesirable. That remains true even if they get a draft pick back if Brandon Lowe, who should also receive a qualifying offer, departs in free agency.
Bednar returning to the Pirates would be a neat story and would solve a need. But as the Pirates look for bullpen help, they'll probably be looking elsewhere.

item.content:encoded:
Yankees predicted to replace Jazz Chisholm with $12M two-time Silver Slugger winner, 4x All-Star originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The New York Yankees have a big offseason ahead after getting swept by their division rival, the Tampa Bay Rays. The Yankees wanted to make a deep postseason run, but ultimately fell short.
All eyes are now on free agents and players who could leave the team. One of those players is Jazz Chisholm Jr., but he would like to stay in New York.
"Chisholm, an All-Star for the second time in 2025, endured a down year at the plate and struggled both offensively and defensively in four appearances in the playoffs. Manager Aaron Boone left Chisholm out of the Yankees' starting lineup for two postseason games, including their season-ending loss on Wednesday. The fans at Yankee Stadium booed Chisholm after he fouled out to first base as a pinch hitter in the bottom of the seventh inning. Nevertheless, Chisholm would rather continue his career with the Yankees than exit in free agency," MLB Trade Rumors wrote.
Early in Chisholm's career, he wasn't always the best player off the field. Yankees legend Derek Jeter even had to get on him when he was an owner of the Miami Marlins.
"When Jazz was in Miami, Derek Jeter was there as the owner and Don Mattingly was the manager. That's two great Yankees who understood tradition and played the game right. They both met with Chisholm on repeated occasions and begged him to get his head straight," NJ.com's Bob Klapisch wrote.
Now, it is just a matter of whether the Yankees bring Chisholm back. Sports Illustrated's Joe Najarian believes the Yankees should sign Luis Arraez instead.
"This hinges on whether the Yankees choose to bring back Jazz Chisholm Jr., but it seems more than likely that they will let him walk. Regardless, the Bronx Bombers still need a player with good bat-to-ball skills to make the lineup less polarizing, and nobody makes contact more consistently than Luis Arraez," Najarian wrote. "Despite Arraez's production dipping after being traded at the deadline to the Philadelphia Phillies, the 29-year-old enjoyed a bounce-back year by hitting .310 with a solid .765 OPS. He did that while striking out just 28 times in 596 plate appearances."
The second baseman has one of the most consistent bats in the game, at least when it comes to making contact. Arraez has also won two Silver Slugger Awards and earned four All-Star selections.
Arraez played under a $12 million contract this past season. Bringing him to New York could give the Yankees more consistency in their lineup, as he has demonstrated an ability to put the ball in play regularly.

item.title: [Yanks Go Yard] Most important issue on Spencer Jones' list of offseason improvements isn't what we expected
item.dc:creator: Stephen Parello
item.description: There weren't many souls hanging around Yankee Stadium last year during late November. Surely the New York Yankees front office was in sessions, plotting how to drag out negotiations with Cody Bellinger as long as possible. However, the field was a cold, barren landscape, devoid of signs of life, except for Spencer Jones. Jones came to the Bronx to get a jump on the 2026 season. He knew his reputation as a boom-or-bust prospect and was trying to put in the work so that things came out more boom
item.content:encoded:
There weren't many souls hanging around Yankee Stadium last year during late November. Surely the New York Yankees front office was in sessions, plotting how to drag out negotiations with Cody Bellinger as long as possible. However, the field was a cold, barren landscape, devoid of signs of life, except for Spencer Jones.
Jones came to the Bronx to get a jump on the 2026 season. He knew his reputation as a boom-or-bust prospect and was trying to put in the work so that things came out more boom than bust. You can largely say that happened in 2026, though maybe not right away.
Now Jones is already starting to focus again on the future and how he needs to improve. In fact, he's made a list of things that he wants to work on this offseason to come back stronger in 2027.
“In my own head, I’ve got a list of things I want to work on, things I want to do. I’m motivated after this. Just move forward, head down into the next season. I struck out a million times this year. I feel like I didn’t help the team in certain contexts that way. I think defensively, I think I can get better. I think I can get faster. And then the mental side of the game — leaning on the resources we have here and making sure that I’m the best competitor when the season starts next year,” Jones said following the Yankees' elimination at the hands of the Tampa Bay Rays
Improving defensively is even more important than limiting strikeouts for Spencer Jones's Yankees future
The bugaboo with Jones has always been the strikeouts. He's got big power and even bigger swing-and-miss potential - or, at least, that's how he's been billed. Part of this has to do with his frame. At six-foot-seven, his strike zone is larger than most, his swing is longer than most, and unfurling those long limbs to explode to the ball takes just a fraction of a second longer.
The Aaron Judge comparisons are a bit tired and lazy, but frame-wise, the concerns were the same for Judge the prospect. The three-time MVP went from striking out 44.2% of the time during his 2016 cup of coffee to winning a batting title in 2025. We're not saying that Jones' evolution will be the same, but what we are saying is that it doesn't have to be in order for him to be a productive player. He had also made some progress reducing the Ks throughout the season.
| Big League Stint | Spencer Jones Strikeout Rate |
|---|---|
| May 8 through May 21 | 44.4% |
| June 5 through July 1 | 40.0% |
| July 22 through End of Regular Season | 34.3% |
There were only 10 qualified hitters who posted a strikeout rate above 30% in 2026, but of those 10, seven finished with a wRC+ over 100. The average wRC+ among the group was 109.9. From July 22 onward, Jones posted a 111 wRC+. There's definite room for improvement, but he's also right there with his fellow whiff-plagued peers. Also, few hit the ball as hard as Jones does when they make contact.
Therefore, it's clear that, for all the hand-wringing, the strikeouts aren't the biggest concern. Instead, the biggest issue that Jones needs to rectify is his defense.
Unlike the strikeouts, Jones had a reputation for being a good defender in center field in the minors. It makes sense, as he possesses 89th-percentile sprint speed and 79th-percentile arm strength. The physical tools are there, but the production has not been, at least at the big league level.
The 25-year-old produced -4 outs above average, -4 defensive runs saved, and a -3 fielding run value over just 315 1/3 innings in center. Extrapolating that out over a full season's workload, it's pretty much Trent Grisham levels of bad.
There's some thought that the movement between outfield positions, with Jones also receiving heavy doses of work in right and left field, caused the issue. There are also some who believe that the height of the stands in big league ballparks, compared to the minor league fields where he played, caused issues with his ability to track the ball.
The excuses are irrelevant. The Yankees have already seen one promising young outfielder become a defensive disaster in Jasson Dominguez, and Jones can't follow suit.
Moreover, the Yankees really need him to be able to handle center field. The options to replace him in center aren't great. On the free-agent market, the top center fielders are guys like Cedric Mullins, Daulton Varsho, and... Trent Grisham. That's not inspiring stuff.
The Yankees' only other alternative on the roster is shifting Cody Bellinger to center, a position he plays much less well than left field. New York's defense has already been an issue, so moving to a suboptimal defensive alignment should be off the table.
Jones has shown an encouraging level of maturity and a dedication to working tirelessly at his craft to improve. We've seen the payoff with his monstrous production against lefties and in clutch situations. That should fuel hope that he can improve in the field.
Getting better defensively is the most important thing that Jones can do this offseason. With that said, this doesn't have to be an either-or scenario, and if he accomplishes his goal and limits the strikeouts while also improving his glove work, we certainly won't complain.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Anthony Volpe hasn’t earned the Yankees’ next opening
item.dc:creator: Alexander Wilson
item.description: Eleven starts at second base shouldn't settle the Yankees' next everyday job. Anthony Volpe deserves to compete for it, but I'd make him win that competition rather than turn a change of position into an automatic fresh start in the lineup. The possible opening is real, even if it isn't final. Bryan Hoch's offseason assessment described Jazz Chisholm Jr. as unlikely to return and second base as a possible home for Volpe. Chisholm hasn't departed yet, and New York hasn't announced its next regula
item.content:encoded:
Eleven starts at second base shouldn't settle the Yankees' next everyday job. Anthony Volpe deserves to compete for it, but I'd make him win that competition rather than turn a change of position into an automatic fresh start in the lineup.
The possible opening is real, even if it isn't final. Bryan Hoch's offseason assessment described Jazz Chisholm Jr. as unlikely to return and second base as a possible home for Volpe. Chisholm hasn't departed yet, and New York hasn't announced its next regular there.
Volpe's Yankees role needs more than an endorsement
After the ALDS exit, Aaron Judge said the club needed Volpe on the team to win a World Series. That support says something about the captain's belief in his teammate. It doesn't answer how often Volpe should play, where he should play or what offensive standard comes with the assignment.
Being worth a roster place and being the best everyday second baseman are different questions. New York can agree with Judge about the first without skipping the work on the second.
Volpe finished the regular season at .245/.321/.336 with two home runs in 70 games. There is some on-base contribution in that line, but a .657 OPS doesn't make a starting job an easy decision. Changing the defensive label doesn't add extra-base production to the bat.
0What do you think?Post a comment.
The defensive trial was a beginning
Volpe appeared at second in 12 games, starting 11 and playing 102 1/3 innings. He made two errors. Neither the position's newness nor those errors should be stretched into a complete evaluation of his range, turns or reliability. It was a small assignment, not a full season of proof.
George Lombard Jr. taking over at shortstop gives the Yankees a reason to examine other ways to use Volpe. It doesn't require them to decide the answer before spring. A player can become comfortable somewhere without immediately becoming the best available choice there.
I'd keep the second-base work going while also preserving a multi-position role as an alternative. If the bat improves and the defensive assessment supports him, there is a useful player to put in the lineup. If the same offensive limitations remain, the Yankees need the freedom to acquire a stronger regular rather than protect a decision they made too early.
Volpe has already had a difficult year. An honest competition isn't another punishment; it's a better opportunity than being handed a job that the club later has to take away again.

Goldschmidt finished with a .765 OPS, including 18 home runs, 13 doubles, one triple and 52 RBIs. His producti
item.content:encoded:
Veteran first baseman Paul Goldschmidt is set to enter free agency after the New York Yankees’ early playoff exit, and one analyst sees a potential landing spot with American League rival Minnesota Twins.
The 39-year-old right-handed hitter spent the 2026 season as a platoon option in the Bronx. He batted .252 with a .313 on-base percentage and .452 slugging percentage across 105 games.
Goldschmidt finished with a .765 OPS, including 18 home runs, 13 doubles, one triple and 52 RBIs.
His production was particularly strong against left-handed pitching. He posted a .299 average and .967 OPS versus southpaws, with 11 of his homers coming in those matchups.
Jackson Kruse of FanSided outlined a fit in Minnesota, where young left-handed hitters Walker Jenkins and Emmanuel Rodriguez are expected to play key roles.
“Since Jenkins and Rodriguez hit from the left side, Goldschmidt would be the perfect platoon partner for the young stars,” Kruse wrote. “Goldschmidt could serve as a DH and a first baseman for Minnesota.”The Twins figure to field a youthful lineup next season, and a veteran presence could help stabilize the clubhouse.
“In addition to his strong ability to hit left-handers, Goldschmidt would bring a much-needed veteran presence to the Twins’ clubhouse. The Twins will be a young team next year, so Goldschmidt’s experience could be a major help to the young players.”
A return to the Yankees appears unlikely, according to projections from Chris Kirschner of The Athletic.
“The Yankees already have two first basemen on the roster: Ben Rice and Luis García Jr., both of whom are left-handed hitters,” Kirschner wrote. “Rice can hit both righties and lefties, while García hasn’t proven he can do that.”
“In 2027, on days when the Yankees face a lefty, they could play Rice at first base, with either Heliot Ramos or Aaron Judge at designated hitter,” the prediction continued.
Goldschmidt has indicated he wants to continue playing.
“Goldschmidt, 39, said after the season ended that he would like to keep playing, but it would be a tough fit to keep him on the roster,” Kirschner wrote.
The former National League MVP has signed one-year deals in each of the past two offseasons and is expected to seek a similar arrangement for 2027.
Throughout his career, Goldschmidt has established himself as a consistent performer, earning seven All-Star selections and multiple Gold Glove awards.
His experience could appeal to contending teams looking for a right-handed bat to complement younger talent.
Whether Minnesota or another club comes calling remains to be seen as free agency approaches.
Goldschmidt’s time in pinstripes may be ending, but his desire to compete keeps his future open.

item.title: [yanksgoyard.com] Yankees must learn from Pirates-Astros trade and deal from their young pitching surplus
item.dc:creator: Stephen Parello
item.description: When one looks at the New York Yankees' roster, the thing that stands out most might be the club's incredible starting pitching depth. Yankees starters led the majors in ERA with a 3.30 mark. Their 3.57 FIP also ranked first, while their 9.43 K/9 checked in at third, and their 2.80 BB/9 came in fifth. The unit was dominant, and it's even more impressive when you consider that Gerrit Cole wasn't ready to return from Tommy John surgery to begin the season, Max Fried and Carlos Rodón had long chunk
item.content:encoded:
When one looks at the New York Yankees' roster, the thing that stands out most might be the club's incredible starting pitching depth. Yankees starters led the majors in ERA with a 3.30 mark. Their 3.57 FIP also ranked first, while their 9.43 K/9 checked in at third, and their 2.80 BB/9 came in fifth.
The unit was dominant, and it's even more impressive when you consider that Gerrit Cole wasn't ready to return from Tommy John surgery to begin the season, Max Fried and Carlos Rodón had long chunks of their seasons erased by multiple IL stints, and Ryan Weathers missed the final five weeks of the regular season. The high-end talent was there, but so was the depth, and that will continue into 2027.
| New York Yankees starting pitching depth chart |
|---|
| 1. Cam Schlittler |
| 2. Max Fried |
| 3. Gerrit Cole |
| 4. Carlos Rodón |
| 5. Will Warren |
| 6. Ryan Weathers |
| 7. Elmer Rodriguez |
New York has six starters who would be locks for any rotation in the league. Elmer Rodriguez got his feet wet this year, and while it was a mixed bag for the former top prospect, he'd likely earn a fifth starter job on a good number of clubs thanks to his pedigree and the fact that he didn't embarrass himself when called upon. While they can't be counted on for much given their injury histories, Clarke Schmidt and Luis Gil are still kicking around, for now.
It's an embarrassment of riches, which stands in stark contrast to other areas of the Yankees' roster that need significant overhauls if the franchise is to turn the tide and snap its nearly two-decade-long streak of playoff futility.
At minimum, New York needs a new second baseman and/or third baseman, a catcher, and at least two bullpen arms. A center fielder might be on the docket as well, depending on how you feel about Spencer Jones' ability to hold up defensively. More position player depth is required, and perhaps some additional help in the outfield could be a need, as it's likely that Aaron Judge gets more reps at DH moving forward.
Those are a lot of holes to fill, and in some cases, such as third base, the free-agent market is slim pickings. That brings us to the logical conclusion of trading a starting pitcher for help elsewhere.
The Yankees trading a young, controllable starter isn't the double-edged sword that it seems to be
One can look at everything laid out above and think it's time to pump the brakes on this idea. The Yankees needed to dip down to their seventh starter in Rodriguez six times in 2026, and that number might grow with Fried, Cole, and Rodón all a year older.
That's true, to an extent, but it's also an incomplete picture of the team's needs relative to the market. Last winter, we saw the market for controllable starting pitchers reach unfathomable heights. The Yankees gave up four prospects for Weathers, who up to that point had never thrown more than 94 2/3 innings in a single season.
We also saw an extraordinary deal where five prospects, all in the top 30, moved from the Texas Rangers to the Washington Nationals in exchange for MacKenzie Gore. At that point in time, Gore had just one season with an ERA below 4.00: 2024's 3.90 ERA performance. Then there was the treasure trove of assets the Baltimore Orioles gave up for Shane Baz and the Taylor Ward-for-Grayson Rodriguez swap.
But the one that stands out, and what the Yankees should try to emulate, was the three-team deal that sent Mike Burrows to the Houston Astros and landed Brandon Lowe, Mason Montgomery, and Jake Mangum with the Pittsburgh Pirates.
At the time of that deal, Burrows had thrown just 99 1/3 career innings, and while it was a three-team trade, one can think of this as Houston sending the prospects necessary to acquire Lowe, Montgomery, and Mangum from the Rays, then shipping the trio to the Pirates for Burrows.
Lowe hit 35 homers this season and continued his long resume of stellar play. Montgomery ascended to the closer role and dominated with a 25-inning scoreless streak to end the year. Mangum is a speedy and solid fourth outfielder. Lowe was a one-year rental, but Montgomery and Mangum are under team control through 2030,
Swapping one of Warren, Weathers, or Rodriguez for a similar package that fills three needs would be a huge boost to the team overall, even if it costs valuable starter depth. The market for cost-controlled starters is likely to be just as insane, since what we saw last year was likely a byproduct of the looming lockout.
Starting pitching on the free-agent market is one of the most expensive commodities, so it makes sense that teams would pay big, asset-wise, for less established starters on inexpensive deals.
If the Yankees were able to pull off a trade in which they acquired a position player solution, a reliever, and a bench piece for one of their young arms, they'd still need to replace that depth. They could do so one of two ways.
First, they could re-sign Ryan Yarbrough. The veteran southpaw was only called upon to make two brief starts this season, but in 2025 he proved that he can still be a reliable swingman, making eight starts overall. He'd be cheap and would still be a viable No. 7 starter.
Or, they could go nuclear and sign a top-of-market free-agent starter. Tarik Skubal would be the ultimate prize, but a reunion with Michael King would be almost as intriguing. That might seem like overkill, but if the Yankees want to end the postseason embarrassment, going nuclear might be what it takes.
Trading from their starting pitching depth and taking advantage of an extreme sellers' market is the best way to fill the majority of the roster's holes, making it too obvious a solution for the Yankees to pass up. At the end of the day, this is about asset management and the fact that the No. 6 or No. 7 starter can fetch pieces that will provide much more value than that hurler alone.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees had another very strong regular season where they went 93-68 in 161 games.
That said, they also had another letdown in the MLB playoffs when they got swept by the Tampa Bay Rays in the ALDS.
In addition, the Yankees also lost the final game on their home field in the Bronx.
Yankees Star Makes Boone Statement
With their season over, a lot of blame has been placed on manager Aaron Boone.
They have only been able to reach the World Series one time over his nine-year stint as manager.
In a recent interview with Michael Kay (via The Michael Kay Show), José Caballero was asked about Boone.
Kay: “Did you like playing for Aaron Boone?”
Caballero: “Hey, I like playing for him. I like playing for the Yankees. I think we are, like I say, a complete team that we could do way better than what we did. And like I said, I think there’s no one else to blame than us as players. We were in there, we the ones making plays and hitting the ball.”
Looking At Boone
Manager Aaron Boone #17 of the New York Yankees walks out to the mound during the fifth inning against the Tampa Bay Rays in game two of the American League Division Series at Tropicana Field on October 05, 2026 in St Petersburg, Florida.
Boone took over the Yankees in 2018.
They have made the MLB playoffs in eight out of his nine seasons (and reached Game 5 of the 2024 World Series).
The Yankees wrote (via X) on February 20, 2025: “The New York Yankees today announced that they have signed Manager Aaron Boone to a two-year contract extension through the 2027 season.”
Looking At Caballero
Jose Caballero #72 of the New York Yankees reacts following his eighth inning three-run home run against the Boston Red Sox at Yankee Stadium on August 30, 2026 in New York City.
Caballero has been in the MLB for four seasons.
He spent the first year of his career with the Seattle Mariners.
Following Seattle, Caballero played part of two seasons for the Rays.
MLB.com wrote (on July 31, 2025): “Tampa Bay Rays traded SS José Caballero to New York Yankees for CF Everson Pereira and Future Considerations. Player To Be Named Later or Cash Considerations.”
